screening_results.reason: This is a non-empirical status/article (narrative review) without original data or participant samples. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (non-empirical paper without original data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET modality applied in an empirical study), I4 (no clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient sample reported), I5 (no sample sizes reported meeting ≥6 participants), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (no coordinates/tables/figures of whole-brain results). The article is an overview of FTD, mentioning imaging modalities descriptively but presenting no empirical imaging analyses or coordinate-based results. Full text appears complete as a narrative article.

The full text reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses with whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts (P<0.001 uncorrected) and frequency/W-score maps; it includes a well-characterized comparison group of behavioural variant FTD patients (n=59, autopsy-confirmed/amyloid-negative). Results include voxel-wise coordinates reported in Supplementary Table 1 and figures. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=59; controls n=61). Therefore the study satisfies imaging modality (VBM), inclusion of clinically/neuropathologically diagnosed bvFTD participants, adequate sample size, whole-brain voxelwise results, and coordinate reporting in text/tables/figures.

This article is a non-empirical narrative review of neuroimaging in Alzheimer’s disease, not an original empirical study of bvFTD patients. It contains no methods, subject recruitment, or between-group voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach space for clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD. Therefore it fails the review’s key inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criteria for non-empirical papers.

This article is a narrative review (“Mise au point”) summarizing imaging modalities in dementia rather than reporting original empirical data. It does not present an original sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, nor specific VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET group analyses with between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard (MNI/Talairach) space. Therefore it fails the required inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criterion E5 (non-empirical review). Exclusion IDs met: E5. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8.

This article is a narrative review (Neurologic Clinics, review article) and does not present original empirical data. Exclusion criteria met: E2 (review/systematic review/meta-analysis) and E5 (non-empirical paper without original data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (the paper itself does not report an original VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET study), I4 (no primary sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients reported), I5 (no participant sample sizes from an original study meeting ≥6), I6 (no between-group contrast coordinates in MNI/Talairach from an original study), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from the target sample), I8 (no qualifying whole-brain results in tables/figures/supplement). Full text appears complete (narrative review with methods/discussion present): fulltext_incomplete=false. Detailed reason: Because this is a review article summarizing neuroimaging literature rather than reporting an original VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET study of bvFTD with whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables, it fails all required inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criteria E2 and E5.

The study reports empirical FDG-PET data and directly compares FDG to early-phase florbetapir in a cohort including clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD patients (n=8). It performs voxel-wise, whole-brain group analyses (SPM two-sample t-tests) after spatial normalization to stereotactic space and presents voxelwise BPM and SPM results (figures and descriptions). Sample sizes meet the threshold (bvFTD n=8; CN n=10; AD n=10). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (imaging modality FDG-PET; bvFTD sample; sufficient sample size; between-group contrasts in MNI space; whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical RS-fMRI and VBM study that explicitly includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=15) and healthy controls (n=15). Imaging modalities meet I3 (resting-state fMRI and VBM). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (I5). Data were spatially normalized to Talairach space and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ICA-derived RS networks, one-sample and between-group t maps, cluster-level inference) are reported, satisfying I6 and I7. Whole-brain results are described in the text and figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-based-only, and patients with major psychiatric comorbidity were excluded. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This article is a clinical/protocol overview and narrative experience report of integrated FDG PET-MRI for dementia, not an empirical case-control/group neuroimaging study. It does not present voxel-based, whole-brain, coordinate-based (MNI/Talairach) between-group contrasts, nor report group-level VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET statistical maps or coordinate tables. Although bvFTD is discussed and illustrative cases are shown, there is no clearly reported sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with N≥6 analyzed in a whole-brain voxelwise framework. Therefore it does not meet the review’s inclusion criteria requiring empirical whole-brain group analyses. Full text appears complete.

This study applied voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on patient MRI data (Methods: DARTEL, normalization to MNI space) and reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain results associating grey matter volume with behavioural measures and patient-vs-control atrophy contrasts. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) and healthy controls (n=20), meeting the minimum sample size requirement. The paper reports results in MNI space and presents whole-brain and small-volume corrected voxelwise statistics (FWE-corrected and uncorrected maps, figures and tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not an excluded modality, no evidence of disqualifying comorbidity reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This paper reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain, voxel-wise analyses (W-score maps and frequency maps) comparing bvFTD patients to controls, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=117 autopsied patients), and reports group-level whole-brain results presented in figures and supplementary material. The sample size exceeds the minimum (≥6). Results are reported as voxel-wise maps in standard space (W-scores derived versus controls) suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections and appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it performed voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (10 bvFTD cases; I4), and had adequate sample sizes (22 patients, 23 controls; bvFTD subgroup n=10 meets I5). The paper reports between-group/parameter correlations in MNI space with specific coordinates (e.g., −8 10 44; I6) and presents whole-brain, voxelwise VBM results (voxelwise GLM, permutation testing, cluster inference; I7). Results and coordinates are reported in the text and figures (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analysis, non-empirical design, or prohibited imaging modality) apply. Therefore the study should be included for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis.

The study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analysis (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=24) (I4) with an adequate sample size (n>=6) (I5). Images were normalized using SPM/DARTEL (MNI space implied) and voxelwise statistical parametric maps were generated and assessed, with whole-brain corrected voxelwise results reported for the bvFTD group (e.g., associations of naming with decreased grey matter at p<0.05 FWE) — satisfying reporting in a defined stochastic space and between-group/within-group voxelwise contrasts (I6, I7). The paper indicates that whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures/supplementary material (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (systematic review, ROI-only, non-empirical, unsuitable modality, or comorbid sample exclusions) apply.

This study includes 20 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 20 healthy controls, uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on structural MRI, and reports voxelwise, whole-brain statistical parametric maps with FWE-corrected results and coordinate-based local maxima (tables/figures). Sample sizes exceed the minimum, and the neuroimaging results are reported in standard stereotactic space using SPM/VBM methods. The full text contains complete Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This article is a narrative review of progressive nonfluent aphasia (PNFA) and the pathological classification of frontotemporal lobar degeneration. It does not present original empirical imaging data, does not report VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET group-level whole-brain results in standard stereotactic space, and does not include a clinical sample of diagnosed bvFTD patients with between-group contrasts. Therefore it fails to meet the inclusion criteria for imaging modality (I3), bvFTD sample (I4), sample size reporting for patient/control groups (I5), and whole-brain coordinate-based results (I6,I7). The correct exclusion is that it is a non-empirical review (E5).

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=64 in the main cohort, plus validation cases) meeting sample-size requirements. Although the primary analyses use automated volumetric MRI, the paper explicitly uses voxel-based morphometry (modulated gray matter volumes) and reports cluster-level, whole-brain voxelwise comparisons (p<0.05, FDR) of bvFTD clusters versus SCD and AD; these results are presented as voxelwise group contrasts (figures and accompanying description), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain VBM results. Thus the imaging modality criterion (VBM) is met, group-level voxelwise contrasts are reported in a defined stochastic space (presented in figures/tables), and bvFTD sample size exceeds six. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only analyses) apply.

This empirical study includes resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM), enrolls clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=21) and matched controls, and performs whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons in MNI space (seed MNI coordinates provided and voxelwise contrasts reported in figures and text). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Whole-brain group-level results are clearly reported for the target bvFTD group. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and includes VBM in addition to seed-based FC). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study does report clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (16/21) and has sufficient sample size (n=21). However, it does not use any of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET); instead it reports structural MRI, CT, and SPECT perfusion. The paper does not present any whole‑brain, voxelwise, coordinate‑based results in MNI or Talairach space (no reported between‑group contrasts or coordinate tables/figures). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and cannot be included in the meta-analysis despite meeting I4 and I5.

The study uses surface-based cortical thickness analyses of structural MRI (vertex-by-vertex cortical thickness and ROI thickness measures), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. The review's exclusion criterion E6 disallows studies that report only cortical thickness methods. Although the sample consists of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with adequate sample size (I5) and reports group-level whole-brain vertex-wise results, it does not meet the required imaging modalities (I3/I6) specified for inclusion. Full text appears complete.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=55) and used FDG-PET in a subset, it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses or between-group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach) with coordinates. Imaging was rated qualitatively by experts rather than analyzed voxelwise; no tables/figures of voxelwise coordinates or whole-brain statistical maps are provided. Therefore it fails the required inclusion criteria for reporting between-group, whole-brain results (I6, I7) despite meeting I3, I4, and I5. Excluded on that basis.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging and analysis inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Although it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=75) (I4) and meets the sample-size requirement (I5), the imaging approach was a visual MRI assessment rather than Voxel-Based Morphometry, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). The paper does not report voxelwise, whole-brain coordinate-based results in MNI or Talairach space (fails I6 and I7), nor does it provide whole-brain group-level voxelwise contrasts. Therefore it cannot contribute coordinate-based whole-brain data required for the review.

This longitudinal cohort study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses (aligned to MNI space) and reported voxelwise group-level contrasts comparing bvFTD patients and controls and subgroups. The sample comprises 58 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (and controls), satisfying the minimum sample-size requirement. Whole-brain voxelwise results are described (figures/tables and supplement) and analyses report MNI-aligned results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment against criteria. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, non-empirical, or unsupported imaging modalities) apply.

The study includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=21) and uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality. Whole-brain, voxelwise VBM analyses (two-sample t-tests) comparing bvFTD to controls are reported (processed with SPM12/DARTEL and referenced as voxelwise results, with figures and supplementary tables), and lesion masks/analyses were normalized to MNI space. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD=21, controls=20). Results are reported at the group level and appear in standard stereotactic space (MNI), with whole-brain voxelwise findings. Full text is complete. Therefore the study meets all specified inclusion criteria for the review.

This article meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (Neary criteria) as target samples (I4), has a healthy control group of N=53 (>=6) satisfying sample-size requirement (I5), reports between-group VBM contrasts using SPM5 with voxelwise results and correction statistics (implying standard stereotactic space coordinates reported in Table 2) (I6), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results for the target bvFTD groups (I7/I8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures referenced) is present and sufficient for screening. No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study does not meet the required imaging-modality and whole-brain reporting criteria. Although it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and has >=6 patients (n=12) satisfying I5, the imaging used is clinical MRI visual ratings rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The paper does not report voxelwise, whole-brain group-level results in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) space nor provide coordinate tables or voxelwise analyses (I6, I7, I8 not met). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears to include core sections (intro, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (neuroimaging n=18, postmortem n=12) meeting sample-size requirements, it does not use any of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). The neuroimaging analysis is manual region-of-interest hypothalamic volumetry (ROI) rather than voxelwise whole-brain VBM or coordinate-based results. The paper does not report between-group voxelwise results in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or provide whole-brain group-level voxelwise coordinates. Therefore it fails I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

The study uses surface-based cortical thickness measures (FreeSurfer processing and Laplace-Beltrami operator) and machine-learning classification rather than VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET. Exclusion criterion E6 (studies that only report cortical thickness methods) is therefore met. Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=48) and has adequate sample sizes, the imaging modality does not match the required modalities (I3) and the paper does not present conventional voxelwise MNI/Talairach coordinate results typical of VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET studies. Full text appears complete. Thus the study must be excluded.

The study does include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=39) but does not use Voxel-Based Morphometry, fMRI, or FDG-PET. Imaging was based on visual rating scales of T1 MRI atrophy rather than voxelwise whole-brain analyses, and no MNI/Talairach coordinate-based between-group voxelwise results are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is a neuropsychological study of episodic memory in bvFTD and AD using the Free and Cued Selective Reminding Test and amyloid PET for group selection. It does not use VBM, FDG‑PET, or task/resting‑state fMRI as required (I3), and it does not report any whole‑brain, voxelwise between‑group contrasts or stereotactic coordinates (I6/I7). Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and has adequate sample size (I5), the key imaging/modality and coordinate-based whole‑brain result inclusion criteria are not met. Full text appears complete.

This article is a narrative/pictorial review of imaging findings in common dementias and does not present original empirical data from a patient sample. It does not report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space, nor does it report between-group contrasts from a studied bvFTD sample. The paper summarizes findings from multiple studies and provides illustrative images, so it does not meet the review’s requirement for original empirical whole-brain results in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients. Full text appears complete but is non-empirical; thus excluded under non-empirical paper criteria.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3) on clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (I4). Sample sizes meet the threshold (AbvFTD n=18, DbvFTD n=16, controls n=30), satisfying I5. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (bvFTD groups vs. controls and between-group contrasts) with FDR correction and references Supplementary Table 1 and figures for results, meeting I7 and I8. VBM preprocessing included stereotaxic normalization (DARTEL), and whole-brain voxelwise results are presented (Supplementary Table/Figures), satisfying I6 (between-group voxelwise results in standard space). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not a review/meta-analysis (E2), it reports whole-brain VBM results not only ROI analyses (E3), there is no indication of concurrent psychiatric/other-dementia/substance-abuse comorbidity in the sample (E4), it is empirical with original data (not E5), and it does not use only FC, DTI, or cortical thickness methods (E6). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review: it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=25) and healthy controls (n=20); uses voxel-based morphometry (MRI) and 18F-FDG PET imaging (voxel-wise SPM analyses); reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise between-group contrasts with coordinates transformed to Talairach space and provided in tables/figures; and sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and exclusion criteria (e.g., concurrent psychiatric diagnoses) were explicitly applied. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to assess neuroanatomical correlates (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (19 bvFTD cases) (I4), has sufficient sample sizes (37 patients, 21 controls) (I5), reports voxelwise group-level results with coordinates in standard space (MNI) (I6), and presents whole-brain voxelwise VBM findings (statistical parametric maps and coordinate tables) clearly identified for the target patient groups (I7). Results and coordinates are reported in tables/figures/supplementary descriptions consistent with acceptable reporting (I8). Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (14 patients) using graph-theory Network Centrality on AAL-atlas ROIs. It satisfies imaging modality (I3), includes bvFTD patients (I4), and meets the sample-size threshold (I5). However, the paper reports ROI-/network-based connectivity and averaged centrality measures rather than voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts reported in stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). No voxelwise coordinate table or voxelwise group-level statistical map in MNI/Talairach space is provided in the main text; results are presented as network/ROI differences. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and falls under exclusion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This article is a narrative review of PET imaging applications across multiple CNS disorders and does not present original empirical data on behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). It does not report a sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, nor does it provide voxelwise, whole-brain group-level results or coordinate tables (MNI/Talairach) from VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET analyses. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria (no target sample, no empirical whole-brain imaging results). The paper is non-empirical review material and thus excluded under E5.

The study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses on clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (probable/possible/pre-bvFTD) with adequate sample sizes (194 total; VBM subset: 44 probable, 19 possible, 14 pre-bvFTD, 36 HC). It provides whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons with familywise error correction and reports cluster coordinates (e.g., −62, −2, 16), consistent with a defined stereotactic space. The paper contains full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an empirical neuropsychological study of visuospatial function in AD and bvFTD without any reported VBM, task/resting‑state fMRI, or FDG‑PET whole‑brain analyses. Although PiB‑PET was performed in a small subset for amyloid status and FDG‑PET or structural MRI were used diagnostically for some patients, the paper does not present group‑level voxelwise results or between‑group contrasts in standard coordinate space (MNI/Talairach). Therefore it fails to meet the imaging modality requirement (I3) and the whole‑brain/coordinate reporting requirements (I6/I7). Per review criteria, studies with no whole‑brain voxelwise results should be excluded. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: none. Exclusion criterion applied: E3 (no whole‑brain voxelwise results reported).

The study meets the review objective and multiple inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) and reports voxelwise TBSS DTI analyses (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (12 bvFTD; I4), has sufficient sample sizes (>6 in patient and control groups; I5), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results using Randomize/TBSS with results referenced in supplement tables (fulfilling I6, I7 and I8). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary tables are referenced for detailed results/coordinates. No exclusion criteria (systematic review, ROI-only, non-empirical, or DTI-only) apply. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=10) and adequate sample sizes (bvFTD N=10, HC N=18), so I4 and I5 are met. However, it does not use any of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET); instead it reports structural MRI FreeSurfer ROI volumetry and ROI-based analyses. The paper does not report whole-brain, voxelwise results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables, and there are no VBM or voxelwise group contrasts. Therefore it fails I3, I6, and I7. This qualifies as an exclusion under E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete for screening purposes (methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses VBM as an imaging modality (I3) and reports voxel-wise VBM results (whole-brain analysis) using standard tools (FSL Randomise) and MNI-based atlases, with cluster-level findings reported, satisfying reporting in defined stereotactic space (I6, I7). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bv-FTD patients (n=9) confirmed by clinical criteria and supported by MRI/FDG-PET (I4), and the bv-FTD subgroup size (9) meets the minimum sample requirement (I5). Whole-brain voxel-wise results are explicitly described and confirmed in the text and figures/supplement (I8). No exclusion criteria (systematic review/meta-analysis only, ROI-only, non-empirical, or disallowed imaging-only methods) are met. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study is an empirical, multi-center structural MRI investigation using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare 52 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to 52 healthy controls. It reports voxelwise, whole-brain (voxel-level and cluster-level FWE-corrected) group comparisons with coordinates referenced in MNI space and presents group-level whole-brain results in figures and text. Sample sizes exceed the minimum. There is no indication of exclusion criteria being violated (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and not limited to disallowed modalities). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This empirical study reports voxel-wise gray matter density (T1 MRI) analyses comparing 32 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to 17 healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-wise methods (Randomise with family-wise error correction). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain contrast results and regression of f0 range with GM atrophy, with peak voxels summarized in table e-1 (supplementary), satisfying reporting of results in a defined stereotactic space. There is no evidence of excluded sample comorbidities or disqualifying methods. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary peak coordinates are referenced. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for VBM-style whole-brain analysis in bvFTD.

This study reports voxelwise analyses of grey matter density derived from structural T1 MRI using ANTs and FSL randomise, with results reported in standard space (MNI converted to Talairach) and clusters surviving correction. The sample includes 63 clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients (MRI available in 55) and 55 demographically-matched healthy controls, meeting minimum sample size. The paper provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) with coordinates and cluster results. No exclusion criteria are met. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all imaging and reporting inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=25) and uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to examine grey matter correlates. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (bvFTD vs controls) and voxel coordinates in MNI space for clusters associated with EMG and SCL measures. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=25; controls n=24). The full text contains methods, results, and neuroimaging analyses with whole-brain VBM results (threshold-free cluster enhancement and voxelwise results reported), satisfying requirements for imaging modality, patient inclusion, sample size, and reporting of between-group voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a retrospective clinical study of mild behavioral impairment (MBI) using conventional structural MRI visual rating scales and neuropsychological tests to predict conversion to dementia (mostly bv-FTD). It does not use VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG‑PET (fails I3), does not include a sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients as the target group at baseline (fails I4), and it does not report any voxelwise between‑group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or provide whole‑brain coordinate tables/voxelwise results (fails I6/I7). Therefore it does not meet the imaging- and analysis-related inclusion criteria required by the review. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an original empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=49) and healthy controls (n=30) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts and regression analyses. The methods explicitly use voxel-based morphometry with whole-brain thresholds and report peak voxel coordinates (converted to Talairach), and results are presented in figures/tables relating GM density to self-appraisal measures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. Thus it satisfies imaging modality (VBM), target diagnosis (bvFTD), adequate sample size, whole-brain voxelwise results in a standard stereotactic space, and acceptable reporting formats.

This is an original, empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=45) and healthy controls (n=35). Methods describe whole-brain voxel-based morphometry with normalization to MNI152 space and voxelwise GLM permutation testing; between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) and whole-brain group-level results are reported. Sample sizes exceed the minimum, and results are presented as voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, non-empirical, seed-FC/DTI-only, or disallowed comorbid samples) apply. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

The full text reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) subgroup (behavioural variant FTD, n=21) (I4) with sample size >6 (I5). Analyses were performed in SPM/DARTEL in standard (MNI) space and report voxelwise group-level results and statistical parametric maps; subgroup VBM contrasts versus healthy controls are described (supplementary materials), consistent with reporting coordinates in a defined stereotactic space (I6,I7). Whole-brain voxelwise VBM results are presented (with small-volume and exploratory whole-brain thresholds) and figures/tables/ supplementary materials are used to convey these findings (I8). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not a review, includes whole-brain VBM, empirical data, no disallowed modalities). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this study used VBM (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and had adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=12; controls n=17) meeting the N>=6 requirement (I5), it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., bvFTD vs. controls) in MNI/Talairach space. The imaging analyses are voxelwise correlational analyses of grey-matter volume with flavour/odour identification across an FTLD cohort, with a restricted bvFTD subgroup analysis reported only at a relaxed uncorrected threshold; no standard group-level between-group contrast coordinates or whole-brain group comparison results originating from the bvFTD group are presented. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (at least one between-group contrast in defined stereotactic space) and I7 (reporting at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly from the target sample group) are not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review criteria: it uses whole-brain Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) analyses (methods and voxelwise regression reported), includes a diagnostically defined bvFTD patient sample (20 patients, including genetically confirmed cases and probable bvFTD), and has adequate sample sizes (20 patients, 20 controls). The paper reports group-level voxelwise results and provides MNI coordinates for voxelwise findings (e.g., IFG peak at MNI −41, 26, 3) from whole-brain analyses. A two-sample VBM group comparison (patients vs. controls) is described as a voxelwise, whole-brain analysis. Supplementary materials are referenced for additional tables/coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; imaging modality acceptable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study includes FDG-PET and clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=7 bvFTD), satisfying I3, I4, and I5. However, it does not report any between-group voxelwise analyses in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach), nor does it provide whole-brain, group-level statistical maps or coordinate tables. Results are descriptive (visual FDG-PET patterns) and there are no voxelwise contrasts; therefore it fails I6 and I7. Full text appears complete.

The paper is an empirical resting-state fMRI study using ICA and voxel-wise analyses in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) versus controls and pAD. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results in MNI space (SPM8/DARTEL; FWE-corrected cluster-level results) and describes between-group contrasts. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The study uses VBM and RS-fMRI modalities and provides regional coordinates/results (with supplementary material referenced). No exclusion criteria are violated (not a review; not ROI-only; not seed-only/DTI/cortical thickness only). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

Although the study uses resting-state fMRI (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=50) with adequate sample size (I4, I5), the full text does not report group-level voxelwise between-group contrast coordinates in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Results are reported as network/node-level labels (AAL regions) and graph metrics rather than voxelwise coordinates or tables of stereotactic coordinates. Therefore criteria I6 and I7 (explicit between-group contrast results in MNI/Talairach and at least one whole-brain voxelwise group-level result) are not satisfied. This falls under exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only ROI/network-level results with no whole-brain voxelwise coordinates). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=17) alongside other FTD syndromes and healthy controls. Imaging modality is task fMRI with preprocessing and normalization into MNI space and second-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) SPM analyses reported (cluster- and peak-level results, figures/SPMs). Sample sizes satisfy the minimum (bvFTD group and control group ≥6). The paper provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results and displays SPMs and cluster/region findings in MNI space; figures and text clearly identify results for the bvFTD group. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and does not trigger exclusion criteria.

This study, while including clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (18/21), does not meet the imaging and analysis requirements for the meta-analysis. It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET as the primary imaging modality (I3). The ante-mortem MRI analyses were ROI-based in a very small subset (n=5), below the required minimum of 6 participants in a group (I5). The paper does not report whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in standardized coordinate space (MNI/Talairach) (I6/I7). Thus it effectively reports ROI-only MRI results, falling under exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete.

This is a genetic case-family report of FTDP-17 with imaging of individual family members (MRI, FDG-PET) but it does not meet key inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. The study sample is small (≤5 siblings, only 2–3 affected)—failing I5 (minimum N=6). It does not present any group-level, between-group voxelwise contrasts or whole-brain results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach), failing I6 and I7. Although FDG-PET was used (satisfying I3), the data are reported as single cases/family imaging and not as whole-brain group analyses. Therefore it cannot be included in a voxelwise meta-analysis of bvFTD studies.

The study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. It uses structural MRI with SIENA/SIENAX (not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), includes only a single bvFTD patient (n=1, below the required minimum of 6), and does not report any between-group voxelwise results in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinates or group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts. The full text appears complete but the methods and results do not provide the coordinate-based whole-brain findings required. Therefore it must be excluded.

This empirical study includes 14 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts reported in MNI space. Sample sizes (bvFTD n=14; controls n=28) exceed the minimum of 6. The paper provides whole-brain VBM results (group-level voxelwise analyses) and reports coordinates/figures; core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text. Although the study also includes DTI analyses, it nevertheless meets the required imaging modality (VBM). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for this review.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (including inclusive/exclusive masking and voxelwise thresholds). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (69 total, with MRI available for 55), exceeding the minimum sample size requirement. Results are reported in stereotaxic space (MNI standard brain; maximum voxel coordinates provided). The paper provides whole-brain voxelwise findings clearly described in text, figures and supplemental material. The full text provided includes background, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria were violated.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=43) and sufficient sample size, it does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Instead it uses visual rating scales on structural MRI (region-based ratings) and reports region-specific atrophy results rather than voxelwise, whole-brain coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7. This matches exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only ROI/regional analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, conclusion).

The study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3) on a clinical sample of 25 bvFTD patients and 21 controls meeting diagnostic criteria (I4, I5). Imaging preprocessing was normalized to MNI space and VBM results (voxelwise, whole-brain) are reported, including significant clusters and a coordinates table/figure (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion (complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI/FC-only, and sample not confounded by concurrent psychiatric diagnoses). Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

Although this paper uses FDG-PET (I3) and studies clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with 12 healthy controls (satisfying I5 via the healthy group), it does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The analyses are ROI-based CMRGlc comparisons and visual MRI ratings without voxelwise, whole-brain coordinate results (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This study should be excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality inclusion criterion (I3). The meta-analysis requires studies using VBM, fMRI (resting-task), or FDG-PET. This study used 18F-flortaucipir tau-PET (and amyloid PET) with structural MRI and FreeSurfer analyses, which does not satisfy I3. The paper does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (20 patients) and healthy and AD comparison groups (I4, I5). It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain comparisons (voxel-based SPM analyses), satisfying I7, but it does not fulfill the required imaging modality criterion; therefore it must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical cohort study including 20 clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients and 31 controls. The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (in MNI space) alongside DTI and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results (FWE-corrected coordinates reported for cerebellum and right MTG), satisfying whole-brain reporting in a defined stereotactic space. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although DTI is also used, VBM is present (I3), so the study is not excluded for relying solely on DTI. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, only ROI/DTI, comorbid psychiatric samples) are triggered. Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=11) and adequate sample sizes, it does not meet the imaging-modality inclusion (I3): it uses ASL-MRI perfusion and ROI-based gray matter volumes rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET. The analysis is ROI-based (multi-atlas ROI), not voxelwise whole-brain/voxel-based results in a standard stereotactic space; no MNI/Talairach coordinates or voxelwise group maps are reported (failing I6 and I7). This places the paper squarely within the exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain/voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Although the sample clearly includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and adequate sample size (24 patients and 24 controls; I5), the study does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET (fails I3). Instead it reports cortical thickness and ROI volumetric analyses using Freesurfer (cortical thickness), and correlations with predefined ROIs rather than whole‑brain, voxelwise group results in stereotactic space. The paper does not report between‑group contrasts in MNI/Talairach coordinates or whole‑brain voxelwise results (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E3 (only ROI analyses/no whole‑brain results) and E6 (uses cortical thickness methods rather than allowed imaging modalities). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) alongside DTI, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=12), and provides whole-brain, voxelwise between-group analyses registered to MNI space with results corrected for multiple comparisons. Sample sizes meet the minimum (≥6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain VBM results and voxelwise contrasts (figures/tables and text), satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are violated.

This study meets the review objective and key imaging/participant criteria: it performed whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses and reports stereotactic coordinates (x,y,z = -24,-14,14) for a significant cluster in the left putamen. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=16) and adequate comparison groups (AD n=14, HC n=20). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from the target sample (FTD) are reported and neuroimaging analyses are thresholded (p<0.05 FWE) with cluster size reported. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and neuroimaging details, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review only, ROI-only analysis, disallowed modalities, comorbid psychiatric sample) apply.

Although the study is an empirical bvFTD study with sufficient sample size (14 bvFTD patients and 14 controls) and addresses ToM in clinically diagnosed bvFTD, it does not meet the imaging and whole-brain reporting requirements of the review. The imaging uses visual MRI ratings of prefrontal atrophy (qualitative/region-based scoring), not one of the required modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET; therefore I3 is not satisfied). The article provides no stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinate results or group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and thus fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Per the review’s exclusion rules, this study reports no whole-brain voxelwise results (matches E3). Therefore it must be excluded despite meeting clinical/sample size criteria.

This is a single-case report (N=1) and does not meet the minimum sample size requirement (I5). The patient was clinically diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease and only had features consistent with bvFTD rather than being a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group, so I4 is not satisfied. Although the study used VBM and FDG-PET (I3) and reports whole-brain VBM results, the design is a case report rather than a group-level comparison of a bvFTD sample meeting the review’s sample-size and diagnostic requirements. Therefore it must be excluded.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports group-level voxelwise comparisons across bvFTD subgroups. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=80 after exclusions) and 30 healthy controls, satisfying sample size requirements. VBM analyses and voxelwise patterns (e.g., frontal and parietal atrophy differences across asymmetric and symmetric bvFTD) are described, and supplementary data are indicated, suggesting coordinate-based whole-brain results are available. No exclusion criteria are violated (not a review, not ROI-only, not an excluded modality). Therefore the study meets the review’s imaging, sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

This empirical study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=25), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts and correlations with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for bvFTD vs controls and behaviour–brain associations. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=25; controls n=25). The full text contains Introduction, Methods (including MRI acquisition and VBM preprocessing/analysis), Results (group VBM comparisons and covariate analyses), and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are violated (not a review, not ROI-only, and participant exclusions for comorbid psychiatric/other dementias/substance abuse were applied). Therefore the paper provides whole-brain VBM results from a bvFTD cohort suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and performed whole-brain, voxelwise analyses comparing FTD subgroups (including bvFTD) to healthy controls. It included 64 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (meets sample-size requirement), and healthy controls (n=32). The paper reports group-level voxelwise results (significant clusters, FWE-corrected) and identifies anatomical regions (e.g., frontotemporal, left inferior frontal gyrus) derived from whole-brain contrasts; figures and supplementary material are referenced for spatial results. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, empirical VBM study, excluded comorbid psychiatric/other dementias per methods). Full text appears to contain methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (VBM), I4 (bvFTD sample), I5 (n>=6), I6 (between-group voxelwise results reported), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (results reported in figures/supplement/text). No exclusion criteria applied.

The full text is complete and the study meets several inclusion criteria (VBM imaging, clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample, sufficient sample size, and whole-brain voxelwise results reported with MNI coordinates). However the paper does not report any between-group contrasts (e.g., bvFTD vs healthy controls); instead it reports within-group voxelwise correlations of reward-seeking scores with regional volume. Inclusion criterion I6 requires at least one between-group contrast in a defined stereotactic space, which is not present. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for structural analyses; includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=30); sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=30, AD n=25, controls n=25); reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain results with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., MNI coordinates reported for left frontoinsula and other clusters) and corrected statistics (pFWE and permutation thresholds). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses (masked to the salience network but using voxelwise thresholds and permutation correction) are clearly described in the text and results/tables. The full text provided includes introduction, methods (including MRI and VBM preprocessing), results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (systematic review, ROI-only, non-empirical, wrong imaging modality, or comorbid-psychiatric confounds) apply.

The study is a VBM whole-brain group analysis and reports MNI coordinates, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, and has adequate sample sizes (10 patient carriers, 20 sporadic FTD, 20 controls). However, the patient sample includes individuals with concurrent neurological/psychiatric conditions (one with ALS, two with parkinsonian signs, one with psychotic symptoms, one with Paget’s disease), which violates the review exclusion criterion E4 that excludes samples with other neurological or psychiatric comorbidities. Therefore the study must be excluded despite meeting the imaging/reporting criteria.

The full text reports voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) whole-brain analyses linking DEXA-derived body-composition measures to grey-matter atrophy in a clearly defined bvFTD sample. The study includes 28 bvFTD patients (meets sample size requirement), reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level results (voxelwise P<0.005, cluster extent threshold provided) with anatomical labeling in stereotactic space (MNI), and presents figures/tables of these results. The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections, sufficient for screening.

This empirical study includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses and reports whole-brain, voxelwise results (pFWE<0.05) using MNI152 standard space, including peak coordinates in Supplementary Table 3. The sample comprises clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=35 overall; VBM subgroup n=12) and healthy controls (overall n=29; VBM subgroup n=20), meeting the minimum sample size requirement. The paper presents group-level whole-brain contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) and within-bvFTD correlations with FCSRT scores, clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a single-family case series/report. Although the study used FDG-PET (satisfying I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases (satisfying I4), it does not meet key inclusion criteria: sample size is well below the required minimum of 6 participants in a patient or healthy group (I5 not met), and no between-group voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables are reported (I6 and I7 not met). The imaging findings are presented as individual case images and descriptive observations rather than whole-brain, group-level statistical maps or coordinate tables. Therefore it must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Although this full text reports voxelwise VBM and whole-brain resting-state fMRI results with MNI coordinates and adequate sample sizes, the participant group consists of presymptomatic C9ORF72 expansion carriers (preSxC9), not clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients. The meta-analysis requires studies including clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4). Therefore the study does not meet the key inclusion criterion I4 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET imaging (I3), includes clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (N=82) (I4) with matched healthy controls and subgroup sizes ≥6 (I5). The methods describe whole-brain, voxel-wise SPM analyses producing group-level t-maps and between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs HC and variant comparisons), reported with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level corrections, indicating results in standard stereotactic space (SPM/MNI) (I6, I7). Whole-brain voxelwise resting-state metabolic connectivity (IRCA) and SICE results are reported and discussed; coordinate/table/figure reporting is implied/standard for SPM results (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not limited to disallowed modalities, and comorbid AD was assessed/excluded). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (11 patients) with 11 matched controls, meeting sample size criterion (>6). The methods describe whole-brain, voxel-wise two-sample t-tests and voxel-wise regression of grey matter on YBOCS scores using SPM5 (a stereotactic voxelwise framework), and results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise findings (figures and cluster descriptions). The paper therefore uses an eligible imaging modality (VBM), includes a bvFTD sample, reports between-group voxelwise analyses and whole-brain group-level results, and provides results in the context of SPM voxelwise (stereotactic) space. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only, non-empirical) apply.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on structural MRI to perform whole-brain, voxelwise atrophy analyses comparing bvFTD subgroups (n=90 with MRI) to age-matched controls (n=44). Patients meet consensus clinical bvFTD diagnostic criteria. The sample sizes exceed the minimum (patients and controls). The paper reports voxelwise between-group contrasts (VBM T-maps, FWE-corrected whole-brain results) and presents VBM-derived atrophy maps (figures) and supplementary materials, satisfying reporting of whole-brain results in a standard space. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., reviews only, ROI-only analyses, seed-based FC/DTI-only methods) apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for imaging modality, sample, sample size, and whole-brain voxelwise reporting.

This is a single-case report (one symptomatic bvFTD proband) with neuropathologic comparisons to two other individuals; it does not meet the minimum sample size requirement (I5: at least 6 participants in patient or healthy group). Although the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and reports whole-brain VBM results (I7), it lacks a group-level patient sample and therefore cannot provide the group-level contrasts with adequate sample size required by the review. It is also unclear that VBM results are reported with stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not satisfied). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although the study uses resting-state fMRI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=38) (I4), and has adequate sample sizes (I5), it reports ROI-based graph/network analyses and network-based statistics (NBS) on a 220-node parcellation rather than whole-brain voxelwise contrasts with stereotactic coordinates. The manuscript does not present group-level, voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach space or coordinate tables required by I6/I7. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/network analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical VBM investigation of behavioural variant FTD including genetically defined subgroups and a sporadic bvFTD comparison. It uses voxel-based morphometry (I3) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD groups to controls and between disease groups (I7,I8). The sample size exceeds the minimum (multiple patient groups >6 and controls n=40) (I5), and participants were clinically diagnosed with behavioural variant FTD (I4). The methods use SPM5 normalization and report voxelwise results (VBM) that would be in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) and are presented in figures/tables, satisfying the requirement for reporting between-group contrasts in a defined space (I6). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext is complete.

This study meets the review objectives and inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to analyze grey matter (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (22 patients; I4, I5), and reports group-level voxelwise analyses aligned to MNI standard space (FNIRT to MNI152) with voxelwise results and cluster reports (I6). The paper provides group-level, voxelwise findings relating atrophy to behaviour (reported within a fronto‑subcortical mask but derived from voxelwise VBM analyses) and presents coordinates/clusters in figures/tables and supplementary materials, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting expectations (I7, I8). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only without whole-brain results, non-empirical methods) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a single-case report (n=1) with FDG-PET and MRI imaging of one patient diagnosed with bvFTD due to C9orf72 expansion. Although imaging modality criterion (I3) and presence of clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4) are satisfied, the study fails key required inclusion criteria: it does not meet the minimum sample size (I5: <6 participants), does not report any between-group contrasts or results in a standard stereotactic space (I6), and provides no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (I7). Therefore it does not provide the group-level whole-brain coordinate data needed for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is an empirical neuropsychological study of episodic memory in bvFTD and AD that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and adequate sample sizes. However, it does not use any of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) and does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and cannot be included in the imaging-focused meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET imaging (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=26) (I4) with sufficient sample size (I5), and performs voxel-based, whole-brain SPM analyses with images spatially normalized to MNI space and reports voxelwise between-group contrasts and correlations (I6,I7). Results are reported in figures and supplementary tables (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is an empirical FDG-PET voxelwise study (not a review or ROI-only), and the sample selection excluded comorbid psychiatric/other dementia cases. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study meets several inclusion criteria (FDG-PET imaging, clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample, adequate sample size, and reports voxelwise MNI coordinates), but it does not report a between-group contrast (e.g., patients vs. controls). Instead, the paper presents within-group voxelwise regression analyses relating occupational scores to rCMRglc. Inclusion criterion I6 explicitly requires at least one between-group contrast reported in defined stereotactic space; this is not present, so the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

The study does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) and adequate sample size, but it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements. The imaging approach is manual hypothalamic volumetry on structural MRI (ROI-based), not VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not satisfied). The paper reports regional volume comparisons and correlations rather than any between-group voxelwise results in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) and therefore does not provide whole-brain, coordinate-based contrasts (I6 and I7 not satisfied). This constitutes an ROI-only analysis, which falls under exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=36) and meets the sample-size requirement, it does not use any of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). The imaging reported is structural MRI/CT and PET/SPECT analyzed by visual reads rather than voxelwise FDG-PET analyses. The paper does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise results in a standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) or provide coordinate tables. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study reporting whole-brain voxelwise analyses in clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients. The sample includes 18 bvFTD patients (14 entered MRI/VBM) and 36 controls (20 imaged), meeting the minimum group sizes. The paper reports between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs HC) and voxelwise correlation analyses using SPM/VBM with cluster-level FWE correction, providing group-level whole-brain results attributed to the target sample. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and not using only excluded modalities).

This full text reports a voxel-based morphometry (VBM) study using whole-brain, voxelwise analyses in MNI space with cluster-level statistics. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (bvFTD n=14 in the MRI subset; 149 patients in the behavioral cohort), and the imaging subset includes >6 patients and >6 controls. The paper reports group-level voxelwise results and neuroanatomical coordinates/cluster results (figures/tables and supplementary material) linking principal components to grey and white matter changes. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review only, ROI-only analyses, seed-based FC/DTI-only methods, or disqualifying comorbidities) are met. Full text is complete for screening.

This study includes VBM imaging and a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=11) with adequate sample sizes, but it does not report a whole-brain, between-group voxelwise contrast clearly attributable to the bvFTD group in MNI/Talairach space. The reported VBM results are regression associations of grey matter with behavioural measures across the combined patient cohort rather than group-level (bvFTD vs control or similar) whole-brain contrasts for the target group. Therefore the study fails to satisfy inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (reporting of a between-group, whole-brain voxelwise result for the target sample). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Exclusion criteria applicable: none of the listed explicit exclusion criteria; exclusion is due to failure to meet the required inclusion criteria (I6 and I7).

The paper is an empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as its imaging modality, included 19 clinically probable bvFTD patients (and control/disease groups), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results with coordinates provided in MNI stereotaxic space. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analyses, disallowed imaging modalities, or comorbid samples) are violated. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=23) and healthy controls, uses voxel-based morphometry and task-free (resting-state) fMRI as imaging modalities, reports whole-brain VBM voxelwise results with MNI coordinates, and presents group-level analyses relating structural and functional measures to autonomic outcomes. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6 per group). Whole-brain VBM results are reported and coordinates are provided (MNI), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise between-group/target-sample results. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, includes whole-brain analyses not only ROI, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria.

This is a clinical/epidemiological study of epilepsy in neurodegenerative dementias using clinical assessment, EEG/qEEG and routine MRI for diagnosis. Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and the bvFTD group size exceeds 6 (I5), the study does not use VBM, task/resting‑state fMRI, or FDG‑PET as an imaging modality (fails I3). It does not report any whole‑brain, voxelwise between‑group contrasts in stereotactic space or provide coordinate tables/voxelwise results (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it does not meet required imaging and reporting criteria for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Although the paper includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) and adequate group sizes, it does not use VBM, fMRI (resting/task), or FDG-PET imaging and does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Lesion maps are shown, but no voxelwise neuroimaging results or coordinate tables/contrasts are provided. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (no whole-brain results reported).

This is an original empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results and reported peak coordinates. It includes a healthy control group (n=20). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and reports between-group contrasts (disease vs controls and between pathologies) with tables of peak voxel coordinates. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

The study uses VBM and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=22), and reports voxelwise results with MNI coordinates. However, the VBM analyses and reported whole-brain voxelwise results are presented for the combined FTLD cohort (and separately for AD) or as correlations with symptoms, not as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts clearly identified as coming specifically from the bvFTD subgroup (the target sample). Therefore inclusion criterion I7 (at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the target sample group) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19), has sample sizes >6, reports voxelwise whole-brain results with MNI coordinates, and provides group-level whole-brain covariate analyses (FWE/FDR-corrected) clearly attributed to the bvFTD sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (VBM procedures), Results (tables/figures with MNI coordinates), and Discussion, so the full text is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not a review, not ROI-only, not an excluded imaging modality, and no evidence of disqualifying comorbidities).

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The methods state that voxelwise analyses were performed with x–y–z coordinates in Montreal Neurological Institute space, and VBM produced whole-brain, voxelwise atrophy results for the bvFTD group (P<0.05, FDR-corrected). Sample sizes meet the minimum (≥6). Whole-brain voxelwise group-level results are reported (main text and supplemental material referenced). No exclusion criteria are met: this is empirical original data (not a review), it is not limited to only ROI or seed-based FC analyses (VBM whole-brain results present), and there is no indication of comorbid psychiatric disorders or other excluded features. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion); supplemental materials are available. Therefore the study meets all specified inclusion criteria for the review.

The full text reports clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=27) and includes resting-state fMRI (ICA dual-regression) analyses, meeting the imaging modality requirement. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts were performed and results are reported/visualized in MNI standard space (TBSS and dual-regression RS-fMRI results), satisfying coordinate and whole-brain evidence requirements. Sample sizes (bvFTD=27; controls=48) exceed the minimum. Results are presented in figures/tables and supplementary materials. The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses SPECT (rCBF) rather than permitted imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) (fails I3). It also does not report between-group contrasts vs. a healthy/control group in a defined stereotactic space (fails I6), reporting only within-group voxelwise correlations. Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), has sufficient sample size (I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates (I7, I8), failure to meet I3 and I6 means it must be excluded per the review’s criteria.

The study reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to healthy controls, with adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=20, HC n=20). Results are reported in MNI space with voxelwise between-group contrasts and cluster coordinates, and whole-brain conjunction analyses are presented. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review’s imaging modality, sample, sample size, reporting of between-group contrasts in standard space, and whole-brain result requirements.

The study does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET); it reports T1-weighted MRI volumetric (whole thalamus) ROI analyses rather than voxelwise whole-brain results in stereotactic space. Although it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=141) and adequate sample sizes, it provides no between-group voxelwise coordinates (MNI/Talairach) or whole-brain voxelwise results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7.

The study includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (methods and results described), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) and controls (n=20), and reports group-level voxelwise between-group contrasts using SPM/DARTEL with images normalized to MNI space and cluster-based FWE correction. Whole-brain VBM results (gray matter loss in specific regions) are reported and clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets imaging modality (I3), bvFTD sample (I4), sufficient sample size (I5), between-group voxelwise results in stereotactic space (I6), and whole-brain group-level voxelwise reporting (I7/I8). No exclusion criteria are met.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11), uses VBM, and has adequate group sizes, the imaging results reported are region-of-interest volumetric comparisons (hippocampus and posterior cingulate) rather than whole-brain voxelwise group-level contrasts reported in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) with coordinates. The manuscript does not present voxelwise whole-brain results or coordinate tables/figures for between-group contrasts. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I7) and falls under exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

While the paper uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases (I4), and compares scans to a large healthy control dataset (N=112) satisfying the sample-size requirement for a control group (I5), it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result derived from the bvFTD target sample. The study reports single-subject SPM voxelwise maps rather than a group-level voxelwise contrast for the bvFTD subgroup (bvFTD n=2), so it fails inclusion criterion I7. The presented results are single-subject voxelwise maps/figures (acceptable per I8) but do not meet the review requirement of at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result for the target clinical group. Full text appears complete.

This study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD sample per Rascovsky criteria (I4) with 52 patients (I5). Voxel-wise SPM analyses were performed, including single-subject SPM maps and group-level whole-brain two-sample t-tests against a normal FDG-PET database, producing voxelwise (SPM/MNI-based) results and conjunction analyses (I6, I7). Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise maps and described in the text/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, non-empirical, wrong imaging modality, or comorbid psychiatric/other dementia confounds) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

Although this study includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=27) and meets sample-size and reporting requirements (voxel-wise whole-brain TBSS results reported in groupwise/MNI space), the imaging modality used is diffusion tensor imaging (DTI). The review’s inclusion requires VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and the exclusion criteria explicitly disallow studies that only report DTI (E6). Therefore the study must be excluded despite satisfying other inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study uses structural MRI volumetry and surface-based cortical thickness analyses (FreeSurfer), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET required by I3. This falls under exclusion E6 (studies reporting only cortical thickness methods). Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and has >=6 healthy controls (I5), the imaging modality does not meet inclusion criteria for the review. Whole-brain vertex-wise thickness results are reported but are surface-based cortical measures rather than the required modalities and do not clearly provide stereotactic coordinate tables in MNI/Talairach for bvFTD-specific contrasts, so the study cannot be included.

This randomized crossover study includes task and resting fMRI (I3), clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4), and sufficient sample size (28 participants; I5). However, imaging results were reported as non-significant and the manuscript states ‘data not shown’; no between-group (patient vs control) whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported, and no coordinates in MNI or Talairach space are provided. Thus the study does not meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (no between-group stereotactic coordinates and no reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Because no whole-brain coordinate results are available for the target patient group, it cannot be included in a coordinate-based meta-analysis and should be excluded (applies to exclusion criterion E3).

The study reports empirical VBM analyses including bvFTD patients and healthy controls, with whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons and ROI analyses. Sample sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD n=23; controls n=50). Imaging data were normalized to MNI space and SPM-based voxelwise results are reported for between-group contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods (VBM acquisition and analysis), results (whole-brain and insula ROI findings), and discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=9) but does NOT use any of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET); it uses 18F‑THK5351 tau PET (a different PET tracer) and 18F‑florbetaben amyloid PET. Primary analyses are region-of-interest (lobe-based SUVR/WM/GM ratios) rather than whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space.
