The paper does not report voxelwise, whole-brain group-level contrasts or coordinate tables that satisfy the whole‑brain/voxelwise requirement. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) methods on T1-weighted MRI (ICA on modulated gray matter images and voxel-wise VBM analyses), includes clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (n=24), has adequate sample size (bvFTD n=24; AD n=31; controls n=30), reports between-group contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space (voxel-wise permutation testing, TFCE, FWE-corrected; SCN clusters listed with MNI coordinates), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise findings attributable to the bvFTD group. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15), has sufficient group sizes (bvFTD and controls >6), reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts registered to MNI standard space (methods describe MNI registration and results are displayed/overlayed on MNI templates), and provides group-level whole-brain results (VBM/TBSS) clearly attributed to the bvFTD sample. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion (not truncated). There are no applicable exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, non-empirical, seed-FC/DTI-only) that would disqualify the paper. Therefore it should be included for the meta-analysis focusing on bvFTD VBM studies.

This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study using ICA-derived intrinsic connectivity networks, including a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) and matched controls and AD patients. The study uses task-free fMRI (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) with sufficient sample size per group (n=12; I5), reports voxel-wise, whole-brain group contrasts with peak coordinates (MNI) and corrected thresholds (I6, I7), and presents results in figures/tables/text (I8). Full article text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, seed-only/DTI/cortical thickness, non-empirical design) apply.

The study does include clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients and adequate sample sizes, but it does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise neuroimaging results in a standard stereotactic space. Imaging reported consists of MRI visual rating scales and occasional FDG-PET in individuals without group-level voxelwise analyses or reported coordinates. Thus it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (no whole-brain results). The full text appears complete.

Although the study is a full empirical resting-state fMRI investigation including clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, adequate sample sizes, voxelwise whole-brain seed-based analyses normalized to MNI space, and reports group-level between-group contrasts, it reports only seed-based functional connectivity (wSDM and Pearson correlation) results from resting-state fMRI. Per exclusion criterion E6, studies that only report seed-based functional connectivity (FC) without other accepted modalities (e.g., VBM or FDG-PET) are excluded from this review. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence the paper must be excluded despite meeting multiple inclusion elements.

Although the paper includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and adequate sample size for that group, it does NOT use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. The imaging method is structural MRI with visual atrophy rating scales (qualitative scores). The study does not report any voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables/voxelwise statistical maps. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete and provides methods/results/discussion, but lacks the required imaging modality and whole-brain voxelwise results.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) and reported whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts (density analyses) including a group of patients meeting criteria for behavioral variant FTD comorbid with ALS (ALS-FTD; n=7). Healthy controls (n=39) and the patient subgroup sizes meet the minimum sample size criterion. The paper presents whole-brain VBM results and ROI density analyses with figures and supplementary tables referenced, indicating voxelwise between-group contrasts attributable to the target bvFTD group. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not alternative modality). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=42) and healthy controls, with voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses comparing bvFTD versus controls and apathetic versus non-apathetic subgroups. Imaging was normalized to a standard space and results are reported as voxelwise clusters (with tables of cluster locations referenced). Sample sizes exceed the minimum threshold. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=7 per patient subgroup) and provides full methods/results, it uses structural MRI with Freesurfer-derived ROI volumetry (orbitofrontal and middle frontal gyrus volumes) rather than VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET. The paper reports region-of-interest volumetric comparisons (cm^3) and does not present whole-brain voxelwise results or between-group coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and uses resting-state fMRI (satisfying I3, I4, I5), the analyses are ROI/seed-based functional connectivity measures and the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast results with coordinates in standard stereotactic space. The meta-analysis requires at least one whole-brain voxelwise result (I6/I7). Therefore the study is excluded because it reports only ROI/seed-based analyses (E3, E6). Full text appears complete.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) and adequate sample sizes (I5), it does not use an eligible imaging modality (I3). Imaging consists of structural MRI volumetric analyses using FreeSurfer (regional/ROI volumes and cortical volumetry), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. The paper reports ROI-based volumetric results rather than any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results or stereotactic coordinates (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it reports only ROI/volume analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise findings and is excluded under E3 and E6.

The study reports primary empirical data using baseline structural T1 MRI processed into voxel-wise grey-matter maps (CAT12/DARTEL) consistent with VBM-style analysis and whole-brain voxel-wise features (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed probable/definite bvFTD patients (n=18) based on FTDC criteria at 2-year follow-up (I4), and group sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=18; psychiatric n=27; neurological n=28) (I5). Images were normalized to MNI space and the paper presents multivariate, whole-brain voxelwise results (SVM weight maps with p-values) with anatomical localization reported in the main text and supplementary materials (Supplementary Table 5, Fig.2), which satisfies reporting of results in a defined stereotactic space and whole-brain group-level voxelwise evidence (I6, I7, I8). The study is empirical, not a review, and includes whole-brain analyses (no exclusion criteria triggered). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion); supplementary material is referenced. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for this review.

This is a DTI study using ROI analyses (FWM, GWM, SWM) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it does not report whole-brain voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Although it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=8) and sufficient sample sizes, it violates the imaging-modality requirement and reports only ROI-based DTI results, which are excluded by the review criteria.

Although the study used VBM (preprocessing and normalization to MNI space) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample size, it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or coordinate tables in MNI/Talairach space. The authors extracted GM volumes using a priori masks (ROI-based extraction) for classification rather than presenting voxelwise whole-brain results. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise reporting and must be excluded.

Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=18) and adequate sample size, the study uses structural MRI cortical thickness ROI analyses (FreeSurfer) rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise results in a standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) or provide coordinate tables. Therefore it fails key imaging and whole-brain reporting inclusion criteria (I3, I6, I7). This qualifies it for exclusion under E3 (ROI-only analyses without whole-brain results) and E6 (reports cortical thickness methods rather than allowed modalities). Full text appears complete.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bv-FTD patients (n=27) (I4), has sufficient sample size (≥6) (I5), reports voxelwise results in MNI space with peak coordinates (I6), and provides whole-brain, group-level VBM results (cluster surviving FWE correction) clearly identified as coming from the patient groups (I7,I8). The full text contains introduction, methods (including imaging and VBM preprocessing/statistics), results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (study is empirical, not ROI-only, uses acceptable imaging modality, and does not appear to be a review or non-empirical paper).

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and adequate sample size, it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET as the primary imaging modality. The neuroimaging analyses are ROI-based using FreeSurfer cortical volumes and DTI-derived FA/MD and WM volumes (atlas ROIs). The paper does not report whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) space or provide voxelwise coordinate tables/figures; analyses are ROI-based. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and E6 (reports DTI and cortical-volume/thickness methods rather than VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study of C9ORF72-associated FTD/ALS that includes clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD cases, but it does not meet the review's imaging and reporting requirements. Although FDG‑PET was performed, only five subjects had FDG‑PET (below the required N≥6). The MRI analysis used STAND-maps/region-based Z-scores rather than VBM and the paper does not report whole-brain, voxelwise between-group results in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) with coordinate tables for the target bvFTD sample. SPECT results included a voxelwise SPM analysis, but SPECT is not an accepted modality per I3. Therefore key inclusion criteria I3, I5, I6 and I7 are not satisfied.

Although this study uses VBM and FDG-PET and reports voxel-wise, MNI-space group contrasts, it does not specifically address behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) as the target sample. The patient sample is familial FTLD with mixed clinical phenotypes (bvFTD, nfvPPA, PSP, ALS), and the paper presents whole-brain results for f-FTLD subgroups (A+ vs A−) rather than a group clearly and explicitly defined as clinically diagnosed bvFTD. It is unclear how many (if any) bvFTD cases are present and whether there are ≥6 bvFTD patients; no group-level, whole-brain results are reported specifically for a bvFTD sample. Therefore the key inclusion criterion I4 (bvFTD sample) and I7 (whole-brain results clearly from target bvFTD group) are not satisfied, so the study must be excluded.

The article uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (and FDG-PET) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients. Although the main focus is two bvFTD-SP case patients, the paper also generated group-level whole-brain VBM maps comparing 20 bvFTD patients to 164 controls (voxelwise, p<0.001) for comparative purposes. Sample sizes therefore meet the >=6 participant requirement (20 bvFTD; 164 controls). Whole-brain voxelwise results are presented as VBM maps (figures) with MNI-referenced template coordinates described in the text/figure legend, satisfying the requirement for between-group contrasts in a defined stochastic space and acceptable reporting via figures. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This study does not address the review objective of bvFTD. Participants were patients with semantic dementia / svPPA with post-mortem-confirmed TDP-43 type C pathology, not clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (fails I4). The imaging modality is T1-weighted structural MRI with region-of-interest volumetric analyses (w-scores) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). The analyses are ROI-based regional volume results, not whole-brain voxelwise results in standard space (violates I6/I7) — thus it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded.

The full text includes VBM analysis (grey matter voxel-based morphometry) in addition to DTI, reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons projected to MNI space, and explicitly presents group-level whole-brain results (FWE-corrected) for bvFTD versus controls and AD. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=27) and healthy and AD comparison groups (≥6 subjects per group). Results are reported as voxelwise maps and described in text/figures/tables. The manuscript contains complete core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (36 bvFTD + 20 FTD-ALS) and healthy controls (n=23). The study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM), reports group atrophy contrasts and voxelwise correlations with psychosis scores, and provides anatomical coordinates in MNI stereotaxic space (results in main text and supplementary tables). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6 per group). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results from the target bvFTD sample are clearly reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, reviews, disallowed modalities) are violated.

Although this empirical study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) and uses FDG-PET (satisfying I3, I4, I5), it does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample (I7) nor provide between-group voxelwise contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (I6). The voxel-based analyses described are correlational across the pooled sample (with diagnostic group as a covariate) and ROI analyses are reported for frontal regions; coordinate tables or voxelwise between-group contrasts for the bvFTD group are not presented in the provided full text (coordinates are referenced as Supplementary Table S2 but no bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise coordinates/contrasts are shown). Therefore it fails required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This empirical study includes 35 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and uses voxel-based morphometry and resting-state fMRI analyses. Whole-brain VBM results are reported (FWE-corrected clusters with coordinates provided in SI Appendix), and seed-based functional connectivity analyses are also presented. Sample sizes exceed the minimum threshold. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from the target patient group. No exclusion criteria are violated. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=22), uses VBM, and has adequate sample sizes. However, the VBM analysis yielded no significant whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results (no findings surviving whole-brain FWE correction); significant effects were reported only after small-volume (ROI) correction. The review exclusion criterion E3 disallows studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results. Therefore the study does not meet the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results (I7/I6) and must be excluded.

This paper reports task-based fMRI (I3) in a sample of clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients (Neary and revised criteria) (I4) with n=20 patients and n=18 controls (I5). The authors conducted voxel-wise, whole-brain group contrasts (with voxel-wise gray-matter covariate correction) and report peak coordinates in standard space (MNI/Talairach) in tables and figures (I6, I7). Whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and tables (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not an excluded modality, and comorbidities were excluded). Full article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) are present, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This full text clearly meets all required inclusion criteria: the study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality; includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=23); samples sizes exceed the minimum (patient groups and controls >=16); analyses were registered to MNI152 standard space and report voxelwise, group-level contrasts (voxelwise GLM with TFCE, permutation testing) and results are overlaid on the MNI standard brain; whole-brain voxelwise results are presented for patient vs control and inter-patient contrasts and for clinical correlations. The manuscript contains full methods, results and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only results, unsupported modalities, or non-empirical design) appear to apply.

This empirical study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (FSL–VBM) to examine neural correlates in behavior variant FTD (bvFTD) and Alzheimer’s groups. The sample includes 10 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (and 10 AD, 10 controls), satisfying sample-size requirements. VBM analyses report voxelwise, group-level results and brain–behavior correlations with coordinates provided in MNI stereotaxic space. The full text includes introduction, methods (image acquisition and VBM), results (group atrophy maps, voxelwise correlates), and discussion. No exclusion criteria are triggered: it is not a review, not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/DTI/thickness-only methods, and participants with comorbid psychiatric/neurological conditions or substance abuse were excluded per the Methods. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses using FSL (MNI standard space) and provides group-level, voxelwise contrasts (including MNI coordinates and figures/tables) comparing bvFTD patients to controls. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=44) and controls (n=28), satisfying the sample size requirement. Imaging modality (VBM), presence of clinically diagnosed bvFTD, ≥6 participants, reporting of between-group contrasts in MNI space, and whole-brain voxelwise group results are all present. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria are violated.

The paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=13) (I4). Sample sizes meet the threshold (I5). VBM results are reported as voxelwise, whole-brain contrasts with coordinates in stereotaxic space (MNI) (I6, I7), and results are presented in figures/tables described in text (I8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This full text meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (50 bvFTD subjects) within the sample (I4); sample sizes exceed the minimum (I5); reports voxelwise, between-group contrasts with Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) coordinates (I6); provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results clearly identified for FTD and bvFTD (I7); and coordinate results/figures/tables are reported in the text/supplement (I8). The article contains complete core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusions) and does not violate exclusion criteria. Therefore it should be included.

This study does not meet the imaging- and sample-specific inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. Although it is an empirical study with adequate sample sizes (93 mutation carriers, 78 noncarriers) and reports longitudinal structural MRI analyses, the participants are familial FTLD mutation carriers (many presymptomatic or mildly/questionably symptomatic) rather than a cohort of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients. The imaging analyses reported are lobar ROI-based gray matter volumes/atrophy associations (summed atlas regions) rather than voxelwise VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET whole-brain contrasts in standard stereotactic space. The paper does not report between-group whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails I3, I4, I6, and I7. It does meet sample size criterion I5. Full text appears complete.

Although this study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and applies VBM methods alongside DTI, it does not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) that would meet the review’s I6/I7 requirements. The VBM procedure described was applied with an anterior cingulate mask to extract mean gray matter density for the ACC (an ROI-based approach) rather than reporting whole-brain voxelwise coordinates or tables. The paper’s primary analyses focus on tractography (DTI) and on ACC-specific measures; thus it effectively only provides ROI/masked results and lacks the required whole-brain voxelwise contrasts. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses VBM), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD), and I5 (sample sizes ≥6), but fails to meet I6 and I7 and is excluded based on E3 (reports only ROI/masked analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

The study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and FDG‑PET whole-brain voxelwise analyses comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to healthy controls (and bipolar patients). Sample sizes (bvFTD n=23 initial, n=21 in MRI analysis; PET n=23) exceed the minimum. Results are reported in stereotactic space (MNI, converted to Talairach) with cluster coordinates and tables/figures referenced. The full text includes introduction, methods (imaging acquisition and voxelwise SPM analyses), results (group contrasts and coordinates), and discussion, so core content is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI‑only results, prohibited modalities, or disallowed comorbid samples) apply. Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the review and should be included.

This is a clinical case series of eight Chinese individuals with FTD describing clinical, neuropsychological, and some structural MRI and PIB amyloid PET findings. It does not use voxel-based morphometry (VBM), FDG-PET, or task/resting-state fMRI as the imaging modality (fails I3). The paper does not report any between-group voxelwise whole-brain contrasts in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) nor provide coordinate-based results (fails I6 and I7). Although it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (satisfies I4) and the sample size meets the ≥6 participants criterion (satisfies I5), the lack of the required imaging modality and absence of whole-brain voxelwise results make it ineligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study (SPM12) that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=24) and healthy controls. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (t-statistic maps normalized to MNI space) and between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls; bvFTD vs AD) with cluster-level FWE correction, and presents anatomo–functional correlations. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Whole-brain results are explicitly described in the methods and results (MNI space), satisfying the requirement for reported between-group contrasts in a defined stochastic space. No exclusion criteria appear to be violated. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the study includes FDG-PET imaging (I3) and a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient sample (I4) with N=8 (I5), it does not report any between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) nor provide group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables. The imaging findings are described qualitatively (hypometabolism on PET/SPECT) in a case series format without reported voxelwise statistical maps or coordinates, so criteria I6 and I7 are not met. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=66) with age- and gender-matched controls (n=30). The paper uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons of each bvFTD-derived subtype versus controls (family-wise error corrected; additional pairwise contrasts reported). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Whole-brain results are described in the text and shown in figures (and referred to in tables), meeting the requirement for voxelwise between-group results in stereotactic space. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so core content is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review, only ROI analyses, seed-based FC/DTI-only methods) apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it uses voxel-based morphometry and task-free (resting-state) fMRI (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with sample sizes of 14 patients per bvFTD subgroup and 14 controls (I5); reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts using standard spatial normalization (MNI template) and voxelwise statistical maps/thresholding (I6, I7). Whole-brain results are presented in figures and referred to supplementary materials (acceptable per I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is original empirical work (not a review), includes whole-brain voxelwise analyses (not ROI-only), and does not rely solely on modalities excluded by E6. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given the detailed voxelwise group results and imaging modalities, the study should be INCLUDED.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET (and VBM) as imaging modalities (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients confirmed after 12-month follow-up (I4), has adequate sample sizes (30 patients, 42 controls) exceeding the 6-participant threshold (I5), and reports voxel-wise, whole-brain analyses normalized to a stereotactic space (images were normalized to MNI space using SPM8 with voxel-based DTI and VBM results), satisfying the requirement for between-group contrasts in defined stochastic space (I6) and providing group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I7). Results are presented in figures and described in text (acceptable per I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a single-case clinical report describing one patient with probable behavioral-variant FTD and includes an FDG-PET scan. Although it meets I3 (uses FDG-PET) and I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD), it does not meet required sample- or analysis-related inclusion criteria: the study has n=1 (fails I5), presents no between-group contrasts or coordinate-based results in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6), and reports no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from the target sample (fails I7). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on group-level neuroimaging studies.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with DARTEL/SPM preprocessing and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (bvFTD vs controls, BD vs controls, bvFTD vs BD) normalized to MNI space. The sample includes 16 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (meets diagnostic criteria) and group sizes exceed the minimum (16 bvFTD, 13 BD, 22 controls). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported (FWE-corrected, p<0.05) and regions/atrophy patterns are described. No exclusion criteria are violated (not a review; not ROI-only; uses VBM; patient sample appropriate). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical study that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts overlaid on the MNI standard brain (I6, I7, I8). The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD patients (I4) with n=15 in the in vivo cohort (I5), and adequate control and Alzheimer’s groups. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply: it is not a review (E2), it reports whole-brain VBM results rather than ROI-only (not E3), participants do not have excluded comorbidities reported (not E4), it is empirical original data (not E5), and although DTI is included the study also uses VBM rather than only DTI/FC/cortical thickness (not E6). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=20) and used FDG-PET as an imaging modality; it therefore meets I3, I4, and I5. However, the full text presents FDG/PiB-PET only as diagnostic biomarkers and does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise imaging analyses or between-group contrasts with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (coordinate-based between-group contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results) are not satisfied. The paper is an empirical study with complete core sections, but lacks the required voxelwise imaging results needed for inclusion in the meta-analysis, so it must be excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on T1-weighted MRI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient sample (N=15) and healthy controls (I4, I5), reports whole-brain voxelwise group analyses (two-sample t-test and multiple regressions) with results given in MNI coordinates (e.g., peak MNI-coordinates reported) (I6, I7), and whole-brain results are clearly described and shown in figures/tables (I8). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analyses, prohibited modalities, or disallowed comorbid samples) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (final n=21) with age- and education-matched controls. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses using MNI space coordinates and FWE-corrected results (e.g., dmPFC and right amygdala), and parametric within-group regression analyses linking regional hypometabolism to prosocial and other-critical sentiment scores. Imaging modality (FDG-PET), sample (clinically diagnosed bvFTD), sample size (>6 per group), and reporting of between-group and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotactic space meet the inclusion criteria. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only, non-empirical methods, or disallowed modalities) are met.

The full text reports a study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=19) and healthy controls (N=20). Imaging modalities include voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and task-based fMRI. Whole-brain, voxelwise VBM group comparisons (normalized to MNI space) are reported (FWE-corrected results) and whole-brain fMRI analyses and group contrasts are described. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Results are reported in a defined stochastic space (MNI) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise findings are clearly identified. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, disallowed modalities) apply.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET imaging (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with adequate sample size (8 bvFTD patients and 26 controls; I5), reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with peak coordinates (Table III) in stereotactic space (I6), and provides group-level, whole-brain results clearly identified for the target sample (I7). Reporting of results in tables/figures/text satisfies I8. No exclusion criteria are violated (not a review, not ROI-only, not using excluded modalities, and comorbid diagnoses were excluded). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

Although the study includes a bvFTD sample (n=15) and reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses, the neuroimaging methods are cortical thickness / ANTs-based structural MRI analyses rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET required by the inclusion criteria. Exclusion criterion E6 disallows studies that only report cortical thickness methods. In addition, the reported whole-brain voxelwise imaging results and coordinate peaks pertain to svPPA patients, not to the bvFTD group (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are clearly reported for bvFTD), so the study does not provide the target-sample whole-brain contrasts required (I7). Therefore it fails to meet required imaging-modality and whole-brain results criteria for inclusion.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11), uses VBM, and reports voxelwise peak coordinates in MNI space, the VBM analysis was performed within a predefined fronto‑striatal ROI mask rather than as an unrestricted whole‑brain voxelwise analysis. The review's exclusion criterion E3 disqualifies studies that report only ROI‑restricted analyses with no whole‑brain results. Therefore the study does not meet the requirement for at least one group-level whole‑brain (voxelwise) result and must be excluded.

The full text reports voxelwise whole-brain gray matter analyses (GMP images, transformed to MNI space) using ANTs and FSL Randomise, i.e., VBM-style methods; includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=54) and healthy controls; sample sizes exceed 6; reports group-level whole-brain contrasts (patient groups vs controls) and whole-brain regression analyses with results in stereotactic (MNI) space and supplementary materials. The paper contains complete methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI analyses, review article, restricted modalities) apply.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=10), uses voxelwise morphometry-like methods and structural MRI, and has adequate sample sizes, it does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) results clearly identified for the bvFTD group. The voxelwise morphometry was restricted to a merged subcortical mask (not whole-brain), and cortical thickness (whole-brain) results for bvFTD did not reach significance and no whole-brain coordinate-based results for bvFTD are provided in the text. The paper therefore lacks the required whole-brain, voxelwise between-group results in standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) for the target sample. Based on the review criteria, this study must be excluded.

This study reports empirical voxel-wise FDG-PET analyses comparing behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients (n=12) with AD and control groups. It uses FDG-PET as an imaging modality, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, has more than six patients in the bvFTD group, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space with reported coordinates and statistical maps. The manuscript contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections. There are no exclusion criteria triggered (not a review, not ROI-only, not a non-empirical methods paper, and not limited to excluded modalities). Therefore it meets all specified inclusion criteria for the review.

The study employed resting-state fMRI (ICA, fALFF, REHO, seed-based and PLS) satisfying imaging modality requirements. The sample included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=8) alongside controls, meeting the bvFTD and sample-size criteria (>6). Analyses used whole-brain voxelwise SPM random-effects ANOVA with multiple-comparison correction and report peak voxel coordinates (e.g., BA46 peak x=36,y=42,z=30), satisfying the between-group contrast in a defined stereotactic space and whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses relating caregiver-rated empathy measures to gray-matter atrophy in a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup. The methods describe whole-brain VBM in SPM99 with group-level contrasts comparing bvFTD (N=12) to healthy controls and regression analyses linking IRI subscales to gray-matter atrophy; results include cluster-level findings and a table of VBM results. Sample sizes meet the threshold (bvFTD N=12; controls N=16). The paper provides whole-brain, voxelwise group results derived from the target bvFTD group and reports coordinates/clusters (Table 2, Figure 1). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses [18F]-FDG-PET (FDG-PET) with voxel-wise SPM8 analyses normalized to MNI space and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (clusters and coordinates) correlating metabolism with theory-of-mind deficits. The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD patients (n=11) alongside controls and Alzheimer’s patients (all groups ≥6), and PET analyses are reported at the group level for the target sample. Therefore it satisfies the imaging modality, bvFTD sample, minimum sample size, voxelwise coordinate reporting, and whole-brain group-level result requirements. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, excluded modalities, comorbid psychiatric/neurological confounds) apply.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and has sufficient sample size (I5), it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach). The paper presents diagnostic accuracy, individual example images and qualitative readings, but no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. The study should be excluded from the meta-analysis that requires voxelwise, coordinate-based whole-brain results.

The study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with FSL-VBM and reports voxel-wise results referenced to MNI space. It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) and healthy controls, with sample sizes above the minimum threshold. The paper provides whole-brain group-level contrasts and covariate VBM analyses, reports anatomical locations and states MNI stereotaxic coordinates, and describes overlap/exclusive masking results (tables/figures/supplementary). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, reviews, disallowed modalities, or comorbid diagnostic confounds) are met.

The full text reports a voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analysis using SPM12 comparing bvFTD patients with mild AD and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (displayed at family-wise error corrected p<0.05). The participant sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=220 randomized; MITT n=214), exceeding the minimum sample size. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs AD) presented in figures and described in text. While coordinate tables are not explicitly quoted in the excerpt, the VBM results are reported as voxelwise, whole-brain analyses and are acceptable per inclusion allowance for figures/supplementary reporting. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, reviews, non-empirical work, or disallowed modalities) apply. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This is an empirical, longitudinal resting-state fMRI study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=12) and control/AD groups (controls n=22, AD n=20), meeting sample size requirements. Imaging modality is resting-state fMRI (satisfies I3). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise network-to-region analyses using registration to MNI space and nonparametric permutation testing (FSL-randomize), with group-level voxelwise results and post hoc contrasts described across baseline and follow-up (satisfies I6, I7, I8). The study provides voxel-based morphometry analyses as well and corrects functional results for gray matter volume. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, includes whole-brain results, not seed-only, and participants were screened for major psychiatric/other neurologic comorbidities). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

Although this is a longitudinal MRI study including clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=37) and sufficient sample size, the imaging modality and analysis used (surface-based cortical thickness via FreeSurfer and subcortical volumetry) do not match the meta-analysis inclusion requirement of VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. The protocol explicitly excludes studies that report only cortical thickness methods. While the paper reports whole-brain vertex-wise surface analyses and between-group contrasts, the primary imaging measure is cortical thickness (surface-based), triggering exclusion under E6.

This is an empirical VBM study reporting whole-brain voxelwise results in a defined stereotactic space. The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD patients (n=21) and meets the minimum sample size threshold. The study uses voxel-based morphometry (SPM5/DARTEL) as the imaging modality and reports group-level, whole-brain results (figures and tables with corrected cluster results and coordinates). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review, ROI-only, non-empirical, prohibited modalities, or comorbid psychiatric diagnoses) are met. Therefore the paper satisfies all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=26) and healthy controls, uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with images normalized to MNI space, and reports group-level whole-brain VBM comparisons and voxelwise regression analyses linking GM atrophy to behavioral measures. Sample sizes exceed the minimum threshold. Whole-brain voxelwise results are described (clusters in OFC, amygdala, APC, temporal lobes) and analyses were conducted in MNI space; supplementary materials with further results are referenced. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, reviews, non-empirical, comorbid psychiatric/neuro diagnoses, or disallowed modalities) are violated.

The study used manual segmentation and shape/volume analysis of striatal structures from structural MRI (T1-weighted) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET, therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I3. Analyses are region-of-interest (caudate and putamen) based and do not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach), so it fails I6/I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=28) and sufficient sample size, and the full text appears complete; however, the imaging modality and ROI-only reporting warrant exclusion from this review.

The study employed voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports whole‑brain voxelwise group analyses with MNI coordinates (I6, I7). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) (I4) and meets the minimum sample-size requirement (I5); results are reported in figures/tables and text (I8). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria are violated (e.g., it is an original empirical study, not ROI-only, and includes VBM rather than only DTI/FC). Therefore the paper qualifies for inclusion.

This is essentially a single-case report (N=1 patient with bvFTD) with VBM and FDG-PET comparisons to a control group (n=19) and a separate group of 25 sporadic bvFTD patients. While imaging modalities (VBM, FDG-PET) and presence of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients are present, the study does not provide a group-level voxelwise analysis derived from a bvFTD patient group (the primary target is a single case), and the patient sample for the target condition is N=1, failing the requirement for a minimum patient group size. Additionally, the paper does not report explicit stereotactic coordinates for between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space in the provided full text (results are presented as voxelwise maps/figures without coordinate tables). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5, I6, and I7, and must be excluded.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and uses resting-state fMRI and 18F-FDG PET (I3, I4) with sample sizes meeting minimum requirements (I5), it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) nor provide coordinate tables for between-group contrasts. The analyses are ICA-derived network integrity (loading coefficients/spatiotemporal regression) compared across groups (network-level scalar comparisons), not voxelwise whole-brain group contrasts, so inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=17 in main analyses) and healthy controls, uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-wise structural analyses, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (with coordinates/SI Appendix), and provides voxel-wise correlation and between-group contrasts. Sample size exceeds the minimum (>=6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and does not appear to include excluded designs (not a review, not ROI-only, not only seed-based FC/DTI/thickness). Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Although the full text is complete and the study includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12), uses resting-state fMRI and reports whole-brain voxelwise TBSS and functional connectivity results, it reports only diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and seed-based resting-state functional connectivity analyses. The review’s exclusion criterion E6 disqualifies studies that only report seed-based FC, DTI, or cortical thickness methods. Therefore, despite satisfying multiple inclusion requirements (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8), the study must be excluded because it only uses modalities/methods listed in E6.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and uses whole-brain VBM (with N>6 bvFTD cases) and reports voxelwise results in MNI space, it does not report any between-group contrasts (e.g., patient group vs. controls) nor any bvFTD-specific group-level whole-brain voxelwise results. The primary VBM analyses are across a mixed patient cohort using regression with insight scores; subgroup analyses by diagnostic group produced no significant results. Therefore the study fails to meet I6 (between-group contrast reported in defined stereotactic space) and I7 (at least one group-level whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the target sample group). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (N=18). The paper uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, includes at least 6 participants per group, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results with cluster peaks and MNI coordinates (SPM8 results, cluster- and voxel-thresholds described). Whole-brain contrasts and correlations (e.g., AD vs bvFTD, and merged-group voxelwise regressions) are clearly reported in the text, figures and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria are violated (not a review, not ROI-only, no disqualifying comorbid sample, not a methods-only paper). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study (fALFF and REHO) that prospectively enrolled patients with frontotemporal dementia including clinically-diagnosed bvFTD (5 bvFTD, 10 SD) and age-matched healthy controls. Total patient N=15 and control N=16 meet the sample-size requirement. The authors performed whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts to identify ROIs (reported as eTable 1 and described in the text/figures) and used those results in subsequent analyses, indicating group-level, whole-brain voxelwise findings (supplementary tables/figures are referenced). The paper includes introduction, methods, results and discussion (full text present). Therefore the study meets the imaging modality, patient sample, sample size, between-group coordinate/voxelwise result, whole-brain evidence, and allowance for reporting in supplementary materials. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

Although the study includes bvFTD patients and used [18F]FDG‑PET and MRI (satisfying I3, I4, I5), the imaging data were assessed by visual rating and categorized as presence/absence of frontotemporal abnormalities. The paper does not report any voxelwise, whole‑brain group comparisons nor provide stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) or VBM/fMRI/FDG‑PET statistical maps. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and provides no whole‑brain voxelwise results. Exclusion criterion E3 (no whole‑brain results / only non‑voxelwise visual/qualitative imaging) applies. Full text appears complete.

Although this empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=22) (I4) with adequate sample sizes (I5), and reports voxelwise results with MNI coordinates (I6/I8), the VBM analyses were performed within an a priori region-of-interest mask limited to prefrontal cortex and medial temporal lobe. Because the paper reports only ROI-masked voxelwise results rather than whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise analyses, it falls under the review exclusion for studies that present only ROI (non-whole-brain) analyses. Therefore it does not meet the whole-brain evidence requirement and must be excluded.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=9) and sufficient sample size, it does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) specified by the review inclusion criteria. The primary imaging methods are diffusion tensor imaging (DTI/TBSS and tractography), structural MRI volumetry (ROI-based multiatlas measures), and arterial spin labeling (ASL) perfusion. The review’s I3 criterion requires VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; therefore the study does not meet I3 and should be excluded. Full text is complete and contains methods, results, and discussion.

This is a case report of two relatives (n=1 patient of interest and neuropathology from his father). Although FDG-PET was performed (I3) and the diagnoses are frontal-variant FTD (consistent with bvFTD; I4), the study does not meet key inclusion requirements: sample size is far below the required minimum (I5), no voxelwise whole-brain analyses or reported coordinates are provided (I6/I7/I8), and results are descriptive rather than reported in a defined stereotactic space. The paper is therefore not eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This empirical study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports voxelwise group-level contrasts and correlations with episodic memory using MNI stereotaxic space. It includes a clearly clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=19) and matched controls (n=19) and AD patients (n=18), meeting sample size requirements. Whole-brain VBM results are reported (figures and tables with MNI coordinates) and overlap/exclusive masking analyses are described. The full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, reviews, comorbid psychiatric or substance-abuse samples) are violated. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective.

The study does not meet the imaging-modality inclusion criterion (I3). It uses structural longitudinal MRI analyses (tensor-based morphometry, boundary-shift integral) rather than VBM, fMRI (resting/task), or FDG-PET as required. The paper does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4), has adequate sample sizes (I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons (I6/I7) using SPM5; full text appears complete. Because failure to meet the modality requirement is sufficient for exclusion, the study should be excluded.

The study reports voxelwise FDG-PET analyses (SPM) with group-level whole-brain results (group SPM analysis and a one-sample t-test on impaired patients) overlaid on an MNI template, fulfilling imaging modality and spatial reporting requirements. The sample comprises 17 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (meets minimum N), and analyses include comparisons against a normative database producing voxelwise contrasts in standard space. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI/FC-only, empirical data, and no evidence of disallowed comorbid sample). Therefore the paper satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD patients and uses FDG-PET (satisfying I3, I4, I5). However, it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) nor provide coordinate tables or voxelwise statistical maps. The analysis centers on individual Z-maps and visual reader performance metrics (sensitivity, specificity, kappa) rather than voxelwise group comparisons. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7 requiring between-group voxelwise results. The full text appears complete.

This is a single-case clinical report (N=1) that uses FDG-PET (satisfies I3) and reports a patient who later met criteria for FTD with behavioral symptoms. However it fails key inclusion criteria: sample size <6 (violates I5), no between-group contrasts reported in stereotactic space (violates I6), and no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (violates I7). Additionally the case has comorbid primary lateral sclerosis and obsessive–compulsive disorder, which conflicts with sample requirements (E4). Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis requirements.

The full text reports an empirical neuroimaging study including 29 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 37 healthy controls. The study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) alongside DTI (VBM is explicitly described in Methods) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with images affine-transformed into MNI space and permutation-based, family-wise-error-corrected results. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (>=6). Whole-brain VBM results for the target bvFTD group are reported and described, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise evidence. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so the full text appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met.

Although this paper includes bvFTD patients and uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain voxelwise SPM results in MNI space, the VBM analyses are reported as correlations across the entire pooled sample (brain–behavior regressions) rather than as a clear group-level, whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast specific to the bvFTD group. The manuscript does not present voxelwise, group-level (bvFTD vs controls) coordinate results that are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample, so it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Other inclusion criteria are met (VBM modality, bvFTD sample, adequate sample size, and results presented in figures/tables), but the lack of a bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise contrast prevents inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on group-level imaging results.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusions: it uses voxel-based morphometry/anatomical MRI and resting-state fMRI (and DTI) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=23) (I4) with sufficient sample size (I5). The imaging processing and statistics were performed in standard stereotactic space (registration to MNI152 template and TBSS/FMRIB58_FA template) and whole-brain, voxelwise pipelines (VBM, TBSS, ICA-based rs-fMRI) are described; group-level, whole-brain results and region-level findings are reported and tied to MNI-based analyses (I6, I7). The paper provides full text with methods, results, and discussion; while exact coordinate tables are not visible in the provided excerpt, the methods explicitly reference MNI-space processing and whole-brain voxelwise procedures and supplemental material is indicated for additional results (I8). Therefore the study should be included for the bvFTD imaging review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) as the imaging modality and reports voxelwise, group-level results (including cluster coordinates) aligned to MNI space. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=30), satisfying the requirement for bvFTD inclusion and the minimum sample size (>=6). Whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts and correlation analyses are clearly reported in the main text and figures/tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not just abstract/metadata), and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only analyses) apply. Consequently the paper should be INCLUDED.

The study directly investigates FTD including clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (11 patients) using FDG-PET (alongside ASL-MRI). Sample sizes meet the minimum (≥6 per group). Images were normalized to MNI space and the paper reports voxelwise t-maps and group-level comparisons (voxelwise and ROI), providing whole-brain, between-group results clearly identified for the patient group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, inappropriate modalities, or comorbid samples) are violated.

This paper is a study protocol (NIMROD) describing planned multimodal imaging in multiple dementia cohorts including FTD (criteria referenced to Rascovsky, which targets behavioral-variant FTD). The protocol includes resting-state fMRI and plans for group sizes >=16, so it meets I3 (fMRI), I4 (FTD/bvFTD cohort inclusion is implied), and I5 (sample size). However, it reports no empirical results: there are no between-group contrasts, no reported voxelwise coordinates in MNI/Talairach space, and no whole-brain group-level results (planned analyses only). Therefore it fails I6 and I7. As a protocol/non-empirical paper without original data, it falls under exclusion criterion E5. Full text appears complete (protocol with methods but no results).

This is an empirical study with clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and early-onset AD (n=14). It used tensor-based morphometry (TBM), a whole-brain voxelwise morphometric method closely related to VBM, with scans registered to ICBM stereotaxic space (i.e., MNI-like) and reported voxel-wise between-group contrasts and voxel-wise regressions (figures and ROI analyses). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported and clearly identified for the target bvFTD group. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. It does not include clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD)—the sample comprises primary progressive aphasia (PPA) variants (semantic dementia, progressive nonfluent aphasia, and one logopenic case) and Alzheimer’s disease and healthy controls. Also, the imaging modality is dual-phase 18F-florbetapir PET (amyloid/perfusion-like), not one of the required modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Although the study has adequate sample sizes (PPA n=6, AD n=8, HC n=8) and reports whole-brain, voxel-wise SPM results in MNI space, failure to satisfy I3 and I4 means it cannot be included in this bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

The study reports empirical whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (structural MRI) with bvFTD patients (n=24) and controls, and provides group-level voxelwise results with MNI coordinates. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Methods include whole-brain GLM with permutation testing and TFCE; neuroanatomical results and coordinates are reported in tables/figures. Exclusion criteria (e.g., comorbid psychiatric disorders, ROI-only analyses) are not violated. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all imaging, sample, and reporting inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=22), uses VBM, reports MNI coordinates, and meets sample size requirements (I3, I4, I5, I6). However, all neuroimaging analyses were conducted within an a priori cortical midline structures (CMS) region-of-interest mask rather than as whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The methods and results indicate an ROI-based VBM approach and do not present whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results outside the CMS mask. Therefore the study meets the exclusion criterion for studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results (E3). Full text appears complete.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (I3 satisfied), includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients (I4 satisfied) and has adequate sample sizes (I5 satisfied). However, the voxel-based morphometry analyses reported are performed and presented for pathologically defined subgroups (e.g., Pick’s, MAPT, TDP-A, TDP-C, FUS) relative to healthy controls, not for the clinical bvFTD group as a whole. The paper does not report a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrast specifically identified as coming from the target clinical bvFTD sample (I7 not met). Although whole-brain VBM contrasts are reported for pathological groups (likely in standard space; I6 likely met), they do not provide whole-brain voxelwise results for the bvFTD clinical group required by the review objective. Therefore the study fails to meet the requirement that at least one whole-brain, voxelwise result is reported for the target (bvFTD) sample and must be excluded.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12 at baseline) and uses resting-state fMRI and DTI, the analyses are tract-specific (DTI tractography) and ROI-based functional connectivity. The paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise group-level results or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for between-group contrasts; results are reported as tract-wise metrics and ROI connectivity matrices/figures. Therefore it fails the requirement for voxelwise/whole-brain coordinate results (I6/I7) and meets exclusion criteria for reporting only ROI/tract-based analyses and DTI/seed-based FC methods (E3, E6). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD subgroup (bvFTD; n=17) within the FTD sample, satisfying the bvFTD sample requirement. Imaging modality is voxel-based morphometry (VBM). Sample sizes meet the minimum (FTD n=52, AD n=20, controls n=18). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level VBM results identified for the FTD group and provides results in MNI space (e.g., left superior frontal gyrus coordinates x=-10,y=28,z=60), fulfilling the coordinate reporting requirement. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, reviews, non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

The study uses FDG-PET imaging (voxel-wise SPM analyses) in a sample of 37 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients, which exceeds the minimum sample size. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (comparison of patient scans vs a control database to identify hypometabolism and regression analyses relating FDG-PET to occupation PCA scores), with reported clusters and FWE thresholding. These satisfy imaging modality (I3), bvFTD sample (I4), sample size (I5), reporting of voxelwise whole-brain group results from the target sample (I7), and between-group contrast against controls for hypometabolism (I6). Results are described in the text/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and adequate sample sizes and provides full methods/results/discussion, it does not perform or report VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET analyses. No whole-brain, voxelwise neuroimaging results or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) are reported. Therefore it fails the key imaging and whole-brain reporting inclusion criteria required for this meta-analysis (I3, I6, I7). Full text appears complete.

Although this empirical study uses resting-state fMRI in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample size (meets I3, I4, I5), it does not report voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach). Instead, analyses are performed on parcellated ROI nodes (AAL atlas) and inter-regional network metrics and nodal measures are reported; no voxel-level coordinates or whole-brain SPM-style results are provided. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and must be excluded under E3 (ROI/parcellation-only analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and uses voxel-based morphometry and resting-state/task-based fMRI. It reports voxelwise, whole-brain group comparisons and voxel coordinates (e.g., left ATL [-45,13,-37], left IFG [-52,2,14]) in MNI space and presents group-level VBM and connectivity results for the bvFTD sample. Sample size meets the ≥6 requirement. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review only, ROI-only, exclusive methods like DTI-only, or comorbid psychiatric samples) are met. Therefore the paper satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This empirical study used FDG-PET and VBM (voxel-based morphometry) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM results (including MNI coordinates) comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=24) to controls (n=12). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patients and controls). The paper presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (SPM VBM analysis) with coordinates and statistical maps, and provides ROI and voxelwise PET analyses. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; does not restrict to ROI-only analyses; excludes comorbid psychiatric/substance cases). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8.

Although the study used FDG-PET and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=27), it does not report any voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Imaging assessments were visual ratings and diagnostic classifications rather than voxel-based or statistical parametric maps. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (at least one between-group contrast in defined stereotactic space and a group-level whole-brain voxelwise result) are not met. No other exclusion criteria appear triggered.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=48) and has adequate sample size, it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. The imaging analysis is based on Freesurfer-derived regional (ROI) volumetric measures and reports ROI correlations rather than voxelwise, whole-brain results or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria requiring VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET imaging modality (I3) and whole-brain voxelwise results reported in a defined stochastic space (I6/I7). This matches exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is a single-case clinical report (n=1) of a young woman with severe prefrontal degeneration. While FDG-PET was used (meets I3), the study does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4 not met), has fewer than 6 participants (I5 not met), reports no between-group contrasts or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) (I6 not met), and provides no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from a target sample group (I7 not met). Additionally, the provided "full text" is only the abstract/metadata (fulltext_incomplete=true). No exclusion criteria (E2, E3, E4, E5, E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), has a control group of n=10 satisfying the minimum group size (I5), and reports voxelwise SPM analyses in MNI space (I6), it does NOT provide any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group results for the bvFTD sample (only single-subject SPM contrasts and ROI summaries). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 (no group-level whole-brain result from the target sample). Additionally, the bvFTD subgroup size is only n=4, limiting group-level inference for the target population. Based on these deficiencies the study is excluded from the meta-analysis focused on group-level whole-brain bvFTD contrasts.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: it does not use VBM, fMRI (resting/task), or FDG-PET. Instead it uses deformation-based morphometry (DBM) and arterial spin labeling (ASL) perfusion MRI with joint-ICA. The paper does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) and provides whole-brain voxelwise group analyses (satisfying I4, I5, I7), but the imaging modality requirement (I3) is not met. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). I6 (reporting of coordinates in MNI/Talairach) is not clearly satisfied in the provided content (region lists are given but coordinate tables are not shown), so it is not claimed as met. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study is a prospective clinical study of late-onset frontal lobe syndrome including clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=55) and reports use of FDG-PET as part of diagnostic workup. However, it does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) imaging analyses or provide coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. No VBM or fMRI voxelwise results or tables of stereotactic coordinates are presented. Therefore it fails the review’s required imaging outcome criteria (no whole-brain voxelwise results), and must be excluded.

This is an empirical, whole-brain VBM study of bvFTD including 24 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 179 controls. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), has ≥6 participants in the patient group (I5), reports voxelwise between-group and interaction results with MNI coordinates (I6), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise findings clearly in the text and figures/tables (I7,I8). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply based on provided information. Replication and longitudinal recommendations noted but do not affect eligibility.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (and reports voxelwise group comparisons after normalization to MNI space), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (final bvFTD n=24), has adequate sample size (>6 participants), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FWE-corrected VBM and TBSS results) that are clearly described. Whole-brain results are presented in the text and figures/ROIs were extracted from thresholded T-maps, consistent with acceptable reporting (including supplementary exploration). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review only, ROI-only, only DTI/FC methods, or samples with disallowed comorbidities) are triggered by the content. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This paper is a study protocol / design paper for the ongoing LOF study and does not report empirical whole-brain neuroimaging results required by the meta-analysis. Although FDG-PET and MRI are planned as modalities, no between-group contrasts, voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) coordinates, VBM, or fMRI results are reported. The sample is defined by late-onset frontal behavioral symptoms rather than a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group, and no group-level whole-brain results are provided. Therefore it does not meet the inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I6, I7) and qualifies as a non-empirical methods/design paper without original imaging results (E5).

The study reports empirical, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using both FDG-PET and optimized VBM-MRI (meets imaging modality requirement). The sample includes 13 clinically diagnosed FTD patients using Neary consensus criteria and explicitly excluded semantic dementia and progressive nonfluent aphasia, i.e., the remaining group corresponds to behavioral-variant FTD presentation. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Analyses used SPM with normalization to MNI space and report voxel-by-voxel group contrasts with results in tables/figures (whole-brain, group-level results). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are violated. Therefore the study should be included.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses VBM and FDG-PET imaging (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4); has at least 6 participants in one group (controls n=10) satisfying the sample-size threshold (I5); reports between-group voxel-wise contrasts with reported local maxima coordinates in standard stereotaxic space (MNI) (I6); presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (I7); and these whole-brain results are clearly described in figures/tables and text (I8). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and coordinate tables, so it appears complete for screening purposes. Note: patient group size is small (n=5) but the inclusion criterion requires at least 6 participants in either patient or healthy group, which is met by the control group. No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) and uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses reported (coordinates, thresholding) in MNI space. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=19; controls n=20). The paper reports group-level whole-brain results and neuroimaging-behavior correlations with coordinates and statistical thresholds, satisfying the meta-analysis imaging and reporting requirements. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, neuroimaging details) is present.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging-modality and reporting criteria for the review. The imaging analysis uses structural MRI with Freesurfer-derived cortical thickness/volumetric measures (surface-based morphometry), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (violating I3). The paper does not report between-group voxelwise coordinates in a standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach), so criterion I6 is not satisfied. The patient sample includes only five VSM-20 family members with MRI (failing the >=6-patient requirement for the target analyzed group), and the study’s patient cohort also includes comorbid neurological syndromes (ALS, parkinsonism, corticobasal features), violating the requirement for a pure bvFTD sample (E4). Finally, the imaging results are based on cortical thickness/volumetric methods rather than the required modalities, so E6 applies. Full text appears complete. Exclusion based on E4 and E6; inclusion criteria I4 and I5 (presence of clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants and at least 6 bvFTD participants in the sporadic bvFTD comparison group) are present, but the modality and reporting requirements are not met.

This study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a clinical FTLD sample with a substantial subgroup diagnosed as behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) (21/29), satisfying the requirement that bvFTD patients are included (I4). Sample sizes meet the threshold (FTLD n=29; controls n=30) (I5).
