The imaging analysis used SPM and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates referenced in standard space (MNI/Talairach) in tables and figures (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only results, seed-based FC/DTI-only methods, or comorbid psychiatric/substance-abuse confounds) are violated. Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This article uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM), includes a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) subgroup with whole-brain voxelwise contrasts reported (coordinates in stereotactic space), and has sufficient sample size (25 healthy controls; total patients n=18) meeting the minimum N>=6 requirement for at least one group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain SPM results for bvFTD vs controls (figures and coordinate tables) and provides methods, results, and discussion in full-text form. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review/meta-analysis, ROI-only, seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness only, or comorbid psychiatric/other-dementia-only samples) are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=22) and reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain VBM results in standard space (MNI). Imaging modality: VBM (satisfies I3). Sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and sufficient sample size (I4, I5). The paper reports between-group contrasts and covariate analyses with results localized in MNI coordinates and shown in figures/tables (I6, I8). Voxelwise GLM and permutation testing with FWE/FDR correction across frontal/temporal masks constitute whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results from the target sample (I7). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not only other modalities).

This is an original empirical study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (SPM8/DARTEL) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results (voxelwise threshold p<0.001, pFWE<0.05) in MNI space. The sample includes 31 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, plus other patient groups and 75 controls, meeting the minimum sample size requirement. The paper provides voxelwise between-group/covariate analyses and reports peak regions (tables/figures) and performs co-atrophy checks, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness only; no disqualifying comorbid sample issues noted). Therefore, all relevant inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met.

This empirical study includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=16), used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, and reports voxel-wise, whole-brain group contrasts with results referenced in MNI space. Sample sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD and control groups ≥6). The paper provides whole-brain voxelwise analyses (permutation testing) and reports anatomical/coordinate results (MNI) for group and dimension correlations. Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, reviews, disallowed imaging methods, comorbid psychiatric/substance disorders) are met. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the review.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=33) (I4), and meets the minimum sample size requirement (I5), it reports region-of-interest analyses focused on the posterior cingulate cortex (PCC), visual readings, ROI-based SUVr and regression/ROC analyses. There is no evidence in the full text of whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts reported in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or any tables/coordinates of voxelwise results. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results and instead falls under the exclusion criterion for studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results (E3). Full text appears complete.

Although this study used VBM (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and had >=6 patients (I5), it does not report any between-group (patient vs control) voxelwise contrasts in a standard space. The voxelwise analyses were restricted to a frontal mask (region-restricted VBM) and report within-group correlations between gray matter volume and behavioral scores with MNI coordinates; however, no whole-brain, group-level between-group results are presented. Therefore it fails the required inclusion criteria I6 and I7, and the analysis effectively constitutes a region-of-interest/masked voxelwise analysis, meeting exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete.

This full text reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=10) (I4) and healthy controls, with sample sizes exceeding the minimum (I5). The paper provides voxelwise, group-level between-group contrasts reported with MNI coordinates and tables/figures (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=28), has adequate sample sizes (patients and controls >6), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise VBM results with Talairach coordinates (satisfying a defined stereotaxic space). The manuscript provides whole-brain analyses and peak voxel coordinates linking atrophy to task performance and caregiver burden. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not a non-empirical methods paper, and not using only excluded modalities). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an original, empirical neuroimaging study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=23) that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and FDG-PET voxelwise analyses. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with anatomical localization in MNI space and describes between-group contrasts and voxelwise correlations (VBM SPM results, thresholding and coordinates reported, with supplemental tables/figures). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. There is no evidence of exclusion criteria being violated (not a review, not ROI-only, not only FC/DTI/cortical thickness, and comorbidities were screened/excluded). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete.

This is a single-case report (n=1) describing an atypical bvFTD presentation with structural MRI and SPECT/perfusion imaging. It does not use VBM, task or resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The sample does not include at least 6 participants (I5 not met). No between-group contrasts or group-level whole-brain voxelwise results in a standardized space (MNI/Talairach) are reported (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it fails multiple mandatory inclusion criteria required for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

Although the study uses resting-state fMRI (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=41) with sufficient sample sizes (I4, I5), it reports ROI/parcellation-based network analyses (AAL116) and graph-theoretical MST results rather than whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in stereotactic coordinates (MNI or Talairach). The paper presents region-level connectivity and AAL node identifiers/coordinates and network metrics, but no voxelwise group contrast tables or coordinates that would satisfy I6 and I7. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is a clinical symptom comparison study that used SPECT/FDG-PET only to support diagnoses; it did not perform VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or voxelwise FDG-PET group analyses and did not report any whole-brain, stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) between-group coordinates. Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases (n=4 within FTD group) and patient group sizes exceed 6, the study fails to meet imaging-analysis inclusion criteria (I3, I6, I7). Therefore it cannot contribute the required whole-brain neuroimaging coordinate data for the meta-analysis.

The study used voxel-based morphometry (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases within pathology subgroups (I4). It also meets the sample size criterion via 50 healthy controls (I5). However, the imaging analyses report whole-brain VBM contrasts by FTLD-TDP pathological subtypes (type 1/2/3) rather than by the clinical bvFTD diagnosis; no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are presented specifically for a bvFTD clinical group (violates I7). Additionally, the provided full text does not present MNI/Talairach coordinates for a bvFTD contrast (I6 not satisfied). Therefore it does not provide the required whole-brain, voxelwise results for the target clinical group (bvFTD) and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion present).

This study does not meet the required imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting criteria for inclusion. It uses structural region-based volumetric analyses (Freesurfer parcellation) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (violates I3), and it reports ROI/parcel correlations and regression results rather than between-group voxelwise contrasts with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (violates I6/I7). Therefore it should be excluded. The full text appears complete.

This is an original, empirical study that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (FSL-VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts mapped to MNI standard space. The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) patients (n=14) as well as Alzheimer’s disease patients and controls, meeting the minimum sample-size requirement. The paper presents whole-brain VBM results (group contrasts and covariate analyses) and reports clusters/figures overlaid on the MNI template; results are reported in tables/figures and described in the text. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so the article is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, non-empirical, or exclusive DTI/FC/cortical-thickness-only methods) apply.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients (n=27) with healthy controls. Voxel-based morphometry was applied and whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported, including MNI coordinates for peak effects and tables/figures; they also performed ROI/SVC analyses but whole-brain results are present. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The full text includes introduction, methods (behavioral and imaging), results with MNI coordinates, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, non-VBM modality, or major comorbidities) are met.

The full text reports an empirical multicenter study including 52 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients and 60 controls, using resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). Analyses include whole-brain, voxelwise VBM (normalized to MNI space) and whole-brain functional connectivity/graph-theory results with group-level between-group contrasts reported (figures and supporting tables). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results clearly attributed to the bvFTD sample and supplies coordinates/normalized-space analyses (MNI). The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) (I4,I5), reports group-level between-group contrasts normalized to MNI space using SPM/DARTEL (I6), and presents whole-brain voxelwise results (e.g., contrasts thresholded at P<0.05 FWE whole-brain) clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD vs control groups (I7). The study reports longitudinal 18F-FDG-PET (FDG-PET) voxelwise analyses (SPM) on clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD (behavioral variant equivalent) with 22 patients and 15 controls. It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and reports maxima in Talairach space. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. It meets all required inclusion criteria (imaging modality, clinical diagnosis, sample size, coordinate reporting, whole-brain voxelwise results). No exclusion criteria are violated.

The study is a methods paper applying a unified VBM/TBM approach to groups including frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patients (N=30), Alzheimer’s disease, and controls, with whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses. However, the FTD sample is not specified as clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD). The review’s I4 criterion requires inclusion of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; because the paper reports only FTD without specifying bvFTD subtype, it does not meet I4 and must be excluded. Other inclusion criteria are met (VBM/TBM imaging modality, adequate sample size, whole-brain voxelwise results reported), and the full text appears complete.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons in MNI space (I6,I7,I8). The sample includes 18 clinically defined ALS-FTD patients (diagnosed by Neary criteria) and 15 controls, meeting the minimum group size (I5). ALS-FTD patients were defined using Neary criteria for frontotemporal dementia, which corresponds to clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD in many studies; thus they satisfy the review’s requirement for bvFTD patients (I4). The full text includes background, methods, results and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This paper reports an empirical FDG-PET study of patients diagnosed with the frontal variant of frontotemporal dementia (fv-FTD), an established synonym/older term for behavioral-variant FTD. The study used voxel-wise SPM2 analyses with Talairach-based localization and reports whole-brain voxelwise correlations (tables/figures of clusters and coordinates). Sample sizes meet the minimum (fv-FTD n=18; controls n=18). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (i.e., core article content) and no exclusion criteria are violated (not a review; not ROI-only; not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness only; comorbidities excluded). Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on MRI and reports group-level whole-brain VBM contrasts with MNI coordinates, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (Neary criteria) with adequate sample sizes (FTD N=26; MRI subset FTD N=21, controls N=12), and provides whole-brain voxelwise results and coordinate tables/figures. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. No exclusion criteria are met. Thus it satisfies all imaging, sample size, diagnostic, and reporting criteria for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI and VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the sample (7 bvFTD cases; I4), has sufficient sample size (14 FTD-GRN+ patients and healthy groups; I5), reports between-group voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics (I6), and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results clearly attributed to the target groups (I7). Results are reported as figures/coordinates (I8). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, reviews, seed-only FC, DTI-only, comorbid psychiatric samples) are violated based on provided content.

The study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients including some behavioural-variant cases (I4), has sufficient sample sizes (37 FTD patients; I5), and presents group-level voxelwise analyses described in the text (I7). However, the provided full text does not include explicit between-group results reported in a standard stereotactic coordinate space (MNI or Talairach), and I cannot verify any reported coordinates for voxelwise contrasts (criterion I6). Because I6 is required and cannot be confirmed from the provided full text, the study must be excluded. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) that includes a clinically diagnosed behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) cohort (n=10). Sample sizes meet the minimum (≥6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise VBM contrasts and discusses results in MNI/DARTEL template space; VBM outputs and comparisons to controls are presented. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study used volumetric MRI segmentation (regional GM/WM volumes) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails inclusion I3). It reports lobar/regional volumetry and group comparisons, not whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6 and I7). The sample includes FTD and semantic dementia but does not explicitly state behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) diagnosis (fails I4). Therefore it does not meet the required imaging modality nor the whole-brain coordinate-based results required by the review. Full text appears complete.

This empirical study includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD participants from a MAPT mutation family (8 symptomatic bvFTD patients, 3 asymptomatic carriers, and 8 non-carrier controls). It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and [18F]FDG PET imaging, performs whole-brain voxel-wise group comparisons using SPM8 normalized to MNI space, and reports voxel-wise results (figures and tables) with specified thresholds and cluster sizes. Sample sizes meet the minimum (≥6) in patient and control groups. Full-text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for imaging modality, diagnosis, sample size, and whole-brain voxelwise reporting.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=24) (I4) with sample sizes above the minimum (I5); reports between-group voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates (e.g., 6, −46, 24) (I6); provides whole-brain, group-level VBM results (comparisons vs. controls and AD) that are clearly described (I7); and results/coordinates are reported in text/figures consistent with acceptable reporting (I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria are violated.

While this study meets several methodological inclusion criteria (uses voxel-based morphometry; adequate sample sizes; reports whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts), it does not clearly report that the symptomatic patient sample consists of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) cases. Participants are described as genetic mutation carriers with progressive cognitive or behavioral change but the paper does not specify bvFTD diagnostic classification or apply accepted bvFTD clinical criteria. The review requires studies including clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4). Because I4 is not satisfied based on the provided full text, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) methods (SPM12) and includes clinically diagnosed FTD cases (stated to correspond to bvFTD) with adequate sample sizes, it does not report a group-level, whole-brain between-group contrast (bvFTD group vs. controls) in a defined stereotactic space with reported coordinates. The paper focuses on single-subject VBM comparisons to a normative database to generate normative brain volume reports and presents SPM overlays/illustrations rather than group-level voxelwise results or coordinate tables in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7 required by the review.

This study includes a voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analysis (registered to MNI space) that corroborates the visual rating results. The sample contains clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=22) and healthy controls, satisfying sample-size requirements (≥6). Group-level voxelwise comparisons were performed and results are reported (with VBM results referenced in supplementary figures available online). Thus the paper provides whole-brain, between-group VBM findings for the target sample. Although peak coordinates are not shown in the main text, the authors state VBM analyses were registered to MNI space and supplementary VBM figures/tables are provided online, satisfying reporting requirements.

This study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses on a sample of clinically diagnosed behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients (n=23) and healthy controls (n=20). It includes whole-brain, voxelwise two-sample t-test group comparisons and voxelwise regression analyses confined to the patient group, with results described and displayed (figures/tables/supplementary). Sample sizes exceed the minimum threshold. Imaging modality (VBM on structural MRI) matches the inclusion imaging types. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only results, prohibited modalities, or comorbid-sample issues) are violated. Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

Although this empirical study uses resting-state fMRI (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (81 bvFTD; I4) with adequate sample size (I5), it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The paper explicitly states no healthy control group was available and presents dynamic connectivity/metastate metrics derived from ICA components and state-space analyses rather than voxelwise whole-brain group-level contrasts or coordinate tables. Therefore it fails the requirement for reporting at least one between-group voxelwise result in stereotactic coordinates and lacks whole-brain voxelwise group-level results from the target sample, so it must be excluded.

While the study uses FDG-PET and MRI (meets I3) and includes a sufficient number of FTLD patients (14; meets I5), it does not report that the patient sample specifically consists of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). Participants are described generically as FTLD patients diagnosed by Neary criteria, with no breakdown by clinical subtype (bvFTD vs. semantic or language variants). The review requires inclusion of studies with clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4), which is not satisfied here. Full text is complete and whole-brain voxelwise SVM maps are reported, but absence of explicit bvFTD diagnosis prevents inclusion.

This study does not include behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) patients. The sample comprises normal controls, Alzheimer’s disease, and semantic-variant PPA (SV-PPA) patients; VBM analyses were performed on NC and AD groups and explicitly excluded SV-PPA from the main VBM to avoid confounding. Although the study uses VBM (I3) and reports whole-brain results in MNI space (I6) and includes subgroup sizes ≥6 (SV-PPA n=10, meeting I5), it fails to meet the critical inclusion criterion I4 (study must include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients). Therefore it does not address the review objective (bvFTD) and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports an empirical study of clinically diagnosed frontal-variant (behavioral variant) FTD patients (n=13) using resting-state FDG-PET with voxelwise SPM2 analyses. Whole-brain, voxelwise cognitivo-metabolic correlations are reported with Talairach/MNI coordinates and cluster results (reported in text/figures/tables). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patients and controls), and the paper includes complete methods, results, and discussion. Imaging modality, sample, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and coordinate reporting satisfy the review’s imaging and reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, reviews, disallowed modalities, comorbid psychiatric/neurological illness) are violated. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a single-case clinical case report (n=1) of C9ORF72-associated slowly progressive FTLD presenting predominantly as semantic variant PPA. While FDG-PET was used (satisfying imaging modality criterion I3), the study does not include clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients (I4 not met), has far fewer than the required sample size (I5 not met), and it does not report any group-level between-group contrasts or whole-brain voxelwise results in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) (I6/I7 not met). Therefore it cannot contribute eligible whole-brain group-level coordinates or contrasts for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete for the case report. Exclusion is based primarily on lack of whole-brain, group-level data and insufficient sample size.

This is a descriptive case series of five FTD-related gene carriers. Although individual patients had MRI and in one case FDG-PET, the study does not present group-level VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET analyses, provides no between-group contrasts or coordinates in MNI/Talairach space, and reports only 5 participants (fewer than the required minimum of 6). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5 (sample size), I6 (between-group coordinate results), and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group results). The full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses resting-state fMRI (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (18 bvFTD cases; meets I4), and has adequate sample sizes (32 FTD patients, 17 asymptomatic carriers; meets I5). It reports voxelwise, whole-brain results with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., -40,44,14) and cluster-level FWE-corrected findings in standard space (meets I6 and I7). Results are presented as coordinates and described in the text/figures (meets I8). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review, ROI-only, seed-only FC, DTI-only, or non-empirical paper) are triggered. Therefore the paper satisfies all required inclusion criteria for this review.

The study uses voxelwise gray-matter MRI analyses consistent with VBM (meets I3) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group atrophy maps (meets I7/I8). However, it does not clearly specify inclusion of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients — participants are described as an FTD-spectrum clinical diagnosis without explicit labeling of bvFTD (I4 not clearly met). Critically, the VBM/imaging subgroup sample sizes for patient subgroups are very small (tau-positive n=5; tau-negative n=4; fv-AD n=3), so the target patient groups reported in whole-brain contrasts have <6 participants (fails I5). Coordinates in Table 3 are referenced but not shown in the provided text, making I6 uncertain. Because the key inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not satisfied (and I6 uncertain), the study is excluded from the bvFTD meta-analysis.

This study uses structural T1-weighted MRI volumetric analysis (automated basal forebrain segmentation using GIF) rather than Voxel-Based Morphometry, fMRI, or FDG-PET, so it fails the required imaging-modality inclusion criterion (I3). Although it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) with sufficient sample size (148 bvFTD; I5), the paper reports region-based volumetric results rather than whole-brain, voxelwise results in a defined stereotactic space (no MNI/Talairach coordinate tables or voxelwise contrasts), thus failing I6 and I7. Therefore it meets the exclusion criterion for reporting only ROI/region volumetry with no whole-brain voxelwise results (E3).

The study does NOT meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting inclusion criteria. It uses volumetric MRI measures (global whole-brain atrophy via BBSI and ventricular expansion via VBSI) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it does not report any group-level voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) contrasts or coordinate tables of whole-brain analyses. Although bvFTD patients are included (n=11) and sample sizes meet the minimum, the absence of voxelwise whole-brain results and use of non-qualifying imaging modalities prevents inclusion in this review focused on VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET voxelwise studies. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

While the study meets several methodological inclusion criteria (uses VBM, reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results in MNI space, and has sufficient sample sizes within patient groups), it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., patient vs healthy control) in MNI/Talairach space. The analyses are within-group voxelwise correlations between neuropsychiatric symptom scores and grey-matter density across genetic FTD carriers, rather than between-group contrasts required by inclusion criterion I6. In addition, although symptomatic carriers are included (some meeting consensus criteria for bvFTD, PPA or FTD‑MND), the paper does not clearly present results specifically for a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (so I4 is not clearly satisfied). Therefore the study fails to meet key inclusion criteria (notably I6) and is excluded.

This study uses VBM (I3), has adequate sample sizes (30 per group; I5), and performs voxelwise analyses in MNI space with whole-brain voxelwise maps (I6, I7). However, the sample is described as “frontotemporal dementia (FTD)” without specification that patients are clinically-diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD). Inclusion criterion I4 requires that the study include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; this is not confirmed in the full text. Because I4 is not met, the study cannot be included for a review restricted to bvFTD. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the study uses VBM and FDG-PET (I3) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons with sufficient sample sizes (I5, I7, I8), the participant sample comprises patients with frontotemporal dementia plus motor neuron disease (FTD-MND). The meta-analysis exclusion criteria disallow samples with concurrent other neurological symptoms; inclusion of motor neuron disease therefore violates E4. Furthermore, the behavioral-dominant subgroup represents FTD-MND with behavioral features rather than a cohort of clinically diagnosed, isolated bvFTD patients. Because E4 is violated, the study must be excluded despite meeting several imaging and reporting criteria.

This full-text reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses and diffusion tensor MRI in a cohort including 13 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and matched healthy controls. The paper presents whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts registered to MNI standard space (TBSS and VBM results are reported and visualized), and reports group-level results for bvFTD versus controls. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD N=13; controls N=25). The study therefore meets the imaging modality requirement (VBM), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, reports whole-brain voxelwise results in a defined stereotaxic space, and presents those results in text/figures/tables. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, inappropriate imaging modality only) apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This study does not meet the imaging and analysis inclusion criteria. It uses conventional structural MRI descriptions (visual MRI findings) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not satisfied). It does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results nor provide coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (I6 and I7 not satisfied). Although bvFTD patients are included in the cohort, the imaging modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting required for this review are absent, so the study cannot be included.

This multicenter PET study includes FDG-PET analyses and reports results for clinically diagnosed FTD patients (behavioral-variant diagnostic criteria were used) with N=36, satisfying imaging modality (I3), inclusion of bvFTD cases (I4), sample size (I5), and reporting of group-level voxelwise patterns (I7). However, the paper does not report any between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic coordinate space (MNI or Talairach) or provide coordinate tables/voxelwise contrast coordinates required by I6. Because I6 is not met, the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is a single-case/family case report of corticobasal syndrome with PGRN mutation that includes FDG-PET images but does not study behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients. It does not meet key inclusion criteria: I4 (subjects are CBS/FTLD-U, not clinically diagnosed bvFTD), I5 (sample size is one proband / family — far fewer than 6), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space), and I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results). The paper is an empirical neuropathologic/genetic case report with neuroimaging but lacks the required group-based voxelwise analyses and bvFTD patient sample for meta-analysis. Therefore it must be excluded.

The study does not meet the imaging and whole-brain analysis inclusion criteria. It uses structural MRI measures (a novel FA index and frontal atrophy ratios) rather than VBM, resting/task fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients but does not specify behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) specifically (I4 not met). The paper does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in MNI/Talairach space or coordinate tables/figures (I6 and I7 not met). Sample size criterion is met (41 FTDs) but failure to satisfy the imaging modality and voxelwise reporting criteria requires exclusion. Full text appears complete.

This is a case report of two siblings (n=2) with C9ORF72-associated FTD/ALS investigated with FDG- and 11C-PiB-PET. Although FDG-PET was used (I3), the study does not include clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD participants specified as bvFTD (I4 not clearly met), has an insufficient sample size (fails I5: only 2 patients), and provides no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or coordinate-based results in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it does not meet the required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete. No predefined exclusion criteria (E2–E6) specifically apply, so exclusion is based on unmet inclusion criteria.

This study is an audit of routine MRI reports and qualitative visual rating; it does not use VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET, nor does it report any group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates. Although the sample includes 22 patients with FTD (meeting the minimum sample size), key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I6, I7) are not met. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports an optimized voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analysis (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (13 bvFTD; meets I4) and adequate group sizes (n>=6; meets I5). Voxel-wise between-group contrasts were performed after normalization to MNI space and whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps are reported and described (meets I6 and I7). Whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in text (meets I8). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an empirical neuroimaging study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=33) and matched healthy controls. Methods include voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and resting-state fMRI analyses with images normalized to MNI space; group-level, whole-brain voxelwise two-sample t-tests are reported and coordinates are provided (Supplementary Table 1). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=33; controls n=34). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts clearly attributed to the bvFTD group and presents results in figures/tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI-only/seed-only, and patients without major comorbid psychiatric/neurological diagnoses). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

The full text reports both task-based fMRI (in healthy subjects) and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses including a direct, whole-brain VBM comparison between AD and bvFTD patients. Clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients were included (VBM sample n=48; behavioral samples include 14 and 15 bvFTD participants), satisfying minimum sample-size requirements. The paper provides group-level, voxelwise between-group contrasts with reported anatomical localization and MNI coordinates/figures and describes whole-brain results (significant GM density differences in prefrontal regions for bvFTD and medial temporal/parietal regions for AD). The text includes methods, results, and figures/tables supporting voxelwise findings. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for imaging modality (I3: VBM/fMRI), bvFTD sample (I4), sample size (I5), reporting of between-group contrasts in stochastic space (I6), whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I7), and allows coordinate reporting in text/figures (I8).

This study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses (using DARTEL/SPM) and presents group-level voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates. The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients (final diagnosis bvFTD in 12/19 C9ORF72 cases; 11 mutation carriers underwent volumetric MRI), meeting the minimum group size (n=11 patients, n=15 controls). Whole-brain, group-level VBM results are clearly reported for the C9ORF72 mutation group (overlaid on the MNI152 template and with MNI co-ordinates displayed in figures), and results are described in the text and figures. Although the imaging group is a genetic (C9ORF72) subgroup rather than an exclusively clinically-defined bvFTD group, the cohort includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases and the voxelwise whole-brain findings are applicable to bvFTD-related pathology reported in the manuscript. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria.

This article is a narrative review/author manuscript (Annual Review chapter) synthesizing evidence rather than reporting original empirical imaging data on bvFTD. It does not present a primary sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with an imaging study using VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, nor does it report between-group voxelwise coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails to meet multiple required inclusion criteria (I3–I7). It matches exclusion criteria for being a non-empirical review/meta-analytic paper (E2) and a non-empirical paper without original data (E5). Full text appears complete (introduction, discussion, references present).

Although the study used 18F-FDG PET (satisfying I3) and included clinically diagnosed FTD cases using bvFTD criteria (n=7, satisfying I4 and I5), it does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise statistical results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The paper presents visual/qualitative reads, SUVR summaries, and descriptive group counts/accuracy metrics, but no voxelwise coordinates, group-level statistical maps, or between-group contrasts in a stochastic space. Therefore criteria I6 and I7 (and I8) are not met. This places the study into exclusion E3 (no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients with behavioral-variant cases (I4) and the FTD group size is ≥6 (likely n=9; I5), it does not present any voxelwise, whole-brain group-level statistical contrasts in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The analysis is based on visual reading/classification of individual scans and reports concordance/sensitivity/specificity, without reporting coordinates, voxelwise maps, or whole-brain statistical results. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (and I8) requiring between-group voxelwise results in defined stochastic space. This matches exclusion criterion E3 (no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

The study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this review. It uses tau and amyloid PET imaging ([11C]PBB3 and [11C]PiB), not one of the required modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) (I3 unmet). The sample comprises 10 patients with familial FTDP-17 due to MAPT N279K mutation (a genetic frontotemporal dementia with parkinsonism), but patients are not characterized as clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) as required (I4 unmet); most cases are PSP-like and only two had initial personality changes. Although the study has sufficient sample size and reports voxelwise SPM analyses in standard space, failure to satisfy the required imaging modality and explicit bvFTD diagnosis means it does not match the review eligibility. Full text appears complete.

This article is a scientific commentary (non-empirical) summarizing and discussing the findings of Jiskoot et al.; it does not present original empirical data or report primary whole-brain voxelwise results with stereotactic coordinates. It does not itself use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET to report between-group contrasts nor report a sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants meeting the sample-size threshold. Therefore it fails to meet the review’s inclusion criteria and meets the exclusion criterion for non-empirical papers.

This study uses T1-weighted structural MRI with automated hippocampal subfield volumetry (region-of-interest analysis), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise results in a stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables. Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and sample sizes meet the minimum, the paper reports only ROI/subfield volumetric comparisons rather than whole-brain voxelwise contrasts. Therefore it violates the review’s inclusion requirements for imaging modality and whole-brain voxelwise results and meets the exclusion criterion for ROI-only analyses (E3).

Although the study used FDG-PET (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=13) within its FTD spectrum group (I4), had adequate group sizes (I5) and performed voxelwise SPM analyses in MNI space (I6), it does not report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results specifically for the behavioral variant FTD subgroup alone. The reported whole-brain contrasts are for a mixed FTD group (various FTLD subtypes combined) rather than for bvFTD-only, so the paper does not provide the required whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the target sample group (fails I7). Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet the review objective because participants were clinically diagnosed with probable Alzheimer’s disease, not behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). Although some cases were later reclassified as frontotemporal dementia after amyloid-PET (n=12), the study did not recruit or present a group of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients nor report group-level whole-brain voxelwise results specifically for bvFTD. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 and I7. The full text appears complete.

The study recruited a heterogeneous early-dementia sample (suspected AD or FTD; labels include probable/possible FTD, AD/FTD, probable/possible AD) rather than a clearly defined clinical behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) group and does not report bvFTD-specific group-level voxelwise contrasts. Although voxel-wise modulated GM maps (VBM-like processing) and whole-brain P-maps are reported and total sample sizes exceed the minimum, the lack of a distinct clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample and absence of bvFTD-specific whole-brain results mean the study does not meet the review’s target-sample criteria. Coordinates in MNI/Talairach space are not clearly provided for bvFTD-only contrasts. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports an empirical, whole-brain voxelwise longitudinal morphometric analysis (SPM12/DARTEL; Jacobian determinant contraction maps) comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls. The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=44) and HCs (n=97), exceeding the minimum sample size. Analyses are performed in standardized (MNI) space with group-level t-maps, consensus ROIs, and cross-validated effect sizes—i.e., between-group voxelwise contrasts are reported and displayed. The manuscript contains full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore it meets the imaging modality requirement (voxel-based morphometry-style voxelwise analysis), includes bvFTD patients, reports whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space, and provides sufficient data for inclusion.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain voxelwise results and adequate group sizes; however, it does not report inclusion of clinically diagnosed behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients. The pathology-based groups are stratified by molecular pathology (3R-tau, 4R-tau, TDP43A/C) and include semantic dementia for TDP43C, but the paper does not state that any participants were diagnosed specifically with bvFTD. Because inclusion criterion I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) is not met, the study must be excluded from a review targeting bvFTD. Full text appears complete.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (FTLD-U vs controls, FTLD-MND vs controls, and direct comparisons) performed after normalization to the MNI template (satisfies I6 and I7). Sample sizes meet the threshold (11 FTLD-U, 7 FTLD-MND, 18 controls), satisfying I5. Participants fulfilled consensus clinical criteria for frontotemporal dementia and are described as having a clinical diagnosis of frontal-variant/frontotemporal dementia (equivalent to behavioral variant FTD in nomenclature), satisfying I4. Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise findings and described in figures and text (I8). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E2,E3,E5,E6) apply.

This is a small clinicogenetic case-series/family report using FDG‑PET (I3 satisfied) but it does not include clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients (fails I4; phenotype described as AD‑like/FTDP-17), has far fewer than the required N≥6 participants (fails I5), and does not report whole-brain, voxelwise between-group coordinates in a standard stereotactic space (fails I6 and I7). The PET findings are presented qualitatively and via ROI/normalized surface projections without coordinate tables or voxelwise group contrasts. Full text appears complete.

This empirical study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise results (FWE-corrected) relating gray matter to conjunction search performance. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12), meeting the minimum sample size requirement. Results are reported as whole-brain VBM findings across standard stereotactic space and group comparisons of voxel values were conducted. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete for screening purposes. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study does not meet the required imaging-modality inclusion (I3). The meta-analysis requires VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET modalities, but this paper uses cortical thickness (structural MRI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI)/FA (multimodal MRI), not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET. This falls under exclusion criterion E6 (studies that only report seed-based FC, DTI, or cortical thickness methods). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This article is a study protocol/methods paper describing the LEFFTDS longitudinal cohort design, procedures, and MRI acquisition methods. It does not present empirical between-group imaging results (no VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET analyses with coordinate-based whole-brain findings), nor does it report group-level contrasts in MNI/Talairach space. It is non-empirical (methods/protocol) without original imaging outcome data, so it does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion requirements (I3–I8) and matches exclusion criterion E5 (non-empirical paper without original data). Full text appears complete for a protocol (introduction, methods, procedures) but contains no results relevant to the review.

This is a single-family case report with one clinically diagnosed bvFTD proband and a few healthy mutation carriers. Although FDG-PET was used (I3) and a bvFTD case is described (I4), the study does not meet key inclusion requirements: sample size is far below the minimum (I5), there are no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in a standardized space (no MNI/Talairach coordinates; I6), and no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from the target sample are presented (I7/I8). Thus it lacks whole-brain, group-level analyses required for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete.

Although the study includes FDG-PET (I3), clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) and ≥6 bvFTD cases (I5), it does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) for the bvFTD group. The FDG-PET analyses described are single-subject comparisons to controls producing counts of hypometabolic voxels, and no coordinates or group-level voxelwise tables/contrasts are presented in the provided full text. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied. Full text appears complete for core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical MRI study that uses a VBM-style whole-brain gray matter pipeline (SPM12 segmentation, DARTEL registration, normalization to MNI space and smoothing) and derives voxelwise SVM weight maps presented as 3D/figure maps. The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients (FTD of the behavioral type) with n=39 (>6). The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise discriminative maps (weight maps) in MNI space and describes regional results in the text and figures (and supplementary material). Therefore it satisfies imaging modality and whole-brain voxelwise result requirements and reports results for the target bvFTD group. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not limited to seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness). Full text appears complete.

This article is a single-case clinical report (n=1) and does not meet the review’s imaging and group-analysis requirements. It used a plain structural MRI for clinical description, not VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). Sample size is below the required minimum of 6 participants (fails I5). No between-group contrasts, coordinate results in MNI/Talairach space, or group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses are reported (fails I6 and I7). Although the case appears to be behavioural-variant FTD clinically (I4 satisfied), the paper lacks the necessary imaging modality, sample size, and whole-brain group results required for inclusion. Full text appears complete for the purposes of screening.

This is a case-report of two clinically diagnosed FTD patients (n=2) with structural CT/MRI images described qualitatively. It does NOT use VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET (I3 not met); the sample size is far below the required minimum of 6 participants (I5 not met); no between‑group contrasts or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) are reported (I6 not met); and no group-level, whole‑brain voxelwise results are provided (I7 not met). The full text appears complete (introduction, case reports, discussion). Therefore the study cannot contribute to the review meta-analysis and is excluded.

This is a single case report (N=1) describing a patient with evolving DLB and later bvFTD-like features. Although 18F-FDG PET was used (meets I3), the study does not include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group of participants (I4), has fewer than 6 participants (I5), provides no between-group voxelwise contrasts or stereotactic coordinates (I6), and reports no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I7). Additionally, the patient had overlapping DLB features (coexisting other dementia), so the sample is not a pure bvFTD group. Therefore it does not meet required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study uses atlas-based ROI volumetry of cerebellar subregions from T1-weighted MRI rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Results are reported as regional ROI volumes and groupwise nonparametric tests, with no voxelwise MNI/Talairach coordinates or whole-brain voxelwise group results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). The study does include bvFTD participants (I4) and adequate sample sizes (I5), but fails I3, I6 and I7. Full text appears complete.

The study is a longitudinal structural MRI volumetric analysis (whole-brain and ventricular volumes using boundary shift integral), not one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). It does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (meets sample size), but it does not report any voxelwise whole-brain group-level results in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables/figures. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet the required imaging-modality inclusion criterion (I3). The imaging work uses SPECT perfusion and visual MRI assessment rather than Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM), fMRI, or FDG-PET, so it does not provide the required modality data for the meta-analysis. The paper does include clinically diagnosed frontal-variant/bvFTD (fvFTD) patients and adequate group sizes (I4, I5 satisfied). A voxelwise SPM analysis was performed on SPECT, but the meta-analysis requires one of the specified modalities (VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study does not meet the imaging modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements for the review. Although it includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (FTD subgroup n=8) and a matched comparison group (meeting I4 and I5), the neuroimaging analyses are based on region-of-interest parcellation (SABRE) and multivariate PLS of regional volumes derived from structural MRI rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (violating I3). Additionally, results are reported as ROI-based regional volume relationships rather than voxelwise coordinates in a standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach), so criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied. Therefore the paper must be excluded under E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

The study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports group-level voxelwise atrophy comparisons (VBM group comparisons) tied to network regions, indicating whole-brain between-group contrasts (I7). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) (I4) and group sizes exceed the minimum of 6 (I5). The methods describe SPM8/DARTEL preprocessing and voxelwise general linear models in standard space, and the results present peak regional atrophy patterns derived from these voxelwise contrasts, implying reporting in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) consistent with I6. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria appear to apply (no ROI-only analyses, not a review, not seed-FC/DTI-only).

This study does not meet the imaging-modality and analysis requirements for the review. It uses structural MRI with manual ROI volumetry of hippocampus and amygdala rather than Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM), fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). The analyses are ROI-based volumetric comparisons and not whole-brain, voxelwise results in a standardized stereotactic space (no MNI/Talairach coordinates reported), so it does not provide the required whole-brain, between-group voxelwise contrasts (fails I6 and I7). Although the sample size criterion is met (FTLD n=17, controls n=10) and the FTLD group includes a frontal-variant (fvFTD) clinical subgroup, the lack of the required imaging modality and absence of coordinate-based whole-brain results warrant exclusion. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical neuropsychological study of fvFTD (n=20) with behavioral tasks and MRI visual atrophy ratings, but it does not use VBM, fMRI (resting/task), or FDG-PET and reports no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results or stereotactic coordinates. Therefore it fails critical inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7. It does satisfy I4 (clinically diagnosed fvFTD sample) and I5 (sample size ≥6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Exclusion is based on not meeting required imaging and whole-brain result criteria for the meta-analysis.

This article is a narrative review/CME overview of FDG- and amyloid-PET in Alzheimer’s disease and does not present original empirical data from a sample of clinically diagnosed behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients. Although it discusses FDG-PET (I3), it does not include bvFTD participants (fails I4), does not report between-group voxelwise contrasts or coordinate tables (fails I6/I7), and is a non-empirical review rather than an original study. Therefore it does not meet the review’s inclusion criteria.

Although the study uses structural MRI and VBM-like preprocessing, the analysis integrates voxelwise W-scores into 179 predefined ROIs and builds a classification model on ROI-level atrophy burdens. The full text does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space, nor does it present voxelwise statistical maps for the clinical groups. In addition, the sample is familial FTLD mutation carriers with heterogeneous clinical presentations (various syndromes) and the paper does not specifically report results limited to clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). Therefore the study fails the requirement for whole-brain (voxelwise) results and does not clearly satisfy the bvFTD sample criterion. This meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results).

The study uses FDG-PET (meets imaging modality I3) and includes FTLD patients, but does not specifically state inclusion of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). More importantly, the paper reports single-subject SPM t-map classifications and diagnostic accuracy metrics rather than reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast results with coordinates in a standard stereotactic space for a bvFTD (or FTLD-bv) group. Therefore it does not provide the required whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach space needed for inclusion. Full text appears complete.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) features (VBM-GM, VBM-WM, VBM-Brain) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise SVM significance maps (p-maps) describing clusters and anatomical locations. The FTD sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12 within FTD n=33). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patients and controls >6). Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported and visualized in template space (figures and p-map descriptions), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain group-level voxelwise outcomes. Thus the paper meets criteria for imaging modality, inclusion of bvFTD, sample size, and whole-brain voxelwise reporting in defined template space (reported via group template and figures). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses manual ROI volumetry of the putamen on T1-weighted MRI rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (does not meet I3). It reports only region-of-interest volume measures and does not provide whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results in MNI/Talairach space (does not meet I6/I7). Therefore it constitutes an ROI-only study with no whole-brain results (meets exclusion E3). The sample sizes are adequate (meets I5), but the imaging modality and lack of coordinate-based, whole-brain results necessitate exclusion. The paper also does not explicitly state behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) diagnosis (I4 not clearly met).

This is a longitudinal study including converters who met diagnostic criteria for probable bvFTD (6 of 8 converters) and uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (VBM and TBSS) comparing converters versus non-converters/non-carriers. At least six bvFTD patients are present (n=6), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are reported and illustrated in figures/maps. The study therefore satisfies the imaging modality criterion (VBM), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, has sufficient sample size (≥6), and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (figures/tables). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study investigates semantic dementia/semantic-variant PPA patients (SD/svPPA), not clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). Although imaging methods (voxel-based morphometry/voxel-based analyses) and whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space are reported and the sample size (n=47) is sufficient, the sample does not meet inclusion criterion I4 (bvFTD patients). Therefore it does not address the review objective of studies on bvFTD and must be excluded.

Although the study met several inclusion criteria (FDG-PET imaging, includes bvFTD patients within a mixed FTD sample, adequate sample size, and reports voxel coordinates), the imaging analyses were restricted to an anatomically defined mask (ROI) rather than a whole-brain, voxelwise analysis. The review requires at least one group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) result. Because this paper reports only masked/ROI-constrained voxelwise results with no whole-brain contrasts, it violates the review’s whole-brain requirement (exclusion E3). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E5 (non-empirical paper): This article is a narrative/pictorial review summarizing MRI findings across dementias and does not present original empirical imaging data or analyses. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 — does not perform original VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET analyses; I4 — does not include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD participant sample; I5 — no participant/sample sizes reported (no patient or healthy groups with ≥6 participants); I6 — no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space; I7 — no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results presented. Full text completeness: full article content (introduction, discussion, references) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not use an acceptable imaging modality (I3 not met) and reports only ROI-based volumetric analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates (I6 and I7 not met). Specifically, imaging was FreeSurfer-based regional volumetry (ROI volumes) rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET, and no MNI/Talairach coordinates or group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=26) and I5 (sample size ≥6). Exclusion criterion met: E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete for screening (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical genetic/clinical case-family study that does not meet the imaging and whole-brain analysis inclusion criteria. The study used structural MRI and Tc-99m-ECD SPECT (regional hypoperfusion reported qualitatively) but did not use VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG‐PET (I3 not met). No voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) are reported—results are descriptive and regionally reported rather than coordinate-based (I6 and I7 not met). Although FTD phenotypes are described in the family, the imaging/methodological requirements for inclusion are not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain group comparisons (SPM12, DARTEL, MNI standard space) and reports cluster-level FWE-corrected voxelwise results (caudate head, frontal and subcortical regions). The ALS-FTD subgroup explicitly met criteria for behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD). The ALS-FTD group contains 7 patients (≥6), and healthy controls are N=24. Between-group contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise findings are reported and identified as coming from the target sample (ALS-FTD/bvFTD). Diffusion analyses are present but VBM provides eligible imaging modality. No exclusion criteria are met, and the provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This is a single-patient case report (n=1) describing a clinical bvFTD diagnosis with genetic findings and structural MRI. It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met), includes fewer than 6 participants (I5 not met), and provides no group-level between-group contrasts or whole-brain voxelwise results in standardized space (I6 and I7 not met). The full text appears complete for a case report (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore it fails required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This paper reports two clinical case reports (N=2) with PET imaging. Although FDG-PET and Florbetapir/T807 imaging were performed (I3 satisfied), the study does not include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group of at least 6 participants (violates I4/I5), nor does it present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or stereotactic coordinates (violates I6/I7). The imaging results are descriptive single-subject findings rather than coordinate-based, group-level analyses required for inclusion. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is not eligible for this meta-analysis.

This paper is a single-patient case report using 18F-FDG PET and a detailed diagnostic workup. While it meets I3 (uses FDG-PET), it does not satisfy key inclusion criteria required for the meta-analysis: it does not include a clinically diagnosed group of bvFTD patients (I4), has a sample size of one (failing I5 which requires ≥6 participants in either patient or control group), and reports no between-group voxelwise contrasts or coordinate-based whole-brain group results (failing I6 and I7). The study therefore cannot contribute group-level whole-brain coordinate data needed for the review. The full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study uses FDG-PET and reports voxel-wise, whole-brain group analyses in Talairach space and includes an FTD group (n=13). However, the review specifically targets behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). The full text consistently labels the patient group as ‘fronto-temporal dementia (FTD)’ without specifying that these were clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases. Because inclusion criterion I4 (explicit inclusion of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) is not met / cannot be confirmed from the full text, the study must be excluded from this bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD patients (n=33) and sufficient sample sizes (controls and patients >6), it does not meet the imaging-modality inclusion requirement. The study uses structural MRI morphometry with automated segmentation and radial distance surface mapping of the putamen (ROI-based shape analysis), not VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET. It reports region-specific surface/ROI results for the putamen rather than whole-brain, voxelwise results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables. Therefore it constitutes an ROI-only analysis with no whole-brain voxelwise contrasts, which violates the inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criterion E3.

The study does not meet key imaging and whole-brain analysis inclusion criteria. Inclusion criterion I3 requires VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; this study used structural MRI and tau (FTP) and amyloid PET in a small subset, but not FDG-PET, VBM, or fMRI. Additionally, there are no reported group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (I6/I7): PET findings are described as small focal uptakes in 3 individual TSC patients and CSF/imaging findings are largely reported qualitatively, not as whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts or coordinate tables. Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (N=16, meeting I5 and partially I4), the absence of the required imaging modality and whole-brain voxelwise results means the study fails critical inclusion criteria and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I5 (FTD sample n=12, >=6), I6 (voxelwise between-group contrasts performed with SPM12), and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 — the paper reports patients with “FTD” but does not specify that these are clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD); the review requires explicit inclusion of bvFTD. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are clearly met. Because I4 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

This is a single-case report (n=1) of a bvFTD patient treated with citalopram. Although FDG-PET was performed (I3) and the patient meets clinical bvFTD diagnosis (I4), the study fails required inclusion criteria: it has fewer than 6 participants (fails I5), reports no between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6), and provides no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (fails I7). Full article content is complete. Therefore it does not provide the group-level whole-brain imaging data required for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical VBM study including clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=20). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise VBM analyses (permutation-based GLMs) with results localized in MNI space and provides group-level contrasts and coordinate results. Sample sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD=20; controls=20; AD=14). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies imaging modality (I3), inclusion of bvFTD patients (I4), adequate sample size (I5), reporting of between-group contrasts in defined stochastic space (I6), whole-brain voxelwise results from target group (I7), and acceptable reporting of coordinates/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met.

Although this study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within its cohort (and has adequate overall sample sizes), the reported whole-brain voxelwise analyses and coordinate results are organized by pathologic FTLD-TDP subtype rather than by a clinically defined bvFTD group. The paper does not provide a separate group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast or coordinates explicitly for bvFTD patients, nor does it specify the number of bvFTD cases or present bvFTD-specific MNI/Talairach coordinates in the provided full text. Therefore it fails the review requirements that whole-brain voxelwise results be reported for the target sample (bvFTD) and that between-group coordinates for that target group be available for meta-analysis.

This is an original, empirical PET imaging study of frontal-variant frontotemporal lobar degeneration (fv-FTLD), equivalent to behavioral variant FTD. It uses 18FDG-PET (satisfying I3), includes clinically diagnosed fv-FTLD patients (I4) with 18 patients (and 24 controls; PET subset n=8 patients, n=6 controls) meeting the minimum sample size (I5). Analyses were voxelwise SPM reported in MNI stereotactic space with between-group contrasts and coordinate results (I6), providing group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results clearly identified for the target patient group (I7,I8). The paper is empirical, with whole-brain voxelwise results and no excluded comorbidity concerns. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical structural MRI volumetry study using boundary-shift integral and Freesurfer to measure whole-brain and hippocampal volumes in genetic FTD (MAPT/GRN). It does not use VBM, task or resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). It also does not report voxelwise whole-brain, stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinate-based group results (I6/I7 not met) — results are global volumetric measures and plotted trajectories rather than voxelwise analyses. Sample size meets the N≥6 requirement but the required imaging modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting criteria are not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

Although this study uses VBM-like voxelwise deviation maps (I3), includes clinically diagnosed FTD with bvFTD cases (I4), and has adequate group sizes (I5), it does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group contrasts or voxel-coordinate results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The paper focuses on individual voxel-wise deviation scores, region-wise volumes, ROC analyses, and reader agreement, but does not present group-level voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables for the bvFTD group. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (required: between-group contrasts reported in defined stereotactic space and at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result). Closest applicable exclusion is E3 (no whole-brain results reported for group-level contrasts).

The study used structural MRI volumetry with FreeSurfer ROI-based analyses (regional volumes and multivariate regressions), not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET, so it does not meet imaging-modality inclusion criterion I3. The paper reports ROI-based associations rather than whole-brain voxelwise, stereotactic-space (MNI/Talairach) coordinate results; no group-level voxelwise, whole-brain results or coordinate tables are provided, so it fails I6 and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses). The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients including behavioral and language variants (the text states behavioral variant FTD was included) and sample sizes exceed 6 (I4 and I5 satisfied). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because it does not use an eligible imaging modality and lacks whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results, it must be excluded from the bvFTD meta-analysis.

Although the study uses VBM-based structural MRI and includes a frontotemporal dementia (FTD) group (n=12), it does NOT specifically identify or report clinically-diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD). Crucially, the paper does not present between-group whole-brain, voxelwise contrast results with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space; results are reported as multivariate SVM classification performance (AUC, PPV/NPV, radar plots) rather than coordinate-based statistical maps or tables. Therefore it fails the key inclusion criteria I4 (bvFTD sample) and I6/I7 (reporting of between-group voxelwise coordinates/whole-brain group-level results). Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts (with coordinates in Montreal Neurological Institute standard space). The sample includes a frontal-variant frontotemporal dementia group (FTD-FV), which corresponds to behavioral/frontally-predominant FTD, with N=22 (≥6). Whole-brain VBM results and voxelwise correlations between gray matter and olfactory scores are clearly reported in the main text/tables/figures. The full article contains introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only analyses, only non-allowed modalities, or non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore the study should be included.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (post hoc subgroup, n=7) (I4) and has sufficient sample size (≥6 in bvFTD subgroup) (I5), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (I7, I8), it does NOT report any between-group (patient vs. healthy control or patient-subgroup vs. control) voxelwise contrast in a standard stereotactic space. The reported contrasts are within-participant (before vs after memantine) and subgroup within-sample analyses, not the between-group contrasts required by inclusion criterion I6. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This study does not meet the core imaging and whole-brain reporting criteria for the review. It uses structural T1/T2 MRI with automated WMH segmentation and zonal/volumetric analyses rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). Results are reported as regional/volumetric and patient-specific zonal summaries rather than voxelwise whole-brain contrasts in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach), and no coordinate tables/voxelwise maps are provided (fails I6 and I7). The sample comprises familial/genetic FTD mutation carriers (symptomatic and presymptomatic) but does not specifically state clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD participants (uncertain for I4). The sample sizes meet the minimum (I5 satisfied). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it provides only regional/ROI-style volumetric lesion analyses with no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results (E3).

This is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (meets I4) with N=31 (meets I5) and the full text is available. However, it uses structural MRI visual atrophy ratings rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3).
