It does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts, stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach), or whole-brain voxelwise group results (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it does not provide the required whole-brain, voxelwise imaging results for inclusion. Excluded on the basis that no whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (closest matching exclusion criterion: E3).

Although the study used [18F]FDG PET (satisfies I3) and included an FTD group of 18 patients (satisfies I5), it does not specify that FTD cases are clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) and it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or provide stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). The paper presents visual ratings, diagnostic outcomes, and case counts rather than voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables, so it fails inclusion criteria I4, I6, and I7. Therefore it does not meet the review’s requirements for whole-brain voxelwise evidence from bvFTD patients.

This full text reports MRI-based voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing early-stage MSTD (bvFTD) patients to controls, with whole-brain voxelwise results and stereotactic locations referenced in supplementary Table 4. The VBM sample comprised 7 patients and 19 age- and gender-matched controls (≥6 participants in a group). Patients were clinically diagnosed with behavioural-variant FTD (bv-FTD). The paper provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise findings (figures/heat maps and coordinates in supplement), satisfying reporting in a defined stereotactic space. The manuscript includes full sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, irrelevant modality) apply. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and uses VBM with results reported in MNI space, and group sizes meet the minimum. However the reported VBM analyses are correlational within a combined FTLD patient cohort rather than between-group (patient vs control) contrasts, and the significant findings derive from small-volume (ROI) voxelwise corrections rather than whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results specific to the bvFTD subgroup. Therefore it does not satisfy inclusion criteria requiring a between-group contrast (I6) and a group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the target sample group (I7).

The study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports voxelwise, whole-brain group contrasts using an MNI template (SPM99), satisfying spatial reporting requirements. The sample included clinically diagnosed frontal variant FTD (fvFTD, equivalent to bvFTD) patients (majority of cases) and 20 healthy controls, with 21 FTD cases (>=6 per group). Group-level whole-brain VBM results are presented and compared between pathologic/clinical subgroups and controls (figures/tables). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This article is a narrative review summarizing imaging findings across dementia subtypes, not an empirical study. It does not present original VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET data from a sample of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients, provides no participant counts meeting the ≥6 threshold, and reports no between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space or coordinate tables. Therefore it fails the requirement for original whole-brain, voxelwise results from a bvFTD sample. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods summary, results narrative, discussion), but it is non-empirical, so excluded under the non-empirical paper criterion.

This is an empirical study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=7) and uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with images normalized to MNI space, reporting voxelwise whole-brain results (clusters, FWE p-values and coordinates referenced in figures/tables) that relate semantic performance and eating-behaviour measures to grey-matter atrophy. Sample sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD n=7; HC n=21). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise VBM results are provided and reported in standard stereotactic space; conjunction and correlation analyses produced anatomically localized clusters. Although some VBM analyses are reported across the pooled participant sample rather than a bvFTD-only contrast, the study nonetheless provides whole-brain voxelwise anatomical results that include and pertain to the bvFTD patients, making it relevant to the meta-analysis objective. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=18) and meets the sample size requirement, it does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Instead it uses region-based structural volumetry from a multi-atlas segmentation tool and focuses analyses on predefined frontal ROIs. The paper does not report whole-brain, voxelwise results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI/region-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

The study used resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=25) (I4) and sufficient sample sizes (I5). Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise, registered to MNI space and reported group-level voxelwise contrasts (network-to-region and region-to-region analyses with TFCE FWE correction and figures overlaid on MNI-152) satisfying reporting in a defined stereotactic space (I6,I7). Whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in text (I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only, seed-only, DTI-only, or excluded comorbid samples) apply. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

While the study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes sufficient sample size (FTLD N=31, I5), it does not meet key inclusion requirements for this review. The sample is described as frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) but the paper does not specify that patients had clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD), so I4 is not satisfied. Crucially, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group contrasts in standard space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD (or FTLD) to controls or another group; analyses are primarily within-subject voxel-wise correlations and ROI-based logistic regressions. Therefore I6 and I7 are not met, and the study effectively provides ROI/within-subject results rather than the required whole-brain between-group voxelwise results (E3). Full text appears complete.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTLD patients (n=6) and adequate control sample and uses automated SPM-based structural MRI volumetry, it reports lobar ROI volumetric measures and simple ratios rather than whole-brain, voxelwise group results or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). The meta-analysis requires VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET with at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrast reported in standard space. This study therefore lacks whole-brain voxelwise results/coordinate tables (and is effectively ROI-based volumetry), so it does not meet key inclusion criteria (I3/I6/I7) and is excluded on the basis of E3.

This empirical study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) to investigate grey matter correlates of episodic memory in clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (both sporadic bvFTD and C9ORF72 carriers). Sample sizes meet the minimum (C9:8; sporadic bvFTD:15; Controls:15). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and brain–behaviour correlations with anatomical localization referenced to MNI space and provides coordinate tables/figures (including supplementary table S1). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, imaging, VBM analysis), Results (voxelwise atrophy and correlations), and Discussion, enabling assessment. No exclusion criteria (e.g., reviews, ROI-only analyses, only non-eligible imaging modalities, or disallowed comorbid samples) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion requirements for the review objective on bvFTD imaging studies.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=18) and compares them with AD (n=17) and healthy controls (n=28). The paper uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (FSL–VBM) with images registered to MNI152 space and reports group-level voxelwise atrophy and covariate results (including separate analyses for bvFTD and AD), meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (>=6). Results are presented as voxelwise cluster findings (with thresholds and space specified), satisfying coordinate/defined-space reporting. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the review.

Although this study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed frontal-variant (behavioral) FTD patients (I4) and a sufficient sample size (70 patients, I5), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise principal component maps derived in MNI space (I7), the manuscript does not present a between-group contrast (patient vs. control) reported as results in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) nor are coordinate-based peak activations/tables provided in the supplied full text. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (required). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered by the available content. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This paper is a two-case clinical report (n=2) and does not meet key inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. Although it uses FDG-PET (I3) and one patient met criteria for frontotemporal dementia, it does not include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample of sufficient size (fails I4/I5: <6 participants). It provides no group-level between-group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (no MNI/Talairach coordinates reported), so I6 and I7 are not met. The study is therefore unsuitable for inclusion. Full text appears complete.

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (7 of 14 FTD cases are bvFTD) and applies whole-brain voxelwise VBM and resting-state fMRI analyses (ICA and multiple local connectivity metrics). Sample sizes meet the threshold (FTD group n=14; control groups ≥6). Methods state spatial normalization to MNI space and report group-level voxelwise results and discriminative maps (figures/tables/supplementary), fulfilling the requirement for between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space and whole-brain evidence. The paper is empirical, not a review, and does not rely solely on ROI or seed-based FC, DTI, or cortical thickness methods. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis imaging and outcome reporting requirements and is relevant to bvFTD. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided.

This is an empirical neuroimaging study that uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (and TBSS/DTI) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise results normalized to MNI space. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=10) and healthy controls (n=26), satisfying the minimum sample size requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain VBM analyses and between-group comparisons (patient groups vs controls) referenced as reported in Supplementary Information (S11), and presents voxelwise clusters and coordinates in MNI space; qualifying whole-brain results are acceptable in supplementary materials per the criteria. No exclusion criteria are violated. Therefore, all required inclusion criteria are met.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (satisfying modality requirement), the report focuses on ROI-derived PET and MRI biomarkers, derived indices, and classifier-based group discrimination metrics (AUC, balanced accuracy). The paper does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables/figures; VBM/TBM are used only to derive indices rather than reported voxelwise results. Additionally, the FTD sample is reported generically as “FTD” without clear specification or counts of behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) subgroup. Therefore the study does not provide the required whole-brain voxelwise results and does not clearly report clinically diagnosed bvFTD results, and so fails key inclusion requirements. Exclusion applies because the analyses are ROI/indices-only with no whole-brain voxelwise results (E3). Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses VBM (I3) and includes sufficient sample sizes (FTD n=11; HC n=22; I5) and reports whole-brain VBM voxelwise results (I7), it does NOT explicitly state inclusion of clinically-diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD). The diagnostic group is listed as “frontotemporal dementia (FTD)” without specification of behavioral variant, so inclusion criterion I4 (explicit bvFTD sample) is not met based on the provided full text. Additionally, the provided text does not show stereotactic coordinates for between-group contrasts within the excerpt (I6 uncertain), though whole-brain results are described. Full text appears complete for screening. Main exclusion is failure to confirm I4 (bvFTD).

This is a single-case genetic/clinical report (N=1) and does not meet the imaging- and analysis-based inclusion requirements for the review. Specifically, the study does not use VBM, task or resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met); includes only one bvFTD case rather than at least 6 participants in a patient or control group (I5 not met); reports no between-group contrasts or results in a standardized stereotactic space (no MNI/Talairach coordinates; I6/I7 not met). There are no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results to include in the meta-analysis. Therefore it must be excluded.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports voxelwise group comparisons with stereotactic coordinates. The sample includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patients (behavioral variants are described by behavioral symptoms) with adequate sample sizes (32 patients total, 27 with usable MRI; 47 controls). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise results (coordinates provided: e.g., x=41,y=12,z=-13; x=43,y=1,z=-7) and displays whole-brain VBM findings (thresholded maps shown on mean brain), meeting the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise evidence; results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria are violated (not a review, not ROI-only, not an excluded modality). Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8.

The full text reports an empirical FDG-PET study that identifies and validates a whole-brain metabolic covariance pattern for bvFTD. It includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (probable and pathology-confirmed definite cases) and healthy controls, with sample sizes well above the minimum. Imaging data were preprocessed in MNI space and voxelwise, whole-brain results/topographies are reported and validated across sites (including voxelwise correlation and thresholded maps). The paper contains full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for imaging modality, sample, sample size, and whole-brain voxelwise reporting.

This study uses task-based fMRI (meets I3) and reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with peak coordinates aligned to a standard space (meets I6, I7, I8). The sample includes an EXEC subgroup (n=5) characterized by dysexecutive and social-interpersonal impairment (behavioral/social conduct changes, emotional blunting, loss of insight), consistent with clinical presentations of behavioral-variant FTD (meets I4). Although the EXEC subgroup has 5 patients (<6), the healthy control group has 11 participants, satisfying the criterion that at least one group has ≥6 participants (I5). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext is complete. Confidence is moderate because the EXEC subgroup is not explicitly labeled "bvFTD" and the EXEC patient count is slightly below 6, but the clinical description aligns with bvFTD and whole-brain voxelwise results are reported.

Although the study uses FDG-PET and includes an FTLD patient group (n=11), the imaging analysis is ROI-based (regional z-scores from GE Cortex ID) and the paper does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise, stereotactically localized (MNI/Talairach) between-group contrasts or coordinate tables/voxelwise maps. The review requires whole-brain voxelwise results in standard space. Additionally, the paper reports FTLD generally and does not explicitly specify clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD). Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise reporting and violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This empirical study directly investigates bvFTD and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=13). It uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (FSL VBM) on structural MRI and reports voxelwise group-level contrasts with MNI coordinates (e.g., x=14,y=-4,z=-16). Sample sizes meet the threshold (bvFTD n=13; controls n=12; AD n=14). The paper provides whole-brain, voxelwise results clearly attributed to the bvFTD group and presents coordinate-based findings in text/figures and tables. The full text contains introduction, methods (including imaging acquisition and VBM preprocessing), results (group VBM contrasts and correlations), and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only analyses, non-empirical, or prohibited imaging modalities) are violated. Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria.

Although the study includes clinically characterized behavioral-predominant FTD patients and uses FDG-PET (satisfying I4 and I3), it does not present group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) with reported coordinates. Imaging findings are described for individual patients (case descriptions of 2–3 mutation carriers) rather than as voxelwise group analyses or between-group statistical maps/tables. Therefore criteria I5, I6, and I7 (adequate group size for the reported imaging sample and reporting of whole-brain voxelwise between-group results in stereotactic coordinates) are not met. Full text appears complete.

This paper is a narrative review of neuroimaging in young-onset dementias rather than an empirical study reporting original voxelwise neuroimaging results. It summarizes multiple conditions (including bvFTD) but provides no primary data, no methods/results reporting of VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET group-level whole-brain contrasts with coordinates from a bvFTD sample. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I3–I7 and falls under non-empirical papers exclusion. Full text appears complete (review article).

This is an empirical VBM study that includes an ALS-FTD subgroup (n=18) who met Neary criteria for FTD and exhibited prominent behavioral abnormalities consistent with behavioral-variant FTD. The study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on whole-brain T1-weighted MRI (1.5T), reports voxelwise group-level contrasts and provides MNI coordinates/voxelwise results in figures/tables. Control group size (n=15) and patient subgroup size exceed the minimum (>=6). Whole-brain, voxelwise results are clearly described. Although the paper labels the group as ALS-FTD rather than explicitly as “bvFTD,” the use of Neary criteria and reported behavioral features support inclusion as bvFTD-relevant. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present; supplementary tables are online but this is acceptable.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (meets I3) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space (meets I6), it does not provide sufficient data specific to clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). The paper includes only 3 clinically labeled FTD patients (FTD = 3), below the required minimum of 6 participants for the target patient subgroup (I5 not met). Whole-brain/group results are reported for FTLD as a combined group (N=13), not specifically for a bvFTD subgroup, so there are no group-level whole-brain results clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample (I7 not met). Additionally, the sample includes multiple other dementia subtypes (mixed etiologies), which conflicts with the requirement to isolate bvFTD effects (exclusion E4 applies). Full text appears complete.

Although this is an empirical VBM study that includes a substantial sample of patients diagnosed with the FTD variant (likely behavioral-variant FTD), uses VBM (MNI-referenced results), and meets minimum sample-size requirements, the imaging analyses are correlational across a pooled multi-diagnosis cohort rather than reporting any between-group voxelwise contrasts specific to the bvFTD/FTD diagnostic group. The paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast or other whole-brain VBM result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD/FTD group alone (the authors state single-diagnostic-group VBM is methodologically unsound and instead perform across-group regressions and co-atrophy checks). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and cannot be included for a meta-analysis requiring bvFTD-specific whole-brain between-group results.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (18 in discovery sample, 7 in the FDG-PET subset) and uses 18F-FDG PET with voxel-wise SPM analyses (satisfying I3, I4, I5), it does not report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts in MNI/Talairach space specifically comparing bvFTD (or any patient group) versus controls. The imaging results consist of voxel-wise regression/correlation analyses (associations between oculomotor parameters and metabolism) across the pooled sample and do not present group-level bvFTD vs. control whole-brain contrasts clearly reported as such. Therefore the paper fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (required between-group whole-brain contrasts identified for the target sample). Full text appears complete. Excluded for lack of required between-group whole-brain results for bvFTD.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to perform whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons between clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients (behaviorally-defined FTD) and healthy controls. Sample size meets the threshold (9 patients, 26 controls). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (atrophy in rostral limbic system regions) and includes at least one coordinate (periaqueductal gray center) and describes results that would be in stereotactic space. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

Although the study uses resting-state fMRI and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, the analyses are ROI/parcellation-based graph-theory metrics (82 VOIs) and edge/hub connectivity results rather than voxelwise, coordinate-based between-group contrasts. The paper does not report MNI/Talairach coordinates or any whole-brain voxelwise group-level results in stereotactic space. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). The full text is complete and sample sizes meet I5 (HC n=26), but lack of coordinate/voxelwise results prevents inclusion in this meta-analysis.

The study is a detailed clinical–pathological report of three familial FTDP-17 kindreds (P301L tau mutation). It does not use the required neuroimaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET); reported imaging includes structural MRI, CT and SPECT, not VBM or PET FDG, and no voxelwise whole-brain analyses in stereotactic space with reported coordinates are provided. Therefore it fails critical inclusion criteria I3, I6 and I7 despite including clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on unmet imaging and whole-brain analysis requirements.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed behavioral/dysexecutive FTLD subgroup (bvFTLD) with n=71 and an imaging subset bvFTLD n=51 satisfying sample size requirements (I4,I5). Whole-brain VBM analyses were performed and images were normalized to MNI space with group-level voxelwise contrasts and reported peak coordinates/tables relating atrophy to fluency measures (I6,I7). Whole-brain results are presented in tables and figures (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of criteria; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This full-text reports a voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analysis comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient (homozygous MAPT R406W) to 30 matched healthy controls. It provides whole-brain, voxelwise group-difference maps superimposed on the MNI template with statistical thresholds (pfwe<0.05 and uncorrected maps), and figures showing atrophy patterns. The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD case, and the healthy control group meets the ≥6 participant requirement. The paper is empirical, not a review, and reports whole-brain results (figures/maps) in a defined stochastic space. No exclusion criteria were violated. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts for behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) patients. The sample includes 31 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (and >6 per group). Results are reported on an MNI standard brain with figures and a supplementary table of coordinates (Table S2), and whole-brain contrasts (bvFTD carriers vs noncarriers and bvFTD vs controls) are described. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only analyses, non-empirical, or incompatible imaging modality) are violated.

This is a single-case VBM study of a pathologically confirmed FTD patient with behavioral symptoms (bvFTD-like) compared to 28 controls; VBM is used and whole-brain atrophy is reported. However, the paper does not provide stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) or a coordinates table for the between-group VBM contrasts, so inclusion criterion I6 is not satisfied. Additionally, the patient has documented alcohol and prescription substance misuse, introducing comorbidity that violates exclusion criterion E4. Although other inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I7, I8) are met, failure to meet I6 and presence of E4 require exclusion.

This study does not meet the imaging-modality or whole-brain voxelwise reporting inclusion criteria. It uses structural MRI volumetric/hemispheric region analyses (MIDAS semi-automated volumetry) rather than VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The paper does not report voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts or provide stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) from such analyses (I6 and I7 not met). The analyses are effectively region/hemisphere-based rather than voxelwise whole-brain results, therefore it falls under exclusion criterion E3 (ROI/volume-only analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). The full text appears complete. Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTLD participants (I4) and involves sufficient participant numbers for some analyses (I5), failure to satisfy I3, I6 and I7 requires exclusion per the review protocol.

This study uses deformation-based morphometry (DBM), not one of the eligible imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), so it fails modality inclusion criterion I3. It also does not report results in a standard stereotactic coordinate space (MNI or Talairach); the analysis used a custom 72-year-old reference atlas and no coordinates/tables in MNI/Talairach are provided, failing I6. Additionally, 5 of the FTD subjects met criteria for ALS (a concurrent neurological condition), which violates exclusion criterion E4. Although the study has sufficient sample size (N=22 FTD) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (meeting I5 and I7), the above modality, stereotactic reporting, and sample composition issues require exclusion.

This study satisfies the review criteria: it uses task-based BOLD fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=16) (I4); sample sizes meet the minimum (patients N=16; MRI subset N=11; healthy controls N=16/14) (I5); reports between-group, whole-brain voxelwise VBM contrasts in SPM/standard space with FDR correction and figures/tables (I6, I7); and results/coordinates are presented in text/figures (I8). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, reviews, or disallowed modalities) are triggered. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise results with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., 58,10,-33) and FWE correction. The sample includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patients corresponding to the behavioral-variant FTD phenotype (30 FTD patients described as the FTD variant with frontal behavioural syndrome). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (30 bvFTD; total N=123; controls N=20). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise findings for the overall sample and diagnostic subgroup analyses (FTD subgroup results are reported), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (review-only, ROI-only, non-empirical, or disallowed imaging modalities) are violated. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8.

Although this study used task-based fMRI, included 7 FTD patients, and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with Talairach coordinates, it does not explicitly state that the FTD patients had the behavioral variant (bvFTD). Inclusion criterion I4 requires clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants. Because the paper refers generally to FTD (and includes familial FTDP-17 cases) without specifying bvFTD, I cannot confirm the sample meets I4. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting the bvFTD-specific sample criterion.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts normalized to Talairach space using SPM99. The sample includes 29 FTD patients, with subgrouping that explicitly lists 14 patients described as having a disorder of social and executive functioning, which corresponds to clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). Group sizes exceed the minimum (FTD n=29; controls n=12). Whole-brain SPM results and naming-atrophy correlations are reported with cluster thresholds and coordinates. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Caveat: the paper does not use the exact label “bvFTD,” but the described social/executive dysfunction subgroup aligns with bvFTD criteria, so it satisfies I4.

Although this paper uses whole-brain voxelwise gray-matter maps derived from T1 MRI (VBM-style processing) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=41) with adequate sample sizes, it does not report any between-group contrast (e.g., bvFTD vs control) in a stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The reported analyses are multivariate correlations (SCCAN) relating PBAC scores to GM across a mixed cohort and while Talairach coordinates are provided for component maps, the study does not present a group-level between-group voxelwise contrast clearly attributable to the bvFTD group. Thus it fails key inclusion criteria requiring between-group whole-brain contrasts coming from the target sample. Full text appears complete.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain voxelwise statistical parametric maps including a FTLD (including a behavioural-variant FTD subgroup of 10 patients) vs healthy control contrast. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (30 patients total; 20 controls; bvFTD subgroup n=10). Methods use SPM/DARTEL producing standard-space voxelwise results (typical MNI space) and the paper describes cluster-level and voxelwise results and maps, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets imaging modality (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), adequate sample size (I5), reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard space (I6), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results for the target sample (I7/I8). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (SPM99) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results normalized to Talairach coordinates, including group-level correlations and subgroup contrasts. The clinical cohort includes a defined SOC/EXEC subgroup (disorder of social comportment, personality, and executive functioning), which corresponds to behavioral-variant FTD symptomatology. Sample sizes meet the threshold (64 FTD-related patients; 13 healthy controls; 17 patients with imaging). Voxelwise results are reported in a defined stereotactic space (Talairach) and presented as group-level whole-brain findings (including contrasts between subgroups), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. Full text contains background, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, non-empirical, DTI/FC-only) apply.

Although the study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and included a clinically described FTD group (Neary criteria, with behavioral features) with sufficient sample size, it does not provide a group-level, between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast reported specifically for behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) in a defined stereotactic space. The VBM analyses reported are regression correlations across a combined sample (patients and controls) rather than a between-group contrast (e.g., bvFTD vs controls) reported as MNI/Talairach coordinates attributable to the target diagnostic group. Therefore the study fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7 required by the review objective.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging- and analysis-related inclusion criteria required for the review. Although it includes a clinically diagnosed FTD sample (N=29) and therefore meets I4 (clinical FTD diagnosis consistent with bvFTD features) and I5 (≥6 participants), the imaging modality/analysis do not meet I3/I6/I7: the paper reports SPECT and PET visual inspection and quadrant-based categorization (left/right, frontal/temporal) rather than explicit FDG-PET (not specified) or VBM/fMRI, and it does not report whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts or coordinate-based results in MNI/Talairach space. This constitutes an exclusion per E3 (no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears to contain core sections (methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a single-case report (n=1) using FDG-PET in a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient. It does not meet key inclusion requirements: sample size (I5) — fewer than 6 participants; no between-group contrasts reported in a standard stereotactic space (I6); and no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (I7/I8). The paper provides a single-subject descriptive PET finding (bilateral insular hypometabolism) without coordinates or statistical whole-brain analyses. Although it meets I3 (FDG-PET) and I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD), failure to meet the above inclusion criteria requires exclusion.

Although this study uses VBM (I3), has group sizes ≥6 (I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM contrasts (I7), it does not clearly meet the key clinical inclusion criterion of enrolling clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients (I4). The paper reports patients with pathologically confirmed FTLD who ‘presented clinically as frontotemporal dementia’ but does not explicitly state that participants were clinically diagnosed as bvFTD, and the cohort likely includes language-variant presentations (e.g., PNFA, SD). Additionally, the provided text does not explicitly report stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for between-group contrasts in the excerpt available, so I6 is not clearly satisfied. Because not all required inclusion criteria are verifiably met (particularly I4 and I6), the study must be excluded from the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

This article is a narrative review of FDG‑PET for Alzheimer’s disease rather than an empirical study with original participant data. It does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, does not report any group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses or coordinate tables (MNI/Talairach), and no sample sizes or between-group contrasts are reported. Therefore it fails the requirement for original empirical data and relevant bvFTD sample. Excluded under E5 (non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete for a review article (introduction, methods/technique discussion, results/summary), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This paper reports a whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) study in a sample of 18 frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patients (including cases with prominent behavioural/frontal presentations) and 17 controls. The methods use SPM99 with MNI-based templates and report voxelwise group-level results with coordinates and statistical thresholds. The sample size exceeds the minimum of 6, and the cohort includes clinically diagnosed behavioural/frontotemporal variant presentations (fvFTD/bvFTD features are explicitly described). Whole-brain, voxelwise results are reported and correlated with behavioural measures (NPI). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, non-empirical methods, or disallowed imaging modalities) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The article is a clinicopathological case series (two autopsy cases) and does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not satisfied). The sample does not include clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD); Case 1 is semantic dementia (SD) and Case 2 is AD/DLB (I4 not satisfied). Sample size is far below the required minimum of 6 participants (I5 not satisfied). No group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in standardized space (MNI/Talairach) are reported (I6 and I7 not satisfied). The full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet multiple inclusion criteria.

The study uses region-of-interest volumetric MRI parcellation (striatum and thalamus) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and reports ROI volume comparisons rather than whole-brain, voxelwise results or standardized coordinates. Thus it does not meet imaging modality criterion (I3) nor whole-brain/voxelwise reporting (I6/I7). Additionally, analyses are ROI-only, so it falls under exclusion E3. The sample (21 FTD patients) meets minimum size but bvFTD diagnosis is not specifically stated. Full text is complete.

Although this VBM study includes patients meeting clinical criteria for the frontotemporal (frontal) variant of FTLD (7/10 ALS/FTLD patients) and uses whole-brain voxelwise VBM (meeting I3, I4, I5, and I7), all such patients are comorbid with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). The review’s exclusion criterion E4 disallows samples with concurrent other neurological disease. Because the target patient group is ALS patients with FTLD (not bvFTD patients without additional neurologic disease), the study does not provide clean bvFTD-only group data and thus must be excluded. Note: the provided full text describes whole-brain VBM results but does not include coordinate tables in the excerpt; however, exclusion is based on comorbidity (E4).

This is an empirical VBM study in FTD using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses reported (FWE-corrected and uncorrected results) and peak coordinates in Talairach space. The sample includes 62 clinically diagnosed FTD patients, with 48 characterized as behavioral-presentation (bvFTD), and 14 healthy controls (all >6). Whole-brain group-level contrasts and correlational analyses are reported and described in text/tables/figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies imaging modality, sample, sample size, coordinate reporting, and whole-brain evidence criteria.

This article is a narrative review/overview of MRI and MEG findings across the ALS–FTLD continuum rather than an original empirical study. It does not present original participant-level data or report between-group voxelwise contrasts with coordinates (MNI/Talairach) from a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria requiring primary data with whole-brain, voxelwise results (I3–I8, notably I4 and I6–I7). It violates exclusion criteria for being a review/non-empirical paper. Although it discusses bvFTD and relevant imaging modalities, it lacks the required empirical coordinate-based results for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This document is an ACR practice guideline/appropriateness criteria, not an original empirical study. It does not report new patient-level data, does not include a sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with group-level analyses, and provides no voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach coordinates. Although it discusses frontotemporal dementia broadly and reviews imaging modalities (including FDG-PET and MRI), it is non-empirical and summarizes evidence/recommendations rather than presenting VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET whole-brain statistical results required by the review. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3–I7 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (non-empirical paper).

This article is a narrative review discussing MRI, FDG-PET, fMRI, and other imaging techniques in dementia. It does not present original empirical data from a sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, nor does it report voxelwise whole-brain group results or coordinate tables from a VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET study. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria for being a non-empirical review/meta-analysis and lacks original data required for inclusion. No inclusion criteria (e.g., I4 clinical bvFTD sample, I3 empirical VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET analyses, I6/I7 voxelwise coordinate results) are satisfied.

Although this empirical study used FDG-PET (I3) and included 8 FTD patients (≥6; I5), it does NOT report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) nor does it provide coordinate tables or voxelwise contrasts. Key inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (between-group contrast coordinates and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results) are not satisfied. Additionally, the paper describes clinically diagnosed FTD but does not explicitly state behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) diagnosis (I4 unclear). Therefore it fails the necessary imaging/results criteria and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This study uses SPECT imaging rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET (fails I3). It reports region-based quadrant SPECT ratings and does not provide whole‑brain, voxelwise coordinate results in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6/I7). Thus it only provides region-of-interest style results rather than the required whole‑brain voxelwise analyses, meeting exclusion criterion E3. The sample size and clinical diagnosis of FTD (behavioural presentations) are adequate, but the imaging modality and absence of coordinate-based whole-brain results prevent inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bv-FTD patients (25 bv-FTD) and reports use of FDG-PET in 9 patients (satisfying I3, I4, I5), it does not present any between-group voxelwise analyses, coordinate results (MNI/Talairach), or group-level whole-brain statistical maps. FDG-PET findings are described qualitatively (frontotemporal hypometabolism) with no voxelwise contrasts, tables of coordinates, or whole-brain group results. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and I7/I8 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging and sample-specific inclusion criteria for the review. Although it uses structural MRI, analyses are ROI-based frontotemporal volumes (summed atlas regions) rather than voxelwise whole-brain VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET with reported stereotactic coordinates. The paper does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space. Additionally, the sample consists of genetic FTLD mutation carriers (some symptomatic, some presymptomatic), not explicitly a cohort of clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) patients as required. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article is a narrative review of biomarkers in FTLD rather than an empirical study reporting original VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET data in bvFTD. It does not provide primary participant-level imaging results, whole-brain voxelwise coordinates for a bvFTD sample, or new experimental data. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria for being a review/non-empirical paper and not eligible for inclusion.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=50) and uses VBM as one of the MRI methods, the full text reports classification sensitivities and misclassification rates rather than group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts expressed in a defined stereotactic space (e.g., MNI or Talairach). The main outcomes are classifier performance metrics, and no coordinates or voxelwise statistical maps/tables are provided in the presented text. Therefore it does not meet the requirement to report at least one between-group contrast in a defined stochastic space/whole-brain voxelwise result. Supplementary materials are not provided here and cannot be assumed to contain the necessary coordinate-based results.

Full text is incomplete (only references and metadata provided). The paper appears to be a narrative review on imaging in dementia and contains no original empirical data, meeting exclusion E5 (non-empirical paper) and likely E2 (review). No evidence that the study used VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met); no indication participants were clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4 not met); no sample sizes reported (I5 not met); no between-group whole-brain coordinate results in MNI/Talairach space are provided (I6, I7, I8 not met). Therefore the study does not meet the inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (MAPT group all presented with bvFTD; GRN group includes bvFTD cases) (I4); sample sizes meet the minimum (11 MAPT, 9 GRN, 15 controls) (I5); reports voxelwise between-group contrasts using SPM/DARTEL in standard space (MNI) (I6); presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the target patient groups (I7); results are reported as voxelwise maps/analyses (figures/tables) consistent with acceptable reporting formats (I8). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses VBM (satisfies imaging criterion), includes a SOC/EXEC subgroup consistent with behavioral-variant FTD, and has adequate sample sizes and whole-brain voxelwise analyses. However, the full text does not report results in a defined stereotactic space (no MNI or Talairach coordinates or coordinate tables are provided in the available text/figures), which fails inclusion criterion I6 requiring at least one between-group contrast reported in MNI/Talairach space. All other inclusion criteria checked (I3, I4, I5, I7) are met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded because I6 is not satisfied.

This full-text reports group-level voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing FTLD-U patients with and without PGRN mutations to controls and to each other. The cohort includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (majority: 6/8 in PGRN+), adequate group sizes (8 PGRN+, 8 PGRN−, matched controls), and whole-brain voxelwise results (VBM) reported and visualized with slice coordinates (e.g., y=30, y=−10, y=−45, −70) using SPM2 (standard MNI space). The paper provides group-level whole-brain contrasts and figures showing voxelwise differences between patient groups and controls, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not another modality only). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is a single-case report (one clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient) that includes FDG-PET imaging, but it does not meet critical inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. Specifically, the study has fewer than the required minimum sample size (I5), contains no between-group contrasts reported in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) (I6), and provides no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I7). The full text appears complete. Although I3 (FDG-PET) and I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD) are satisfied, failure to meet sample size and whole-brain/group-contrast criteria leads to exclusion.

This paper is a literature review of diagnostic options for frontotemporal dementia rather than an empirical imaging study. It does not report original data using VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET, does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD participant samples or sample sizes, and presents no between-group voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates. Therefore it fails all key inclusion criteria (I3–I7) and meets exclusion criteria for being a non-empirical review/meta-analysis. Full text appears complete for a review article.

This is a neuropathological case series of four patients (n=4) reporting individual MRI, PET and SPECT findings alongside detailed clinical/pathological data. Although FDG‑PET was used in two cases, the study does not present any group‑level VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET voxelwise analyses, reports no between‑group contrasts in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) space, and the sample size is well below the required ≥6 participants. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7) and provides no whole‑brain, group‑level coordinate results. Full text content appears complete.

This article is a narrative/review-style perspective on the use of FDG-PET to improve AD treatment and does not report original empirical data on clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients. It focuses on Alzheimer’s disease, discusses FDG-PET’s diagnostic role (including distinguishing FTD from AD), but provides no participant sample of bvFTD, no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables in MNI/Talairach space, and no methods/results of an empirical VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET study. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete for screening purposes (narrative content present).

This is a single-family case report of a compound heterozygous TREM2 mutation presenting as FTD-like syndrome. It does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) but reports clinical MRI and SPECT; it does not include a group of bvFTD patients (only one proband and family members), so sample size criterion (≥6) is not met; it provides no between-group voxelwise contrasts or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) and no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results. Therefore it fails multiple required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This manuscript is a narrative review on PET radiopharmaceuticals for brain aging and Alzheimer’s disease, not an original empirical study of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). It does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, nor does it present primary voxelwise VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET group-level whole-brain results in MNI/Talairach space. The paper is non-empirical (review), thus violating inclusion criteria requiring original empirical data and bvFTD samples. Therefore it must be excluded.

This is an empirical VBM study (SPM99) reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses with results normalized to Talairach space and peak coordinates reported. The sample includes 29 clinically diagnosed FTD patients, with a NON-APH subgroup (n=14) described as non-aphasic patients with social/behavioural and executive impairment consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). Group and subgroup sizes meet the minimum (≥6). The paper provides full methods, results (group-level whole-brain contrasts and coordinate tables/figures), and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness only, and comorbid psychiatric/other dementias were excluded by authors). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied.

The study recruits a heterogeneous FTLD group but does not specify inclusion of clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) cases nor report results specifically for a bvFTD subgroup. The review requires samples of clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4). Although the paper uses voxel-based whole-brain FDG-PET and morphometry (VBM) analyses and reports group-level voxelwise contrasts in MNI space, it does not meet the critical criterion of explicitly studying bvFTD. Therefore it must be excluded.

The study does not use any of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). It uses surface-based morphometry (cortical thickness and fractal dimension via CAT12), which does not meet inclusion criterion I3. Although the sample includes bvFTD patients (n=8) and group sizes exceed the minimum (I4 and I5 are met), the paper does not present results as coordinates in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) in the provided full text, so I6 may not be satisfied. The primary reason for exclusion is methodological: the imaging modality is outside the allowed set, falling under exclusion criterion E6 (studies reporting only cortical thickness/other non-allowed modalities). Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet the review inclusion criteria. It used structural ROI volumes derived from FreeSurfer (region-of-interest volumetry), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). The sample consists of mild Alzheimer’s disease (AD) patients from ADNI (no clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample; fails I4). The analysis reports associations of predefined ROIs rather than voxelwise, stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) whole-brain coordinates or voxel-based results (fails I6/I7). Therefore it effectively reports ROI-based results only, which matches exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete.

The study does not meet imaging-modality inclusion criterion I3. It uses O-15-water rCBF PET (H2(15)O) rather than FDG-PET, VBM, or fMRI, so it is outside the review’s eligible imaging modalities. The sample does include clinically defined FTD cases with behavioral features and sufficient overall sample size (22 affected individuals), but the imaging modality requirement is mandatory and not satisfied. The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion included).

This is a single-case clinical report (n=1) of left lobar frontotemporal degeneration describing preserved golf skills. It does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET)—only CT, SPECT, and structural MRI are reported. The sample size is below the required minimum (I5), and no between-group voxelwise contrasts or coordinates in MNI/Talairach space are reported (I6/I7). Therefore it fails multiple required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study uses VBM and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses on a large clinical cohort including an FTD group; imaging modality (VBM) and sample size criteria are satisfied. However, the manuscript reports FTD as a group diagnosed using Neary criteria but does not specify that patients are behavior-variant FTD (bvFTD) or provide subgroup analyses explicitly limited to bvFTD. The review requires clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants specifically (I4). Because the paper does not clearly identify the FTD subgroup as bvFTD, it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4; therefore it must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the imaging modality used is 99mTc-ECD SPECT, whereas the review requires VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. Although the paper includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (fvFTD), has adequate sample sizes, reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with MNI coordinates, and provides group-level contrasts, the core imaging modality criterion is not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This empirical VBM study includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) and reports voxelwise VBM results normalized to MNI space. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=12; controls n≥12). The paper describes whole-brain VBM comparisons (FTD group vs. controls) and group-level voxelwise contrasts with reported coordinates and figures; bvFTD-specific atrophy and voxelwise correlations with behavioral measures are presented (with small-volume correction within ROIs but based on SPM voxelwise analyses). Imaging modality (VBM) and coordinate reporting satisfy requirements. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided content is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a clinicopathologic case series of 6 FTD patients that does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). The study reports clinical evaluations, SPECT (not among required imaging modalities), polysomnography, neuropsychological testing, and autopsy pathology. It does not present voxelwise whole-brain analyses, between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space, or coordinate tables (fails I6 and I7). It does include clinically diagnosed FTD patients and has n=6 cases (satisfies I4 and I5), but because it lacks the required imaging modality and whole-brain, coordinate-based results, it does not meet all inclusion criteria and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This article is a narrative review of EEG/MEG/TMS measures in neurodegenerative diseases rather than an empirical neuroimaging study. It does not report original VBM, fMRI (resting or task), or FDG-PET data (I3 not met), nor does it include a sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with between-group voxelwise neuroimaging results reported in stereotactic space (I4, I6, I7 not met). The paper summarizes prior literature and methodology and thus constitutes a non-empirical review without primary coordinate-based whole-brain results. Therefore it meets the exclusion criterion for non-empirical papers (E5). Full text appears complete.

This is a single-case report (n=1) using FDG-PET in a clinically diagnosed FTD patient. Although FDG-PET (I3) and clinical FTD diagnosis (likely bvFTD phenotype) (I4) are present, the study fails critical inclusion criteria: sample size is below the minimum of 6 participants (I5 not met), no group-level between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met), and no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from the target sample (I7 not met). The full text appears complete. Therefore the paper must be excluded.

This is a small clinical case series (3 patients) and is excluded because it does not meet the imaging, sample-size, or whole-brain analysis requirements. Exclusion criterion applied: E3 (no whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (participants clinically diagnosed with frontotemporal dementia with behavioral presentations consistent with bvFTD). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET—uses CT/MRI/SPECT), I5 (sample size <6), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (no coordinates/tables of voxelwise whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (contains background, methods, cases, discussion). Therefore the study is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts normalized to MNI space. The sample includes 16 clinically diagnosed FTLD patients, 13 of whom are characterized clinically as frontotemporal dementia with prominent behavioural features (consistent with bvFTD), and 9 healthy controls (both groups >6 participants). Results include voxel coordinates and small-volume corrected findings and clearly report whole-brain VBM analyses for the target patient group. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analyses, non-VBM modalities, comorbid psychiatric samples) are met.

This article is a narrative review summarizing structural MRI and diffusion (DTI) findings across dementias rather than an original empirical study. It does not report original participant data, nor does it present primary VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET whole-brain voxelwise group results with coordinates from a bvFTD sample. Therefore it fails multiple inclusion requirements (no original bvFTD sample results, no voxelwise whole-brain contrasts reported) and meets exclusion criteria for reviews/non-empirical papers. Excluded under E2 and E5.

This is a single-case FDG-PET case report and literature review, not an empirical group study of bvFTD. It fails multiple required inclusion criteria: lacks clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (I4), has fewer than 6 participants (I5), and provides no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate data in a standard space (I6/I7/I8). Although the imaging modality (FDG-PET) meets I3, the absence of a qualifying sample and whole-brain, voxelwise group results means the study cannot contribute to the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (case report with introduction, case, discussion).

This study reports FDG-PET imaging (I3) in a clinically diagnosed frontal/behavioral variant FTD sample (bvFTD) (I4). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (142 patients overall; PET subgroup N=41 patients and N=16 healthy controls) satisfying I5. The analyses are voxelwise SPM2 whole-brain comparisons with reported Talairach coordinates and cluster results, meeting I6 and I7; whole-brain results are clearly presented in figures and text, satisfying I8. No exclusion criteria are violated: this is an original empirical PET study (not a review), includes whole-brain voxelwise results (not ROI-only), and excludes comorbid psychiatric/other dementias per methods. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core content is complete.

The study reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=15) (I4, I5). Whole-brain voxel-wise general linear models with permutation testing were used, and results are reported with maximum coordinates in MNI stereotaxic space (I6). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) results for the patient groups are presented (I7) and results are described in figures/tables (I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review only, ROI-only, non-empirical, unsupported imaging modalities, or disallowed comorbid samples) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

The study uses manual ROI-based volumetric MRI morphometry of the hippocampus and entorhinal cortex rather than VBM, fMRI (task or resting), or FDG-PET (I3 not met). It reports ROI volumes and sagittal profiles without any whole-brain, voxelwise analyses or stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI), so it provides no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (fails I6/I7) and is limited to ROI analyses only (exclusion E3). Although the FTD sample size (n=13) meets the minimum (I5), the paper does not specify behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) specifically and does not provide whole-brain coordinate results required for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused review: it used [18F]FDG PET (I3); included clinically diagnosed FTLD patients with 9 cases labeled as frontotemporal dementia (FTD) diagnosed per Neary criteria (i.e., behavioral variant FTD cases are included) (I4); sample sizes are 14 FTLD and 15 EOAD (≥6) (I5); reports voxelwise between-group SPM results with stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) in Table 2 (I6); results derive from whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses clearly attributed to the FTLD group (I7); coordinates and figures/tables present the whole-brain findings (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not solely seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness, empirical original data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical VBM study of a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient with whole-brain, voxelwise results reported as stereotactic coordinates. Methods describe optimized VBM and voxelwise t-statistics comparing the patient’s scans to 84 healthy controls; significant clusters and MNI-style coordinates are reported. The imaging modality (VBM) and bvFTD sample are explicit. The control group exceeds the minimum sample size (84 controls), satisfying the requirement that at least one group (patient or healthy) has ≥6 participants. Whole-brain voxelwise results are provided and clearly attributed to the target sample. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper is a clinical-pathologic case series describing an autosomal dominant subcortical gliosis kindred with frontotemporal dementia features. It does not use the required neuroimaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) — only structural MRI and CT were reported. The study does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in MNI/Talairach space or provide coordinate tables/figures suitable for meta-analysis. Although the sample includes multiple affected family members with FTD-like syndromes, the imaging and analysis methods do not meet inclusion criterion I3 and the paper provides no voxelwise, whole-brain contrasts (violating I6/I7). Therefore it cannot be included in a coordinate-based meta-analysis of bvFTD imaging studies.

While this study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes sufficient sample sizes (14 FTD, 31 AD; I5), it does not meet key inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. Participants are pathologically confirmed FTD cases, but the paper does not present a cohort explicitly of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) as required (I4). Many FTD cases had heterogeneous clinical presentations (including aphasic and other subtypes), and several were initially clinically diagnosed as AD. Additionally, although the authors used voxel-wise SSP statistical maps versus controls, the paper does not report whole-brain, group-level between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic coordinate space (MNI/Talairach) with coordinate tables as required (I6/I7). Therefore it fails I4, I6 and I7 and must be excluded.

Although the study used FDG-PET (I3) and included >6 FTD patients (n=17) satisfying sample size (I5), it does not clearly specify that the FTD subgroup are clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) (I4 not met). Crucially, the paper reports diagnostic accuracy metrics and case images but does not present any group-level whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast results with coordinates in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach), nor tables/figures of voxelwise results, so it fails to meet criteria I6 and I7. The study therefore provides no whole-brain voxelwise coordinate data required for inclusion; it effectively reports diagnostic classification and ROI/SSP-style analyses (E3). Full text appears complete. Exclusion based on absence of whole-brain voxelwise results (E3).

This is a case-series/genetic report of two p.A53T SNCA mutation carriers presenting with an FTD-like phenotype. Although both cases fulfilled criteria for possible behavioral-variant FTD (satisfying I4), the study does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (it reports structural MRI and DaTSCAN), so it fails I3. The sample size is far below the required minimum of 6 participants in a patient or healthy group (I5). The paper does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables (failing I6 and I7). Therefore it does not meet the required imaging modalities, sample size, or whole-brain coordinate-based results for inclusion.

This is an inter-societal consensus guideline/recommendation paper reviewing the literature and providing expert Delphi-based recommendations on FDG-PET use. It is not an original empirical study reporting primary voxelwise neuroimaging results or coordinate tables for clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients. It does not present group-level whole-brain (MNI/Talairach) between-group contrasts nor primary sample data meeting the requirement of at least 6 bvFTD participants. Therefore it fails the inclusion criteria and is a non-empirical paper, to be excluded.

This study used structural MRI hippocampal volumetry and a visual MTA rating scale (ROI-based measures) rather than Voxel-Based Morphometry, fMRI, or FDG-PET required by I3. It reports hippocampal (region-specific) volumetric and rating results rather than whole-brain, voxelwise coordinate-based results, so it does not provide the whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in a standard space required by I6/I7. Although the sample includes an FTD subgroup (n=17) meeting sample size I5, the imaging modality and lack of whole-brain voxelwise results violate inclusion criteria. Therefore the study is excluded under E3 (reports only ROI analyses/no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

The study does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET); it reports MRI and Tc99 ECD SPECT perfusion only and provides no whole-brain voxelwise results in a standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7. It does meet I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (sample size ≥6), and the full text appears complete.

This article is a narrative review of FDG PET in various dementias rather than an original empirical study. It does not report new patient-level data, does not include a sample of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD participants with group-level analyses, and provides no whole-brain voxelwise between-group coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I4–I7 and is a non-empirical paper, matching exclusion criterion E5.

This study does not meet the key clinical inclusion criterion (I4). Although it uses voxel-based morphometry (I3), reports whole-brain voxelwise group results in standard space (I6, I7), and has adequate group sizes (I5; FTLD n=55), the sample is defined by pathological diagnoses of FTLD subtypes rather than by a clinical diagnosis of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). The manuscript does not specify inclusion of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients or separate analyses of a bvFTD clinical group. Therefore it fails the requirement to include clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, so it cannot be included in the review.

Although this paper uses FDG-PET and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses versus controls, the patient sample consists of 3 individuals with IBMPFD who presented with semantic dementia (semantic variant PPA), not clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). The review’s critical inclusion criterion I4 (participants must be clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) is therefore not met. While the study satisfies I3 (FDG-PET), I5 (a healthy control group of 29 meets the sample size threshold), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (I7), it does not include bvFTD cases and thus cannot be included in a meta-analysis focused on bvFTD. Additionally, the patient group size (n=3) is below the required minimum for patient samples, meaning the primary target group would not meet I5 if that criterion is interpreted to require patients rather than controls. Full text appears complete.

This study uses automated regional volumetry (atlas-based tissue segmentation and FreeSurfer hippocampal volumes) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, so it does not meet imaging-modality inclusion criterion (I3). Although it includes patients with FTD, the subtype is not specified as behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) and the paper reports regional volume percentiles and diagnostic accuracies rather than whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6 and I7). The analyses are region-based (lobar/hippocampal volumes), not whole-brain voxelwise results, which matches exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only/no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Therefore I exclude the study.

Although this study uses VBM (I3), reports whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates (I6,I7,I8), and has adequate sample sizes (I5), it does not include behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) patients. The patient group is semantic dementia (SD), a distinct FTLD subtype, not bvFTD, so the key inclusion criterion I4 is not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded from a bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry and reports whole-brain, voxelwise results with coordinates, and the FTD patient group has 8 subjects (satisfying imaging modality, sample size, voxelwise reporting, and whole-brain results). However, the paper does not explicitly state that the FTD cases are the behavioral variant (bvFTD). The inclusion criterion I4 requires clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants; the provided full text only refers to ‘FTD’/’frontotemporal lobar degeneration of FTD type’ without specifying clinical subtype. Because the review objective targets bvFTD specifically, this ambiguity prevents confirming I4, so the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

Although the paper includes FDG-PET data and clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases (I3 and I4 satisfied), it fails to meet key inclusion requirements: the sample size is only 3 affected subjects (violates I5 requiring ≥6 participants), and it does not provide group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates in a defined stereotactic space (violates I6 and I7). Therefore it does not satisfy all inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

Although the study used VBM preprocessing and includes a substantial sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=55) and controls, it does not report any group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical contrast results in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or provide coordinate tables/voxelwise maps. Instead, the analysis extracted regional volumes from a priori-selected ROIs (Harvard-Oxford atlas) and performed classification based on those regional measures. Therefore the paper effectively reports ROI-based results without whole-brain voxelwise contrasts, violating inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and meeting exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete.

This is a narrative review/case-series article, not an empirical group neuroimaging study. It does not report VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET group-level voxelwise analyses in clinically diagnosed bvFTD with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. The paper summarizes clinical syndromes and individual cases, and therefore meets the exclusion criterion for non-empirical papers/reviews.

The study does not meet the imaging-modality inclusion criterion (I3). It uses structural MRI processed with FreeSurfer to report regional volumetric and cortical thickness ROI analyses rather than Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM), fMRI, or FDG-PET. The paper reports ROI- and region-based results (cortical thickness/volumes) rather than whole-brain voxelwise results in a standard stereotactic space (violating I6/I7), so it should be excluded. This also triggers exclusion criteria E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results) and E6 (reports cortical thickness methods which are explicitly excluded). Although an FTD group (n=22) is present, the imaging modality and analysis approach do not match the meta-analysis requirements for bvFTD VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET whole-brain voxelwise data.

The study uses VBM (I3), has adequate group sizes (I5), and reports whole-brain VBM results referenced to MNI space (I6). However it does NOT include a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) group (inclusion criterion I4). The ALS-FTD group in this paper is an ALS+FTD sample and is not explicitly described or diagnosed as bvFTD; therefore the key inclusion criterion for bvFTD samples is not met. Full text appears complete.

Although this study used FDG-PET with SPM (meets I3), reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts in MNI space with tables/figures (meets I6, I7, I8), and includes >=6 FTD patients (n=7) and controls (meets I5), it does NOT specify that the FTD sample comprises clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD). The inclusion criterion I4 requires that participants be clinically diagnosed bvFTD; the paper reports ‘FTD’ without specifying subtype or that diagnostic criteria for bvFTD were applied. Because I4 is not satisfied (and cannot be confirmed from the full text), the study must be excluded from a bvFTD-focused review. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed FTLD patients including a behavioral/social/executive (SOC/EXEC) subgroup equivalent to bvFTD. The study used whole-brain optimized voxel-based morphometry, reporting voxelwise between-group contrasts warped into Montreal Neurologic Institute space with tables/figures of significant clusters. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (40 patients total; imaging subgroup n=32; controls n=27). No exclusion criteria are violated (subjects with primary psychiatric disorders or other neurologic conditions were excluded). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, enabling assessment of whole-brain coordinates and group-level results.
