This is an empirical VBM study that includes 58 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (meets sample size requirement) and 44 controls. The study used voxel-based morphometry with SPM8/DARTEL and normalized images into MNI space, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise results surviving family-wise error correction (pFWE<0.05) with figures/tables of cluster results. It therefore satisfies imaging modality (VBM), inclusion of bvFTD patients, adequate sample size, reporting of voxelwise results in a standardized space, and whole-brain group-level voxelwise findings. Reporting of results in figures/tables and supplementary material meets the acceptable formats for whole-brain results.

Although this is an empirical imaging study with adequate sample sizes (FTD n=44, AD n=30, HC n=27), it does not meet the imaging and analytic inclusion criteria for the review. The study used structural MRI volumetry with lobar (ROI) volume measures processed via BRAINS2, not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). It reports lobar ROI analyses rather than voxelwise, whole-brain results in a standardized stereotactic space (no MNI/Talairach coordinates or voxelwise contrasts provided), so it fails I6 and I7. Therefore it qualifies for exclusion under E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study explicitly includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=44) and healthy controls (n=60), uses appropriate imaging modalities (structural MRI with VBM and resting-state fMRI), and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (VBM) and group-level functional connectivity results. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain VBM results and describes anatomical distributions of effects; whole-brain results are described in the text and figures/tables are indicated as part of the VBM analysis. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review only, ROI-only analyses, comorbid psychiatric/other-dementia samples) are met. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the review.

This study used structural MRI regional gray-matter volumetry with ROI-based analysis (SABRE) rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET, so it does not meet the imaging-modality inclusion criterion (I3). The sample comprises mixed FTLD subtypes (FTD, PNFA, SD, and mixed cases) and does not clearly or exclusively report clinically-diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients, so it fails the bvFTD-specific sample requirement (I4). Additionally, results are reported as ROI/regional volume correlations and group comparisons rather than voxelwise, stereotactic-coordinate whole-brain contrasts (violating I6/I7). This study therefore should be excluded. Applicable exclusion criterion: E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results).

The study does not meet key imaging and analysis inclusion criteria. It reports structural MRI findings (visual descriptions of atrophy and FLAIR signal changes) but does not use Voxel-Based Morphometry, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). It does not report voxelwise between-group contrasts in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (I6 and I7 not met). The clinical sample includes various FTD phenotypes and some cases with prominent behavioral features, but clinically-diagnosed bvFTD is not clearly specified for the imaging sample (I4 not confirmed). The cohort size meets the minimum participant threshold (≥6) (I5 met). Full text is complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports voxelwise, group-level results with MNI coordinates; included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients as part of the sample (47 bvFTD) (I4); sample sizes exceed the minimum (96 patients, 34 controls; bvFTD N=47) (I5); reports results in a defined stereotactic space with peak MNI coordinates (I6); and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise findings clearly attributed to the patient sample (I7/I8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not restricted to excluded modalities, and no disqualifying comorbid sample issues reported).

This is a narrative review/continuing-education article and does not report original empirical data. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (non-empirical paper/review without original data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no original VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET data reported as an empirical study), I4 (no clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient sample reported), I5 (no participant counts or groups meeting the ≥6 requirement), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from a target sample), I8 (no whole-brain results/coordinates in text/tables). Full text appears complete but contains synthesis of existing studies rather than original voxelwise imaging results, so it must be excluded.

Although the study uses FDG-PET and includes a substantial subgroup of behavioral-variant FTLD patients (35 behavioral variant cases) with adequate sample size, the analysis is ROI/parcellation-based (AAL 116 VOIs) and presents metabolic connectivity results as region-wise connections and matrices. The paper does not report voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach coordinates or provide coordinate tables/voxel-level statistical maps. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results and is excluded per E3 (ROI-only analyses). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study does not meet key imaging and reporting inclusion criteria. It used SPECT and visual MRI ratings rather than VBM, fMRI (resting or task), or FDG-PET (I3 not met). It does not report voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or provide coordinate tables (I6 and I7 not met). Although the sample included clinically diagnosed FTD patients (I4) and the sample size is ≥6 (I5), the primary imaging modality and the absence of coordinate-based, whole-brain voxelwise results preclude inclusion in the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present), so exclusion is based on failure to meet imaging/reporting inclusion criteria rather than missing information.

This is a single-case report (n=1) of FTD with concomitant ALS using FDG-PET and other imaging. Although FDG-PET was used (I3) and the patient was clinically diagnosed with FTD (I4), the study fails key inclusion requirements: it does not have at least 6 participants in patient or control groups (I5), reports no between-group contrasts or group-level whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach space (I6/I7), and therefore provides no qualifying whole-brain group-level data. Additionally, the sample includes concurrent neurological disease (ALS), violating the sample purity requirement (exclusion criterion E4). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical study of sleep and actigraphy in bvFTD patients (n=13) but does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET imaging. No whole-brain voxelwise neuroimaging analyses or between-group results reported in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinates. Although it meets clinical sample criteria for bvFTD (Neary criteria) and sample size (≥6), it fails the required imaging-modality and whole-brain result criteria (I3, I6, I7). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

The full text reports a multicenter 18F-FDG PET study that explicitly includes patients with the frontal variant of FTD (equivalent to behavioral-variant FTD), uses FDG-PET as the imaging modality, and reports voxelwise, whole-brain analyses normalized to the Talairach atlas. The FTD group (n=98) and control groups exceed the minimum sample-size threshold. Group-level, voxelwise comparisons and 3D-SSP maps are presented for FTD versus other groups, satisfying whole-brain result reporting. The study also excludes major psychiatric comorbidity and reports original empirical data. No exclusion criteria apply. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided; supplemental material availability is noted but not required. Thus all relevant inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met.

This is a clinical case series using conventional structural MRI and qualitative radiological descriptions in a genetically defined family with FTLD/PGRN mutation. It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3), and it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in standardized stereotactic space (fails I6 and I7). The paper presents no voxelwise coordinate tables or MNI/Talairach results and is not a neuroimaging group comparison study. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (no whole-brain results / not a voxelwise whole-brain neuroimaging analysis). Full text is complete.

Although the study used Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (I3) and had sufficient group sizes (I5) and reported VBM correlations (I6), it does not meet the review’s target-sample requirement. The patient sample included ‘frontotemporal dementia (FTD)’ patients but did not specify behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or provide a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (I4 not met). Moreover, the VBM analysis was performed across all diagnostic groups combined rather than reporting a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast specific to an FTD/bvFTD group (I7 not met). Therefore the study does not provide the required whole-brain results specific to the target sample (bvFTD) and must be excluded.

The study uses whole-brain, voxelwise longitudinal MRI morphometric analysis (SPM unified segmentation, DARTEL, and Jacobian determinant change maps multiplied by gray-matter maps), which is a voxel-based morphometry–type approach appropriate for I3. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (bvFTD n=37) satisfying I4, and group sizes exceed the minimum (I5). Between-group voxelwise contrasts (t-statistic maps) are reported and warped to MNI space, meeting I6, I7 and I8. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. It used FDG-PET as the imaging modality (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=13) alongside other groups and healthy controls (I4) with adequate sample sizes (≥6 per group) (I5). Imaging data were processed with SPM8 normalized to Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space and group-level two-sample voxelwise t-tests were performed comparing each diagnostic syndrome to controls, with family-wise error correction and cluster reporting, indicating between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (I6). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for diagnostic groups (including bvFTD) (I7). Results are presented in text/figures and refer to supplementary material/tables for clusters, which is acceptable (I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided content appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

Study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) for whole-brain grey matter analyses (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=7) (I4); group sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD n=7; HC n=40) (I5); analyses were performed in MNI standard space and results are reported with MNI coordinates (I6); the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts for phenotype groups including bvFTD versus controls (I7); whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and described in text (I8). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

Although the study used VBM (I3) and included clinically-diagnosed FTD syndromes including bvFTD (I4) with adequate sample sizes (I5), it does not report a whole‑brain, group-level voxelwise contrast (in MNI/Talairach space) specific to the bvFTD group. The VBM result reported is a correlation of vertical saccade velocity with dorsal midbrain volume across a mixed FTLD sample and subsequent voxelwise comparisons focus on PSP vs other groups at that peak — not a bvFTD whole‑brain between‑group contrast. Therefore key inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (between‑group contrast in stereotactic space and a whole‑brain result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD group) are not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article is a narrative review summarizing FDG PET findings across dementias rather than an original empirical study. It does not report an empirical sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, provides no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates, and does not present original data with sample sizes meeting the inclusion thresholds. Therefore it fails the required inclusion criteria (I4–I8) and fits exclusion criterion E5 (non-empirical review).

While this study uses FDG-PET and reports voxelwise, whole-brain group comparisons with adequate sample sizes (AD n=19, FTLD n=13, controls n=10), it does not specify that the FTLD patients are clinically diagnosed with the behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). The meta-analysis requires inclusion of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4). Because the FTLD sample is not explicitly described as bvFTD, I cannot confirm the required target diagnosis and thus the study does not meet all inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion) so exclusion is based on failure to satisfy I4 rather than incomplete reporting.

This study does not meet the review’s target sample criterion. While it uses VBM-based processing (satisfies I3) and includes sufficiently sized groups for AD, depression, and controls, it does not clearly include clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients: the paper only mentions a generic ‘frontotemporal dementia’ training class without specifying bvFTD or reporting bvFTD-specific participant characterization. Furthermore, the article presents machine-learning classification performance rather than group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts reported in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) for a bvFTD group; no coordinates or voxelwise group contrast results attributable to bvFTD are provided. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4, I6, and I7. Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet the imaging-modality inclusion criterion (I3). It used manual region-of-interest cortical volumetry (manual parcellation) rather than Voxel-Based Morphometry, fMRI, or FDG-PET. It also does not report whole-brain voxelwise stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinates or group-level voxelwise results, so it fails the whole-brain evidence/coordinate criteria (I6, I7). Therefore it should be excluded. The sample sizes are adequate, but the methodology is ROI-only. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study used manual ROI volumetry of the caudate nucleus on T1-weighted MRI rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and reports region-of-interest volumetric comparisons rather than whole-brain, voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates. Therefore it fails the imaging-modality requirement (I3) and the whole-brain/voxelwise coordinate requirements (I6,I7). It constitutes an ROI-only analysis with no whole-brain results, which matches exclusion criterion E3. Sample sizes meet the minimum (≥6). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This study reports voxel-wise SPM analysis of 18F-FDG PET (meets I3) in 29 clinically diagnosed FTD patients (excluded PPA and semantic dementia), with clinical features described that match behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) (meets I4). Sample sizes are adequate (29 patients, 11 controls) (meets I5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts and lists peak coordinates (MNI converted to Talairach) in Table 3 (meets I6, I7, I8). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, non-empirical work, disallowed modalities, or documented comorbid psychiatric/other-dementia samples) are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This is a retrospective neuropathological case series describing eight pathologically proven FTD patients who presented with severe amnesia. Although the sample size meets the minimum (8 patients), the study does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET); it reports structural MRI and HMPAO-SPECT only and provides no VBM or voxelwise group-level analyses in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) with coordinates. There are no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results reported, nor any between-group contrasts in defined stereotactic space. The sample is heterogeneous FTD (pathologically confirmed) and not explicitly a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) group. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I6 and I7 are not met; the study violates the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise imaging results (exclusion criterion E3 applies). Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (meets I3), it does not include clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) patients (it studies FTDP-17/PPND familial tauopathy rather than sporadic bvFTD), has only 5 affected patients (below the required >=6; violates I5), and does not report voxelwise, coordinate-based whole-brain results in MNI/Talairach space (violates I6/I7). The imaging results are qualitative/ROI-style (cerebellar ratios and region descriptions) without group-level whole-brain voxelwise coordinates, therefore failing the whole-brain evidence requirement (E3). Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on lack of key inclusion criteria (clinical population and sample size) and absence of whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results.

This is an empirical VBM study (structural MRI with voxel-based morphometry) that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=28) and healthy controls. Sample sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD n>6; total N=102). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise VBM results with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., x,y,z peak coordinates reported) and describes whole-brain analyses and thresholding procedures, satisfying the requirement for results in a defined stochastic space. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise findings are clearly reported (main effect analyses and follow-up analyses), and whole-brain results are presented in text, figures, and supplementary materials. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is a narrative review article summarizing social cognition and frontotemporal dementia, not an empirical neuroimaging study. It does not present original participant-level imaging data (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) with group contrasts, coordinate results in MNI/Talairach space, or sample sizes meeting the inclusion criteria. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3–I8. It meets the definition of a non-empirical paper (review) and thus should be excluded.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FD) patients (bvFTD-like) and adequate sample sizes (meets I4 and I5), it does NOT use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Instead it uses visual/manual MRI atrophy ratings. The paper does not report results in a stereotaxic coordinate space (MNI/Talairach) nor does it provide whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only region-based/ROI-style analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports a single-case (n=1) VBM analysis of a familial FTD (MAPT L266V) case. Although VBM was used (I3 satisfied), the study does not include a group of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample size: the patient group contains only one affected individual, failing the minimum-sample inclusion criterion (I5). It also does not clearly present a cohort of clinically-diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients (I4 not met as a target bvFTD group). While a two-sample t-test versus 12 controls was performed, this single-subject comparison does not fulfill the requirement for group-level whole-brain evidence from a target bvFTD sample (I7/I5). Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on failure to meet required inclusion criteria (insufficient patient sample and no bvFTD group).

This study does not meet the review inclusion criteria. It uses T1 structural MRI with information-theoretic structural complexity measures and FreeSurfer cortical thickness/volume estimates rather than one of the required modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), so I3 is not satisfied. The sample includes FTD patients (n=19) but the paper does not explicitly specify behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) as the diagnostic subgroup required by I4. Crucially, the reported analyses are region-based (13 predefined regions) and classification/LDA comparisons rather than voxelwise, whole-brain (stochastic-space coordinate) results; no MNI/Talairach coordinates or voxelwise group-level maps are reported, so I6 and I7 are not met. Therefore the paper must be excluded.

Full text appears incomplete — provided content is a references list and article metadata only, with no methods, results, or figures. Therefore I cannot verify any inclusion criteria. No evidence is present that the study used VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met); that it included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4 not met); that sample sizes meet the >=6 requirement (I5 not met); that stereotactic between-group coordinates (MNI/Talairach) are reported (I6 not met); or that at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result for the target sample is reported (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list can be confidently applied based on the incomplete text. Fulltext_incomplete=true takes precedence; additional assessment requires the complete article.

This study reports voxel-based 18F-FDG PET analyses in clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients (Lund-Manchester criteria), explicitly excluding semantic dementia and progressive aphasia variants, implying behavioral-variant FTD. Imaging modality is FDG-PET with voxelwise, whole-brain group comparisons and voxel-based regression; results are reported with Talairach/MNI coordinates. Sample size (29 patients, 16 controls) exceeds the minimum of 6. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a single-case clinical and neuropathologic report (n=1) describing an autopsy-verified mixed PSP/AGD/AD in a patient clinically diagnosed with frontotemporal dementia. It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met), reports no group-level analyses or whole-brain voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates (I6 and I7 not met), and the sample size is below the required threshold (I5 not met). Although the patient had clinical FTD features consistent with the behavioral variant (I4 met), failing any required imaging/modality, group, and reporting criteria means the study must be excluded.

Although this study used VBM (I3) and included a clinically defined social/dysexecutive (SOC/EXEC) subgroup consistent with bvFTD (I4) with sufficient sample size (SOC/EXEC n=17; I5), it does not provide group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables. The VBM processing produced subject-level thresholded T-maps which were intersected with predefined Brodmann Area ROIs to derive ROI-based atrophy measures and subsequent seriation and regression analyses. Because the paper reports ROI-based/atlas intersection results and individual subject VBM maps rather than clear group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts or coordinate tables, it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only/no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is a clinical natural-history cohort study of primary progressive aphasia (PPA) without neuroimaging analyses of the types required by the review. It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I3 not met). The sample comprises patients with PPA (language-predominant presentation), not clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) (I4 not met). No between-group voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) are reported (I6/I7 not met). Therefore the study does not provide the imaging data or target population required for inclusion. Full text appears complete and provides clinical methods and outcomes but no qualifying neuroimaging results.

This study reports whole-brain FDG-PET (SPM) analyses with voxel-wise results and provides coordinates (Talairach/MNI) in a supplement. Imaging modality is FDG-PET (meets I3). The sample comprises clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients using consensus criteria, with most patients presenting behavioral symptoms consistent with bvFTD (meets I4). Sample sizes meet the threshold (29 FTD, 8 FTD/MND; meets I5). The paper reports between-group voxel-wise contrasts in standard space and whole-brain group-level results (meets I6 and I7), with coordinates/tables in supplements (meets I8). No exclusion criteria are clearly violated (study is empirical, not ROI-only, not a review). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is sufficiently complete for screening.

This study does not meet the review inclusion criteria for bvFTD whole-brain voxelwise FDG-PET studies. Although it uses FDG-PET (satisfying I3), the frontotemporal dementia (FTD) group is small (n=4), below the required minimum of 6 participants (violates I5), and the paper does not specify that these are behavioral-variant FTD cases (I4 not satisfied). The analysis is ROI/template-based (BRASS VOIs) and discriminant analysis rather than a whole-brain voxelwise contrast with stereotactic coordinates; no MNI/Talairach coordinates or voxelwise group-level results are reported (violates I6/I7 and meets exclusion E3). Full text appears complete.

This article is a narrative review intended as a practical guide for radiologists, not an empirical study. It lacks original participant data, no methods or results reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses, no voxel coordinates in MNI/Talairach space, and does not present an independent sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD with between-group contrasts. Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET studies with bvFTD samples and whole-brain results).

While the study meets some methodology criteria (uses FDG-PET and has sufficient group sizes), it does not meet key inclusion requirements for this review. The sample is described as frontotemporal dementia (FTD) but the paper does not specify behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD), so I4 is not satisfied. The study focuses on voxel-based classification and presents discriminative/ratio images, but it does not report between-group voxelwise contrasts with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space or clearly identified group-level whole-brain coordinate tables/figures for the target bvFTD sample (I6 and I7 not satisfied). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study uses FDG-PET (I3) and performs whole-brain SPM voxelwise analyses with group comparisons versus controls and correlations (whole-brain results clearly reported) satisfying voxelwise, group-level results (I7). The sample includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patients (behavioral variant FTD is the FTD subgroup used) meeting the bvFTD target (I4). Sample sizes meet the minimum (17 patients, 9 controls) so at least one group ≥6 (I5). The paper reports between-group contrasts using standard stereotactic SPM procedures and refers to tables/figures of results (coordinates/results in defined stochastic space are presented in the SPM-based analysis), satisfying I6 and I8. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria are met.

Although the paper uses voxel-wise MRI analyses (SPM12) producing whole-brain atrophy maps (VBM-style) and reports group-level voxelwise coordinates in ICBM/MNI space, it does not report a sample of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients. The cohort comprises familial FTLD mutation carriers (MAPT, GRN, C9orf72) across asymptomatic, mildly/questionably symptomatic, and overtly symptomatic stages with heterogeneous clinical presentations; the manuscript does not state that participants were clinically diagnosed as bvFTD nor isolates a bvFTD patient group for between-group contrasts. The meta-analysis requires studies with clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), so this key inclusion criterion is not met despite satisfying imaging and reporting criteria.

The study does not meet key imaging and analysis inclusion criteria for the review. It uses visual/radiological ratings of structural MRI (qualitative assessment) rather than VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). It does not report voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables/figures (I6/I7 not met). Although the paper includes a pathologically confirmed FTLD group (n=17) and adequate sample sizes (so I5 is met), it does not clearly report clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD as the designated sample (clinical subtypes include “frontal lobe dementia,” which may overlap but is not explicitly labeled as bvFTD per inclusion I4). The full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to satisfy the required imaging modality and whole-brain coordinate reporting criteria.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (n=21) and uses PET/SPECT, the imaging data are reported as regional ratings and qualitative/inter-rater scores rather than voxelwise, whole-brain statistical contrasts in a standardized space. The paper does not present VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET voxelwise results with coordinates (MNI/Talairach), nor any group-level whole-brain coordinate tables/figures. Therefore it fails the required imaging/analysis inclusion criteria (voxelwise whole-brain results in standard space) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only region-based/ROI-style reporting with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is a narrative review article (metadata labels it a "Review article") and does not present original empirical data. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (non-empirical paper). Although the review discusses imaging modalities (including FDG-PET) and frontotemporal lobar degeneration, it does not report an original bvFTD participant sample, sample sizes, voxel-wise whole-brain between-group contrasts, or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no primary VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET empirical data reported), I4 (no clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample with participant data), I5 (no reported group sizes ≥6 for an original study), I6 (no between-group coordinate results in MNI/Talairach), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (not applicable). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the article must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a single-center retrospective diagnostic study that includes FDG-PET and reports 10 FTD patients, but it does not report any whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group neuroimaging contrasts or provide results in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables. The study focuses on diagnostic accuracy, confidence, and inter-rater agreement rather than VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET voxelwise group analyses. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts or stereotactic coordinates) and does not clearly specify behavioral-variant FTD as the target subgroup. Although imaging modality (FDG-PET) and sample size criteria are met, the absence of whole-brain voxelwise results precludes inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a genetic and neuropathologic study of a progranulin (GRN) frameshift mutation in a family with frontotemporal dementia. It does not use the imaging modalities required by the review (no VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET); instead methods are DNA sequencing, real-time PCR, fibroblast mRNA analysis, and neuropathology. The sample is described as FTD cases with variable clinical presentations (including primary progressive aphasia and memory disturbances) but is not specified as clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). There are no between-group, whole-brain voxelwise imaging results reported in MNI or Talairach space. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I3, I4, I6, and I7 and is excluded.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (meets I3) and has adequate sample size (43 FTD patients, meets I5), it does not specifically report clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) — patients are described only as FTD, so I4 is not satisfied. The paper is a machine-learning classification study using AAL anatomical VOIs and selected ROI-based features rather than reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). No tables or coordinates of voxelwise between-group results are provided, and the analyses focus on ROI/feature selection and classification metrics rather than whole-brain statistical maps. Therefore criteria I6 and I7 are not met and exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete.

This is a single-case clinical report (n=1) describing a patient with Niemann–Pick disease and Paget’s disease with fronto-temporal dementia. While FDG-PET was used (I3 satisfied), the paper does not specifically report clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) (I4 not clearly met), includes only one patient (fails I5: needs ≥6 participants), and provides no group-level between-group contrasts or whole-brain voxelwise results in standardized (MNI/Talairach) space (I6/I7 not met). Therefore it does not meet multiple essential inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete.

Although this study used FDG-PET (I3) and included an adequate FTD sample (n=18, satisfying I5), it does not meet key inclusion requirements for the review. The FTD group is reported generically as “FTD” with no specification that patients had the behavioral variant (bvFTD), so I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD) is not satisfied. In addition, the paper does not report whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or provide coordinate tables/voxelwise results (I6/I7); instead it presents 3D-SSP z-score maps and diagnostic performance metrics. Because it lacks bvFTD-specific clinical diagnosis and does not provide voxelwise whole-brain coordinate results required for the meta-analysis, the study must be excluded.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=25), uses VBM, reports MNI coordinates, and has adequate sample sizes, the neuroimaging analyses were performed using an a priori ROI mask (motor-system ROIs) rather than whole-brain, voxelwise analyses. The paper therefore reports only ROI-constrained voxelwise results and does not provide group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for the target sample, which violates inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical FDG-PET study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=6 in template creation; n=24 in the validation sample), meets the minimum sample-size requirement, uses voxelwise SPM analyses in MNI space, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results for the bvFTD group. The paper provides methods, results, and discussion sufficient for inclusion and meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study presents CycleGAN synthesis of 11C-PiB amyloid PET images and does not investigate behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). It does not use the required imaging modalities (FDG-PET, VBM, or fMRI)—it uses amyloid PET (11C-PiB). The sample does not consist of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, and although the total sample size exceeds 6, no between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space are reported. The paper is methodological/validation for image synthesis rather than a voxelwise group comparison study. Therefore it fails multiple required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I6, I7) and must be excluded.

This study used VBM and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=17) and reported whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons (4 delusion vs 13 non-delusion). However, the full text as provided does not report results in a defined stereotactic space (no MNI or Talairach coordinates or explicit stereotactic coordinates are given in the text provided). Inclusion criterion I6 requires at least one between-group contrast reported in MNI/Talairach space. Because that specific requirement is not demonstrably met in the provided full text, the study cannot be included for the meta-analysis despite meeting other imaging and sample criteria.

This retrospective memory-clinic case series does not meet the imaging and analytic requirements for the review. It used clinical CT (and MRI in selected patients) rather than VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). Although a small number of frontotemporal dementia (FTD) cases are reported (1.8%, ~7 patients), the paper does not specify clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or apply bvFTD diagnostic criteria (fails I4). There are no voxelwise, whole-brain statistical imaging results reported in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach), nor are there coordinate tables or group-level voxelwise contrasts (fails I6 and I7). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded for not satisfying multiple required inclusion criteria.

While the study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons aligned to MNI152 and has adequate group sizes (>6), it does not explicitly include clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) patients. The patient groups are ALS, FTD-ALS (FTD with ALS comorbidity), PNFA, and controls; FTD-ALS is described as exhibiting behavioral and cognitive dysfunction but is not explicitly defined or diagnosed as bvFTD. The meta-analysis requires explicit inclusion of clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4). Because I4 is not met, the study must be excluded despite meeting imaging- and reporting-related criteria.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (meets I3), reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses in MNI space (meets I6, I7, I8), and has adequate group sizes (ALS-FTD n=17, controls n=18; meets I5). However, the patient sample comprises ALS-FTD (patients with both ALS and FTD) rather than a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) cohort. The paper does not clearly report inclusion of standalone bvFTD patients meeting bvFTD diagnostic criteria, so it fails inclusion criterion I4 required for this bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. Therefore it does not meet all required inclusion criteria and should be excluded.

This text is a methods/review-style book chapter on 18F-FDG PET use in dementia (including Alzheimer’s and other dementias) and does not report original empirical data on behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). It contains no participant sample, no clinical bvFTD group, no sample sizes, no between-group statistical contrasts, and no reported voxelwise coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. It is therefore non-empirical and does not meet the required inclusion criteria (I4–I7). Primary exclusion applies because this is a non-empirical/methods/review chapter rather than an original study with data.

The study is excluded because it does not include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample and does not report whole-brain voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) results. Although FDG-PET was used (I3) and the overall patient sample size is ≥6 (I5), the FTLD subgroup is small (n=4) and not specified as behavioral variant FTD (I4 not met). Analyses are VOI-based and visual 3D-SSP assessments rather than whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results, so it effectively reports ROI/VOI/visual analyses without qualifying whole-brain coordinate-based contrasts (E3). Full text appears complete.

This study reports voxel-wise, whole-brain analyses using RAVENS maps (a VBM-style, stereotactic voxel-based approach) and high-dimensional pattern classification. The FTD group includes 12 patients, of whom 8 presented with behavioral/executive-onset symptoms (bvFTD), satisfying inclusion of bvFTD cases. Voxelwise effect-size maps comparing CN vs FTD and FTD vs AD are reported and described (figures and text), and analyses were performed in stereotactic (common) space. Sample sizes meet the >=6 threshold. Although coordinate tables (MNI/Talairach labels) are not explicitly shown in the provided text, whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotactic space are clearly reported and illustrated, meeting the requirement for whole-brain, between-group contrasts.

This is a single-case report of a patient with ‘probable frontotemporal dementia’ (n=1) rather than a sample of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients. Although FDG-PET was used (I3) and there are >=6 healthy controls (I5), the study does not report any group-level between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach), nor does it provide whole-brain, voxelwise group results or coordinates. Key inclusion criteria I4, I6 and I7 are therefore not met. The full text appears complete. Consequently the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on group-level imaging in bvFTD.

The study is an empirical clinical series of 32 FTLD patients reporting clinical features of stereotypies and qualitative/region-based functional imaging (SPECT/PET) but does not use VBM, task or resting‑state fMRI, or explicitly FDG‑PET voxelwise analysis. It does not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or between-group contrasts. Therefore it fails multiple inclusion criteria (I3, I6, I7) required for the review. The full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses and DTI, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=39) and controls (n=61), and provides whole-brain, voxelwise results reported in MNI space (figures/tables described). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). VBM results and coordinates/overlays on the MNI standard brain are reported, satisfying whole-brain group-level reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, non-empirical, or disallowed modalities) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a clinicopathologic case series of a familial PGRN mutation. It does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review: imaging modality I3 (no VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; only conventional MRI images are reported, without voxel-based analyses), sample I4 (subjects are not a group of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; most presented with amnestic AD-like or mixed phenotypes, only a minority had FTD features), and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements I6/I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space or coordinate tables). Full text appears complete (contains methods, results, discussion, neuropathology). Exclusion criterion applied: E4 (sample includes other forms of dementia/mixed pathology rather than a clean bvFTD sample).

Although the study uses 18F-FDG PET (satisfying I3), it does not meet key inclusion criteria for this review. The study reports a heterogeneous clinical sample including 5 patients with frontotemporal dementia (FTD), but does not specify behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) (I4 not met). The FTD subgroup size is n=5 (<6), so the minimum sample-size criterion is not satisfied for the target group (I5 not met). The paper reports visual/region-based PET findings and group counts but provides no voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts or coordinate results in MNI/Talairach space (I6 and I7 not met). Thus it lacks the required group-level whole-brain voxelwise results. This study should be excluded for failing multiple required inclusion criteria.

Modality and analysis mismatch with inclusion criteria. This study uses manual volumetric MRI (region-of-interest lobar and hippocampal tracings) rather than Voxel-Based Morphometry, fMRI, or FDG‑PET (I3 not met). Results are ROI-based volumetric measures and asymmetry ratios rather than whole‑brain voxelwise (E3 applies). Sample size is adequate (10 FTD patients; I5 met), and it includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (not explicitly labeled bvFTD), but the primary exclusion is methodological (ROI-only MRI). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from the review focused on VBM/fMRI/FDG‑PET whole‑brain studies of bvFTD.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (threshold p<0.001 uncorrected, cluster>200 voxels). The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) patients (84 bvFTD out of 118 total), and group sizes exceed the minimum of 6 participants. Results are reported in standard stereotactic space (MNI coordinates are provided). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria are violated (the study explicitly excluded participants with major psychiatric disorders, other dementias, substance abuse, and performed whole-brain analyses rather than ROI-only or methods not allowed). Therefore it should be included.

This is a structural MRI study measuring anterior commissure and substantia innominata thickness/area (manual ROI measurements), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, so it does not meet the imaging-modality inclusion criterion (I3). The paper reports only region-of-interest measures and no whole-brain voxelwise/coordinate-based results in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6/I7), and thus meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only with no whole-brain results). The sample size is adequate (FTLD n=7, AD n=20, controls n=16), satisfying I5, but the modality and whole-brain reporting requirements are not met, so the study must be excluded.

This is a single-case autopsy report using SPECT and MRI, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. It does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, has only one subject (fails sample size ≥6), and reports no whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails multiple required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and reports whole-brain VBM group contrasts (I6–I8), the bvFTD clinical subgroup only contains 3 participants (bvFTD n=3). This is below the required minimum of 6 participants for the target patient group (fails I5). Therefore the study does not meet the sample-size inclusion criterion for inclusion in a bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

This study does not address the review objective of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). Although it uses FDG-PET (satisfying imaging modality I3), the sample comprises probable Alzheimer’s disease, amnestic MCI, and healthy controls — it does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4 not met). Additionally, the paper reports visual and semi-quantitative (SUVr / 3D-SSP) analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach); therefore it does not meet I6/I7. The full text is complete. Based on these deficiencies, the study must be excluded.

This is a nationwide clinical/registry study of FTD that includes a substantial bvFTD sample (n=78) and reports clinical, neuropsychological, and behavioral results. However, although FDG-PET was used in some patients for diagnostic purposes, the paper does not report any voxelwise, whole-brain neuroimaging analyses (VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET) nor any between-group contrasts in stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Therefore it fails key imaging-related inclusion criteria (I3, I6, I7). The study does not present ROI-only or coordinate tables of whole-brain results either. Because no group-level whole-brain voxelwise imaging results are reported, it does not qualify for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is a single-case longitudinal clinical and neuropathological report of a patient with TBK1-associated FTD. It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (it reports volumetric MRI and manual/automated regional segmentation), includes only one patient (fails the minimum sample size requirement), and does not report any group-level between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard (MNI/Talairach) space or whole-brain group-level voxelwise results. Therefore it does not meet key inclusion criteria (I3, I5, I6, I7) and reports no qualifying whole-brain group results (exclusion: E3).

This study does not meet key imaging and analysis inclusion criteria. It uses structural MRI lobar volumetry (region-based Talairach lobar volumes derived via BRAINS2) rather than Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM), task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). Results are reported as lobar ROI volumes and correlations (no voxelwise, stereotactic-coordinate (MNI/Talairach) whole-brain between-group contrasts are provided), so it does not satisfy I6 or I7 and is effectively an ROI-based volumetric analysis (meets exclusion E3). Sample size is sufficient (28 patients, 16 controls; satisfies I5), and FTD subtype patients are included, but the lack of voxelwise whole-brain imaging results and non-VBM/functional/metabolic modality means the study cannot be included in this meta-analysis. Full text appears complete.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports voxelwise whole-brain results with MNI coordinates. The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (Neary criteria), representing behavioral/dysexecutive variant FTLD, with n=14 FTD (>6). VBM analyses report group-level voxelwise correlations (with MNI coordinates) and whole-brain/region-masked results clearly attributed to the patient groups. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the imaging modality, patient sample, sample size, and reporting requirements for inclusion.

While the paper uses FDG-PET and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=10), it does not report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical results identified as coming from the bvFTD target group. The study's SPM analyses were performed at the single-subject level (each subject vs. control group) for diagnostic classification and rater evaluation; results are presented as single-subject SPM maps and summary detection rates rather than group-level voxelwise contrasts or coordinate tables for the bvFTD group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 (requirement for at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result for the target sample). Full text appears complete.

Although this study used FDG-PET (and also FBB amyloid-PET) in a clinical cohort and included patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD), it does not meet key inclusion requirements for the bvFTD meta-analysis. The paper does not specify that clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) patients were included, reporting FTLD and PPA subtypes but not clearly identifying bvFTD as a target group (I4 not satisfied). Critically, the study does not report between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) with coordinate tables or whole-brain voxelwise group-level results — it relies on visual reads/3D-SSP and case illustrations rather than voxelwise coordinate-based analyses (I6/I7 not satisfied). Therefore it must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

The study uses surface-based cortical thickness analyses (FreeSurfer) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. Inclusion criterion I3 requires VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; exclusion criterion E6 disallows studies that only report cortical thickness methods. Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (bvFTD subgroup present) and sample sizes meet minimums, the imaging modality does not meet the required techniques and therefore the study is not eligible for inclusion.

Although this study includes behavioral-variant FTLD patients (9 bvFTD cases) and uses whole-brain gray-matter segmentation for automated classification (SVM), it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast results in stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). The paper focuses on classification accuracy of an SVM versus radiologists rather than presenting voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables for the bvFTD group. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 (between-group contrast in defined stereotactic space) and I7 (reporting at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the required imaging and analysis criteria for the bvFTD meta-analysis. The study uses structural T1-weighted and FLAIR MRI with region-wise segmentation/grading and CSF measures (ROI-based features), not VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). The patient sample includes FTLD broadly (92 FTLD patients) but does not specify clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) (fails I4). The analyses are region-of-interest/feature-based rather than whole-brain voxelwise contrasts reported as stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinates; no voxelwise group-level coordinate tables or voxelwise between-group contrasts are provided (fails I6 and I7). Although sample sizes meet the minimum (I5), the absence of required modality and whole-brain voxelwise results mandates exclusion. Full text appears complete.

This study uses structural MRI with ROI-based regional gray matter density measures (91 ROIs) derived from SPM segmentation and atlas parcellation rather than voxel-based morphometry (VBM) or voxelwise analyses. The paper reports group differences at the ROI level (t-statistics per ROI) and does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it does not meet imaging-modality criterion I3 (VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET) as implemented here, nor the requirements for whole-brain voxelwise results (I6, I7). It therefore falls under exclusion criterion E3 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

Although this study includes clinically-diagnosed behavioral variant FTLD patients (9 bvFTD cases within the FTLD group), uses voxelwise structural MRI processing consistent with VBM, reports whole-brain, voxelwise SVM weight maps, and has adequate sample size, it does not report between-group contrast results in a standardized stereotaxic coordinate space (MNI/Talairach). The paper presents voxel importance maps/figures but does not provide group-level contrast coordinates or conventional stereotactic coordinate tables required by inclusion criterion I6. Therefore it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I6) for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is an SPECT rCBF study using a multiblock ROI-based discriminant analysis (MUBADA). Although it includes clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients (N=33) and adequate sample sizes, it does not use one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) and reports results at the ROI level (28 a-priori ROIs) rather than reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails modality criterion (I3) and whole-brain/voxelwise reporting criteria (I6, I7) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=54) and adequate sample sizes, it does not use any of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET). The neuroimaging methods are FreeSurfer-based cortical thickness and subcortical volume analyses (surface-based morphometry/ROI and longitudinal volume measures), not voxel-based whole-brain VBM or functional/PET analyses. The paper reports ROI/region-wise thickness and volume correlations rather than voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it violates the imaging-modality inclusion criterion and meets exclusion criteria for reporting only cortical thickness/ROI-style analyses without whole-brain voxelwise coordinates.

Excluded because the study reports VOI/ROI-based analyses and visual/region-based logistic regression without presenting any whole-brain voxelwise group-level results in stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses 18F-FDG PET) and I5 (FTD patient group n=7, ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (paper reports 'FTD' but does not explicitly specify behavioral-variant FTD/bvFTD), I6 and I7 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts or coordinate tables/voxelwise whole-brain results are reported). Exclusion criterion E3 applies (only ROI/VOI analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded for this review.

This article is a narrative/systematic evidence review and Delphi-consensus guideline on the clinical utility of FDG-PET, not an original empirical study. It does not report primary group-level voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) results from a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample, nor does it provide coordinate tables or whole-brain group contrasts for bvFTD. The paper explicitly summarizes evidence across multiple dementia syndromes (FTLD in general) and issues recommendations, but contains no new empirical bvFTD imaging data meeting the inclusion requirements (I4–I8). Therefore it meets exclusion criteria for being a review/non-empirical paper.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (I3) and has adequate sample size (≥6; I5), it does NOT meet key inclusion requirements. Participants are pathologically confirmed FTLD cases but are not reported as clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD), so I4 is not satisfied. The paper reports region-based (predefined regions) assessments and rater judgements rather than whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with coordinates in a standard space (MNI/Talairach); thus I6 and I7 are not met. This constitutes an ROI/region-only analytic approach, triggering exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from the coordinate-based, whole-brain meta-analysis targeting clinically diagnosed bvFTD.

The study is an empirical rs-fMRI investigation that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=21) and healthy controls. It uses resting-state fMRI and VBM methods, performs whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group ICA and dual regression) with permutation testing in MNI space, and reports significant between-group voxelwise results (e.g., decreased FC in salience network/insula). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (34 bvFTD cases) within the sample (I4); group sizes exceed the minimum (I5); reports voxelwise results with coordinates in standard MNI space (I6); provides group-level, voxelwise VBM analyses (full-factorial model and statistical parametric maps) that derive from the patient cohort that includes bvFTD (I7); and whole-brain voxelwise results and coordinates are reported and described in the text and figures/tables (I8). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

The manuscript reports an empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) and healthy controls, using high-resolution T1 MRI with gray-matter probability mapping and voxelwise permutation-based analyses registered to MNI space. The paper presents whole-brain, group-level VBM-style contrasts (patients vs. controls) and voxelwise regressions relating behavior to GM density, with results reported in text/figures (and supplementary materials). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analysis, only connectivity/DTI/thickness methods, or comorbid confounds) apply. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied.

The article is a narrative review of clinicopathologic patterns and imaging of tauopathies and does not present original empirical neuroimaging data. It does not report primary VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET group analyses with clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, nor does it provide whole-brain, voxelwise between-group coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria for being a review/non-empirical paper and not an original study. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods discussion), so exclusion is based on study type and lack of primary voxelwise results relevant to bvFTD.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (Methods: SPM2 VBM analyses) (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (16 bvFTD of 26 FTLD patients) (I4) and sample sizes exceed the minimum (26 patients, 21 controls) (I5). The paper reports voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain results (statistical parametric maps assessed at p<0.05 FDR corrected over the whole brain) and local maxima summarised in tables, consistent with reporting coordinates in a defined stereotactic space (SPM framework implies MNI/Talairach coordinates) (I6, I7). Whole-brain results are presented in text, figures and tables (I8). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review only, ROI-only analyses, disallowed imaging modalities, comorbid samples) are violated. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and supplementary material is noted but not required. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Although this study meets several inclusion criteria (uses VBM [I3], includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients [I4] with N=23 [I5]), it does not report a between-group contrast or whole-brain voxelwise results specific to the bvFTD group or a bvFTD vs. control comparison. The VBM analysis presented is a voxelwise correlation across a heterogeneous sample of 75 neurodegenerative patients (diagnosis entered as covariates), yielding group-level correlates for the combined patient cohort rather than results attributable specifically to the bvFTD group. Inclusion criteria I6 (reporting at least one between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space) and I7 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from the target sample group) are not satisfied. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from the review.

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=16) and uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with reported voxelwise results. Sample sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD n=16; controls n=19). The paper reports group-level neuroanatomical associations with interoceptive accuracy including whole-brain corrected maxima given in MNI coordinates (e.g., right amygdala [18 −15 −21]), and additional coordinates within pre-specified ROIs; maps and coordinates are clearly reported. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, ethics) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only paper, ROI-only without whole-brain results, disallowed imaging modality, or disqualifying comorbid sample) were triggered. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (6 bvFTD) and uses FDG-PET (satisfying I3, I4, I5). However, all PET analyses are ROI-based (standardised ROIs, visual PIB reads, ROI-normalised CMRglu) and statistical comparisons are performed on ROI values; no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts in stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables/figures are reported. Therefore it does not meet I6/I7 and is excluded under E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper is a narrative review summarizing neuroimaging findings across dementias rather than an original empirical study. It does not report original group-level whole-brain VBM, resting-state or task fMRI, or FDG-PET analyses on a clinical bvFTD sample with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space, nor does it present primary data with sample sizes meeting inclusion criteria. Therefore it fails the requirement for original empirical data and subject-level/group whole-brain results. The article is non-empirical and synthesizes others’ findings, so it should be excluded.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI), satisfying imaging and reporting requirements. Sample sizes meet the threshold (33 patients, 12 controls). Although the cohort includes heterogeneous FTD phenotypes, the text indicates GRN mutation carriers present with behavioral-variant FTD among other presentations, implying clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients are included. Whole-brain group-level results are reported and clearly attributed to the patient groups. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the full text is complete and the study uses VBM, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=45), reports whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates (voxelwise correlations between CSF NfL and gray/white matter volume), and meets other imaging/sample criteria, it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., bvFTD vs. controls) in stereotactic space. Inclusion criterion I6 specifically requires at least one between-group contrast reported in defined stochastic space, which is not satisfied. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study reports an empirical VBM (voxel‑based morphometry) analysis and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=10). Sample sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD n=10; healthy controls n=19). The paper presents voxelwise group‑level neuroanatomical results for bvFTD (statistical parametric maps and regional local maxima reported with MNI coordinates) and discusses VBM findings; whole‑brain voxelwise maps are shown (thresholded for display) and peak coordinates were significant after correction within prespecified ROIs. Thus it satisfies imaging modality (I3), inclusion of bvFTD patients (I4), adequate sample size (I5), reporting of results in stereotactic space (I6), provision of group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from the target group (I7), and acceptable reporting format (I8). No exclusion criteria appear to be violated; full text is provided and complete.

This article is a non-empirical review and methods-focused paper on tau filaments and PET tracer development. It does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, nor does it report VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET group neuroimaging data. No participant sample, group-level between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space, or whole-brain voxelwise results are provided. Therefore it fails to meet the review’s inclusion criteria and matches the exclusion criterion for non-empirical papers without original neuroimaging data.

The full text reports a VBM whole-brain study that includes a clinically diagnosed bv-FTD group (n=15). VBM (an accepted imaging modality) was used and whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results are reported with corrected thresholds and anatomical clusters (figures and table of results with MNI coordinates referenced). Sample sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD n=15; controls n=15). The paper provides whole-brain voxelwise results clearly described in text, figures and tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, review/meta-analysis, non-empirical methods, exclusive use of other modalities, or comorbid psychiatric/ substance/other disqualifying sample characteristics) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This article is a narrative/position paper reviewing FDG-PET as a potential biomarker for frontotemporal dementia and proposing future validation studies. It does not present original empirical data, participant samples, or between-group voxelwise results in a stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). It lacks methods, subject numbers, and coordinate-based whole-brain results required by the inclusion criteria. Therefore it meets the exclusion criterion for non-empirical papers (E5).

This is an empirical study of bvFTD including FDG‑PET and ASL‑MRI with voxelwise analyses and adequate sample sizes; however, the provided full text does not report any between‑group contrast results as coordinates in a standardized stereotactic space (e.g., MNI or Talairach). Inclusion criterion I6 requires at least one between‑group contrast reported in a defined stochastic space. Although whole‑brain voxelwise maps and figures are described, no coordinate tables or explicit stereotactic coordinates are present in the provided text, so I6 is not satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply based on the provided content.

This study is a single-case report of a bvFTD patient (N=1) compared to 12 healthy controls using a tau PET ligand ([F]AV-1451). It does not use one of the eligible imaging modalities (VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET) and instead uses tau-PET. Analyses were performed on a parcellated ROI basis (83 atlas regions) with region-wise t-scores and cluster/ROI-based comparisons; the paper does not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Additionally, the patient group size (N=1) is below typical thresholds for inclusion of patient samples. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. Imaging modality: FDG-PET was used with SPM-99 voxelwise analysis (I3). Sample: 25 clinically diagnosed FTD patients (diagnosed by revised Lund-Manchester criteria, with primary progressive aphasia excluded) and 15 controls — sample sizes exceed the minimum of 6 (I5). Although the paper does not explicitly use the term “bvFTD,” the FTD group was defined by clinical features characteristic of the behavioral variant and PPA cases were excluded, consistent with inclusion of bvFTD patients (I4). The paper reports voxelwise between-group contrasts with cluster maxima given in Talairach space (x/y/z coordinates) and whole-brain SPM results for the FTD vs controls comparison (I6, I7). Coordinates and results are reported in text/tables/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are violated.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria: the imaging modality is tau PET ([F]AV-1451), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3); the patient sample contains a single bvFTD case (n=1), below the required minimum of 6 (fails I5); analyses are atlas-based/region-of-interest parcellation rather than whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotactic space and no coordinate-based voxelwise contrasts are reported (fails I6 and I7). These features mean the study effectively reports ROI-only analyses, meeting exclusion criterion E3. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This article is a narrative review of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), not an empirical neuroimaging study of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). It does not include original data on bvFTD patients, nor does it report VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET whole‑brain voxelwise results with stereotactic coordinates. The paper is non-empirical and synthesizes prior literature (review/meta-review), so it meets exclusion criteria for being a review/non-empirical paper. Therefore it does not satisfy any required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis.

The study uses structural T1-weighted volumetric segmentation of amygdala subnuclei (FreeSurfer/GIF), not VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). Results are ROI-based volumetric measures and do not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts in MNI/Talairach space or coordinate tables (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it matches exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses, no whole-brain results). The full text appears complete.

This study reports PET imaging (including FDG‑PET) in PPND/FTDP‑17 patients (so I3 met). However, it does not include clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) participants explicitly (I4 not met), has very small sample sizes (3 patients for FD/RAC, 2 for FDG — I5 not met), and does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or provide coordinate tables (I6 and I7 not met). The PET analyses are ROI-based regional/metabolic values rather than whole-brain voxelwise results, so exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only, no whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded.

This study used a linear structural MRI measure (Bifrontal Index) on axial T1 images rather than VBM, FDG-PET, or fMRI. It does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Therefore it fails the key inclusion criteria requiring imaging modality (I3) and whole-brain voxelwise results/coordinates (I6/I7). As it only provides linear/region-specific measures and no voxelwise whole-brain results, it meets exclusion criterion E3.

Although this study used FDG-PET (I3) and included clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients (I4), it is a case series of three subjects (n=3) and thus does not meet the minimum sample size requirement (I5). The paper reports individual imaging findings and descriptive neuropathology but does not present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) required for meta-analysis (I6, I7). Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria for this review. The provided full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and sample sizes exceed 6 (I5), it does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET). The imaging performed is amyloid PiB‑PET (amyloid PET) with ROI-based SUVR analyses and histopathology; no whole-brain voxelwise analyses, MNI/Talairach coordinates, or voxelwise group-level results are reported. Thus it fails I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only/no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

Provided full text is incomplete (only title/metadata/abstract-level info). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is not present, so I cannot verify any inclusion criteria. Therefore I exclude this record due to incomplete full text. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality not specified in provided text), I4 (bvFTD sample not specified), I5 (sample sizes not reported; cannot confirm ≥6), I6 (no between-group coordinate results reported), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported), I8 (no tables/figures/supplementary results available). Exclusion criteria met: none can be confidently assigned from the incomplete text (it may be a review, but this cannot be confirmed). Recommend obtaining full-text PDF for definitive screening.

This study does not meet the required imaging-modality or whole-brain voxelwise reporting criteria. It uses manual MRI volumetry (ROI-based) and SPECT perfusion, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). The analyses are primarily ROI/volumetric and diagnostic-classification metrics (AUCs) without reporting voxelwise, whole-brain group-level contrasts or stereotactic coordinates (fails I6 and I7). It also does not explicitly state inclusion of behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) as a defined subgroup (I4 not clearly met). The sample size is adequate (FTD n=38), and the full text appears complete. Primary applicable exclusion: E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results).

This study reports whole-brain, voxelwise FDG-PET analyses using SPM96 in clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients (Lund and Manchester criteria) and healthy controls. The FTD sample (n=10) meets the minimum sample-size requirement; healthy controls n=46. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain contrasts (FTD vs HS, FTD-MND vs HS, and direct group comparisons) performed in stereotaxic space via SPM normalization. Behavioral symptoms are explicitly used in the diagnostic criteria, consistent with bvFTD clinical characterization. No exclusion criteria are violated: the study is empirical, not an ROI-only analysis, and uses FDG-PET rather than excluded modalities. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections, so it is complete for screening purposes. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on bvFTD imaging results.
