The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients among the sample (5 bvFTD out of 15 FTD participants) (I4), had adequate sample sizes (15 FTD patients and 12 controls, meeting the ≥6 requirement for a patient or healthy group) (I5), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise VBM results in standard space (MNI152) with corrected statistics and supplementary materials (satisfying I6, I7, and I8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and supplementary coordinates/results are referenced. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not an ROI-only study, not a review, not an excluded modality).

The study includes an FTD group (n=87), which likely includes bvFTD cases, used VBM/TBM imaging, and meets the sample size criterion. However, the paper does not present any between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in a standard stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach) or coordinate tables/figures that can be identified in the provided full text. The VBM/TBM features were used to derive summary indices/patterns for classification and details are referred to an Appendix, but no explicit whole-brain, voxelwise results or coordinates for the bvFTD/FTD group are reported in the main text. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (reporting between-group contrasts in defined stereotactic space and providing whole-brain voxelwise group-level results) are not satisfied, so the study is excluded.

This study is an empirical CSF biomarker investigation (amyloid, tau, NFL, YKL-40, etc.) and does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=45) and adequate sample sizes, but it does not use any neuroimaging modalities specified in the inclusion criteria (VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET), nor does it report whole‑brain voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates. Therefore it fails key inclusion criterion I3 (imaging modality) and the requirements for whole‑brain between‑group imaging results (I6/I7). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical VBM study of frontotemporal lobar degeneration that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (19 bvFTD across subgroups) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts in standard stereotactic space. Imaging modality: VBM (SPM8/DARTEL) with voxelwise statistical parametric maps and coordinate tables in MNI space; small-volume and whole-brain results are reported. Sample size meets the minimum (37 patients total; ≥6 bvFTD). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results clearly identified for the target patient sample and contains full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, non-empirical, disallowed modality) are violated.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It uses FDG-PET imaging (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients (Neary criteria), i.e., behavioral-variant FTD within the FTLD cohort (FTD subgroup reported) (I4). Sample sizes meet the threshold (44 FTLD total; FTD subgroup n=26; group-level subgroups n=8 and n=36) (I5). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM2 group comparisons with results converted to Talairach coordinates and provides cluster peak coordinates (I6, I7). Whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures (I8). Full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion; fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria appear to be violated.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes an FTD subgroup of 14 patients (I5), it does not meet key inclusion requirements for this meta-analysis. The paper does not specify that the FTD cases are the behavioral variant (bvFTD) and does not present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or report coordinates from between-group contrasts. Instead, results are based on visual reads and descriptive regional findings. Therefore I6 and I7 are not satisfied, and the study provides only non-voxelwise/qualitative PET findings (qualifies for exclusion under E3). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This article is a narrative review/overview of clinical and imaging diagnostics of neurodegenerative dementias, not an empirical study of bvFTD. It does not report original data from clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients, does not present voxelwise VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET group-level whole-brain results or MNI/Talairach coordinates, nor does it report sample sizes meeting inclusion criteria. Therefore it fails multiple required inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criteria for non-empirical review articles.

This article is a narrative review of PET tau radiotracers in parkinsonian tauopathies, not an empirical study of bvFTD. It does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, nor does it use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET as primary imaging modalities (focus is on tau-PET). No original participant data, no group-level between-group voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach space, and the Data Availability statement confirms no datasets were generated. Therefore it fails all required inclusion criteria and meets the exclusion criterion for non-empirical review articles.

This is a genetic case-control study of tau haplotypes in clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FTD). It does not use any of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), does not report whole-brain, voxelwise neuroimaging results or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach), and does not specifically study the behavioral variant of FTD (bvFTD). Although sample size meets the minimum (100 patients), multiple required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I6, I7) are not satisfied. The full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded from this imaging-focused bvFTD meta-analysis.

This is an empirical longitudinal MRI volumetric study of C9ORF72-associated FTD but it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). The imaging analyses are based on volumetric segmentation, FreeSurfer regional volumes and nonlinear fluid registration (ROI/volume-based), with no voxelwise whole-brain results reported in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinates (fails I6 and I7). Therefore the study effectively reports ROI/region-based results only and lacks the required whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (meets exclusion criterion E3). The clinical sample does include behaviourally diagnosed FTD patients and meets sample-size requirements, but the imaging modality and absence of stereotactic voxelwise coordinates prevent inclusion.

The study uses deep learning on structural T1-weighted MRI (raw 3D MRI) and computes gradient-based contribution maps, not VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET. Therefore it does not meet imaging-modality inclusion criterion (I3). Also, the FTD sample is labeled generically as FTD without specifying clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD), so it does not satisfy I4. The paper does meet sample-size (I5) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contribution maps transformed to MNI space with between-group t-tests (I6, I7, I8), but failure to meet I3 and I4 means it must be excluded.

This article is a narrative review (non-empirical) summarizing recent imaging studies across neurodegenerative disorders. It does not present original participant-level data, methods, or results (no imaging analyses, no voxelwise group contrasts, no coordinate tables) and therefore does not meet inclusion requirements for empirical VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET studies of bvFTD. It discusses FTLD/FTD broadly but does not report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients with sample sizes or stereotactic coordinates. Excluded under E2 (review) and E5 (non-empirical paper without original data).

This is a clinicopathological diagnostic accuracy study, not a voxelwise neuroimaging group analysis using VBM, fMRI (resting/task), or FDG-PET as required. Although structural MRI and some functional imaging (PET/SPECT) were used clinically, the paper does not present whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results with coordinates in a standard space, nor does it specifically report VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET analyses. The sample is mixed FTLD syndromes (behavioral, PPA, semantic, PSP, CBS) and not focused on clinically diagnosed bvFTD with whole-brain imaging results. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I6–I8. Full text appears complete.

Although the study used FDG‑PET and reports whole‑brain, voxelwise results in MNI space (satisfying imaging and reporting criteria), it does not meet the review’s requirements for bvFTD sampling. The cohort includes a small FTD subgroup (FTD = 3), which is below the required minimum of 6 participants for the patient group of interest (violating inclusion criterion I5). Additionally, the sample is heterogeneous (Alzheimer’s disease, FTLD subtypes, other dementias, MCI, subjective cognitive impairment), i.e. it includes other dementia forms rather than a clean bvFTD sample, triggering exclusion criterion E4. Therefore, despite appropriate modality (FDG‑PET) and whole‑brain reporting, the study is excluded because it lacks sufficient bvFTD participant numbers and contains mixed dementia subtypes that confound attribution to bvFTD.

This is a single-case clinical report of childhood-onset cerebellar ataxia due to a homozygous SQSTM1 mutation, not a study of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). It does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET)—only routine MRI is mentioned—has a sample size of one, and reports no whole-brain voxelwise analyses or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Therefore it fails to meet key inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). Full text appears complete.

Although the study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (bvFTD n=8) with adequate group sizes, the VBM group-level results are reported for a combined FTD group (bvFTD + semantic dementia) rather than for the behavioral-variant FTD subgroup specifically. Inclusion criterion I7 requires at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result clearly identified as coming from the target sample group (bvFTD). Because the paper collapsed FTD subtypes and does not present separate whole-brain voxelwise contrasts or coordinates exclusively for bvFTD, it does not meet I7 and therefore cannot be included in a bvFTD-specific VBM meta-analysis.

Study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts with coordinates transformed to Talairach space. The sample includes a SOC/EXEC subgroup described as nonaphasic patients with disorders of social comportment and executive processing, which corresponds to behavioral-variant FTD; this subgroup has N=32 (overall N=88), meeting the minimum sample-size requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain atrophy results for patient subgroups (including SOC/EXEC) and provides coordinate information and tables/figures. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, imaging modality acceptable, no disallowed comorbidities reported). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion under I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This is a structural MRI study using volumetry and shape (surface displacement and Laplacian invariants) of hippocampus and lateral ventricles, not VBM, task/resting‑state fMRI, or FDG‑PET (fails inclusion I3). Although it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and adequate sample sizes (I5), it does not report whole‑brain, voxelwise group results in stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) and instead reports ROI/subcortical surface analyses (thus no qualifying whole‑brain coordinate results; fails I6 and I7). Therefore it meets the exclusion criterion for studies reporting only ROI/subcortical analyses with no whole‑brain results (E3). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports two single case reports (N=2) with GRN mutations, not a group study of bvFTD. Although single-subject VBM and FDG-PET/PiB-PET were used (I3 satisfied), the sample does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (patients presented with AD-like or logopenic aphasia phenotypes), the participant count is far below the required minimum (I5), and no group-level whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts from a bvFTD sample are reported (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it does not meet the review inclusion criteria.

This study does not meet the imaging and whole-brain voxelwise reporting inclusion criteria. It used EEG and Freesurfer-based volumetric/cortical reconstruction (surface-based cortical thickness/region volumes), not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET (violating I3). The paper does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in standard space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables/figures (violating I6 and I7). Although the sample of FTD patients (n=20) meets the sample-size criterion (I5), the imaging modality/methods are excluded per E6 (cortical thickness/volumetry methods only) and no voxelwise whole-brain results are provided. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (FSL VBM) linking grey-matter intensity to behaviour and group differences, satisfying the imaging-modality criterion. The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD participants (11 bvFTD out of 34 FTD patients) and control/AD groups; subgroup sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=11, controls n=15, AD n=10). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain contrasts and correlations in MNI space with coordinates provided (tables/figures/supplementary), meeting the reporting and whole-brain evidence criteria. No exclusion criteria are violated. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality; includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=16) and healthy controls; sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=16, controls n=18); reports between-group voxelwise contrasts and correlations using VBM in MNI space (template from IXI database and SPM8/VBM8), with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results presented (including coordinate-based results and figures) rather than ROI-only analyses. The manuscript contains full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is empirical (not a review). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review.

Full text reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses with whole-brain, voxelwise results and coordinates (MNI space) and figures/tables. The sample includes a frontotemporal dementia (FTD) subgroup (n=15) within the FTLD cohort, consistent with clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD per referenced diagnostic criteria. Sample sizes meet the minimum (FTD n=15; overall groups n=25). The paper reports group-level whole-brain VBM contrasts and correlations (family-wise error corrected results within ROIs and whole-brain analyses), satisfying reporting of between-group contrasts in standardized space. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply.

This full text meets all required inclusion criteria for a VBM study of bvFTD. The study employed whole-brain Voxel-Based Morphometry normalized to MNI space and reports voxelwise, group-level between-group contrasts (FWE-corrected and exploratory thresholds) with results overlaid on the MNI template. The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTSD (bvFTSD) patients (16 bvFTSD within the FTSD group) and group sizes exceed the minimum (FTSD n=20; controls n=39). Whole-brain voxelwise results from the target patient groups are clearly reported in the text/figures. No exclusion criteria are met and the provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a narrative review article summarizing diagnostic techniques for FTD rather than an original empirical study. It contains no original participant data, no VBM/resting-state/task fMRI or FDG‑PET group-level analyses with reported whole-brain voxelwise coordinates, and no sample of bvFTD participants with results in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails all required inclusion criteria (I3–I7) and meets the exclusion criterion for non-empirical papers. Full text appears complete.

The study uses FDG-PET with voxelwise SPM analyses and reports MNI coordinates (meets I3, I6, I7, I8), includes 29 clinically diagnosed FTD patients (excluded PPA and semantic dementia — consistent with bvFTD; meets I4) and sample size exceeds minimum (meets I5). However, 3 of 29 patients had mild associated signs of motor neuron disease (a concurrent neurological condition). This violates exclusion criterion E4 (sample must have no concurrent neurological symptoms). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore, despite satisfying imaging and reporting requirements, the presence of concurrent neurological symptoms requires exclusion under the review's strict criteria.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level results with peak coordinates. The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) patients (n=20) and adequate sample sizes. The paper reports voxel-wise analyses and coordinates (MNI/Talairach-style) and whole-brain FWE-corrected results. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria are violated. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); subjects were prospectively recruited meeting research/international criteria for behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) (I4); group sizes are sufficient (7 and 10 FTLD patients, and matched controls) satisfying the >=6 requirement (I5); images were normalized to MNI space and SPM2 was used for voxelwise comparisons, indicating results are reported in a defined stereotactic space (I6); the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts between FTLD subgroups and controls (I7) with results presented as voxelwise analyses (I8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a narrative review (‘Five new things’) summarizing findings across disorders; it does not present original empirical data from a bvFTD sample, nor does it report VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET whole-brain, voxelwise results or coordinates for clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients. It therefore fails all inclusion criteria (no bvFTD patient sample or neuroimaging results) and meets exclusion E5 (non-empirical paper).

This full text meets the review inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (bvFTD N=4) within the sample (I4), has at least 6 participants in a group (healthy controls N=10) satisfying the sample-size threshold (I5), reports whole-brain voxel-to-voxel group analyses with images normalized to MNI space (preprocessing mentions MNI normalization) and presents between-group voxelwise results (I6, I7). Whole-brain results are described in the manuscript and referenced tables/figures (I8). Note: the bvFTD subgroup is small (n=4), which may limit subgroup-specific inferences; this reduces confidence slightly but does not violate inclusion criteria.

The study uses VBM and reports whole-brain, voxelwise results in MNI space with adequate sample sizes (VBM subset n=22; subgroups n>=11), satisfying imaging (I3), sample size (I5), coordinate reporting (I6), whole-brain evidence (I7), and acceptable reporting locations (I8). However, it does not include participants explicitly diagnosed as behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD). The patient groups are labeled PNFA, SemD, and SOC/EXEC (social/executive disorder). Although SOC/EXEC resembles bvFTD clinically, the paper does not state a clinical diagnosis of bvFTD, so it fails inclusion criterion I4 (presence of clinically diagnosed bvFTD). Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This article is a narrative review describing rare genetically defined causes of dementia and does not report original empirical imaging data. It does not include a sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, nor does it present VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results or coordinate-based between-group contrasts. Therefore it fails multiple required inclusion criteria and meets the exclusion criterion for non-empirical papers (reviews) without original data.

This grant report summarizes multiple projects and datasets but does not present the specific whole-brain, voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) between-group coordinate results required by the review. Although FDG-PET and structural MRI are used and the overall project aims include differentiating bvFTD from AD/NC, the full text does not provide: (1) explicit reporting of clinically diagnosed bvFTD group sizes or details of bvFTD-specific group-level voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic space, and (2) any tables/coordinates or clear whole-brain voxelwise results attributable to a bvFTD group. Much of the reported work is hippocampal surface or ROI-based analyses, machine-learning classification summaries, and descriptions of FDG-PET patch features, which do not satisfy the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise coordinate reporting. Therefore the study does not meet the critical inclusion criteria (I6/I7) and is excluded under E3 (reports only ROI/non-whole-brain results).

This is a narrative clinical review (overview) of neuroimaging in dementia, not an empirical neuroimaging study. It contains no original participant sample, no VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET analyses reporting group-level voxelwise contrasts, and provides no coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it does not meet the review’s inclusion criteria. Exclusion applied: E5 (non-empirical paper without original data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no empirical VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET data/analyses), I4 (no clinically diagnosed bvFTD participant sample), I5 (no participant counts ≥6 reported for patient/healthy groups), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), I8 (no qualifying whole-brain results in tables/figures/supplement). Full text appears complete (narrative review), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Full text unavailable (content = 'nan'), so core methods/results cannot be verified. Therefore I cannot confirm any inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable: I3 (imaging modality VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET unknown), I4 (bvFTD clinically diagnosed sample unknown), I5 (sample size >=6 unknown), I6 (reported between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach unknown), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level result unknown), I8 (reporting of coordinates in tables/figures/supplementary unknown). No exclusion criteria are identified as met based on available information (E2,E3,E4,E5,E6 not confirmed). This empirical study directly addresses bvFTD using resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). It enrolled 12 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (and 30 controls), satisfying the minimum sample-size requirement. Analyses were conducted in standard space (MNI normalization) with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (VBM and ICA-derived component maps and spectral/FNC analyses) reported and FDR-corrected; supplementary materials are referenced for maps/tables. The paper contains full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, includes no prohibited modalities only, and does not indicate comorbid samples). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and the study should be included.
